full_judgment:
Md Shohrowardi J: The Rule Nisi has been issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 1-8-2018 passed by respondent No. 1, the Election Appellate Tribunal, Jamalpur in Election Appeal No. 3 of 2018 affirming those dated 28-5-2016 passed by respondent No. 2, the Election Tribunal, Jamalpur in Election Tribunal Case No. 27 of 016 violating the provisions of Rule 62 of the স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) নির্বাচন বিধিমালা, ২০১০ shall not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 2. Short facts relevant for disposal of the Rule are that the election of No. 3 Parramrampur Union Parishad, Dewangonj, Jamalpur was held on 28-5-2016 and total 7 (seven) candidates contested in the election for the post of Chairman. Out of total 25860 (twenty-five thousand eight hundred and sixty) votes, 21,900 (twenty-one thousand and nine hundred) votes were cast in 12(twelve) centers, and after counting ballot papers, the Presiding Officers found total 20,990 (twenty thousand nine hundred and ninety) valid votes and 910 (nine hundred and ten) invalid votes. After counting ballot papers, the Returning Officer declared the election result on the same day. The petitioner got 4139 (four thousand one hundred and thirty-nine) votes and the respondent No. 3 got 3939 (three thousand nine hundred and thirty-nine) votes and other 5(five) candidates also got 12,911 (twelve thousand nine hundred and eleven) votes. After counting ballot papers, tile Returning Officer declared the petitioner as elected Chairman of No. 3 Parramrampur Union Parishad and election result was published on 21- 6-2016 in Bangladesh Gazette. Thereafter, the petitioner has taken oath on 16-7-2016. 3. After declaration of the election result, the petitioner filed an application on 2-6-2016 to the Election Commission making some allegations against the Presiding Officers and the returned candidate regarding corrupt practice adopted during election of No. 3 Parramrampur Union Parishad, Dewangonj, Jamalpur and prayed for cancellation of the election result of the said Union Parishad declared by the Returning Officer or to recount ballot papers. The contents of the application dated 2-6-2016 are quoted below: “বরাবর, মাননীয় প্রধান নির্বাচন কমিশনার নির্বাচন কমিশন সচিবালয় শেরেবাংলা নগর, ঢাকা। বিষয়ঃ জামালপর জেলাধীন দেওয়ানগঙ্জ উপজেলাস্থ ৩নং পাররামরামপুর ইউনিয়নের ২৮-৫-২০১৬ তারিখের অনুষ্ঠিত ৫ম ধাপের নির্বাচনে ব্যাপক অনিয়ম এবং প্রকাশ্য কারচুপিসহ গণনায় ভুল করায় নির্বাচন স্থগিত রাখিয়া পুনরায় নির্বাচনের জন্য আবেদন। জনাব, যথাবিহীত সম্মান প্রদর্শন পূর্বক বিনীত নিবেদন এই যে, আমি মোঃ সোহেল রানা, পিতা-মৃতঃ আবুল হোসেন মিয়া, সাং ডিশ্বীরচর, থানা-দেওয়ানগঞ্জ, জেলা- জামালপুর, দেওয়ানগঞ্জ উপজেলাধীন ৩নং পাররামরামপুর ইউনিয়নবাসীর পক্ষ থেকে এই মর্মে জানাইতেছি যে, গত ২৮-৫-২০১৬ ইং তারিখে জামালপুর জেলাধীন দেওয়ানগঞ্জ উপজেলাধীন ৩নং পাররামরামপুর ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ নির্বাচনে আমি এলাকার জনগণের মনোনীত স্বতন্ত্র খার্থী হিসাবে আনারস প্রতীক নিয়া নির্বাচনে অংশগ্রহণ করি । আমি নির্বাচন কমিশনের সকল প্রকার বিধি মানিয়া নির্বাচনের প্রস্তুতি নিতে থাকি। প্রথম থেকেই কিছু অসাধু নির্বাচনী কর্মকর্তার যোগসাজসে আমাকে হয়রানী করিতে থাকে । এরই অংশ হিসাবে প্রিজাইডিং অফিসারের সহিত যোগসাজস করিয়া সরকার দলীয় চেয়ারম্যান প্রার্থী মোঃ ফজলে রাবী জুয়েল এবং তাহার সন্ত্রাসী দলবল নিয়া বলরামেরচর সরকারী প্রাথমিক বিদ্যালয়ের কেন্দ্রে অস্ত্রশস্ত্রসহ প্রবেশ করিয়া জোর পূর্বক ভোটের বাক্স তুলিয়া নিয়া আমার এজেন্টদের মারধর করে কেন্দ্র থেকে বাহির করে দেয়। ইহা ছাড়া ভিটাকান্দি পোড়া ভোট কেন্দ্রে সরকার দলীয় সমর্থকরা প্রবেশ করিয়া সাদা ব্যালট পেপারে শুধুমাত্র চেয়ারম্যানের ভোট মারিয়া জোর পূর্বক ভোট বাক্সে ঢুকাইয়া রাখে । ইউনিয়নের বিভিন্ন কেন্দ্রে ব্যাপক অনিয়ম কায়েম করে। সুষ্ঠ বিচারের জন্য আমি আমার সমর্থকদের নিয়া আলোচনা করে সন্ধ্যার পর এত কারচুপির পরও আমি বিভিন্ন কেন্দ্রে ভোট গণনা করিলে বিপুল ভোটে আগাইয়া থাকি । এমতাবস্থায় সরকার দলীয় প্রার্থী নির্বাচন কমিশনের অসাধু কর্মকর্তী কর্মচারী এবং প্রশাসনের লোকজনদেরকে অবৈধ পন্থায় লাভবান করিয়া আমার প্রাপ্ত ভোট ৩৯৩৯ এবং নিকটতম প্রতিদন্দ্বীর ভোট ৪১৩৯ দেখাইয়া সম্পূর্ণরূপে মিথ্যা, বানোয়াট এবং ভিক্তিহীনভাবে সরকার দলীয় সমর্থককে জয়ী ঘোষণা করিয়াছে । এতদসংগে কাগজপত্র তুলিয়া বেসরকারী ভাবে ফলাফল প্রকাশের মধ্যেও ব্যাপক ভুল ভ্রান্তি ও কারচুপি পরিলক্ষিত হইতেছে (যাহা আমি শুনানীতে উপস্থাপন করিতে সক্ষম)। ইহা ছাড়া বিভিন্ন কেন্দ্রে ভোট গণনায় ব্যাপক অনিয়ম কাগজে কলমে জলন্ত প্রমাণ আছে। এমতাবস্থায় মাননীয় প্রধান নির্বাচন কমিশনার সরাসরি হস্তক্ষেপ করিয়া আমার প্রদত্ত তথ্যাদি নিরপেক্ষভাবে যাচাই পূর্বক বর্ণিত আমাদের ইউপি নির্বাচনের ফলাফল স্থগিত রাখিয়া পুনঃ নির্বাচনের আদেশ প্রদান করিলে এলাকার জনগণ বিপুল উদ্দীপনায় পুনরায় নির্বাচনে অংশগ্রহণ করিলে আমি বিজয়ী হব। এমতাবস্থায় এলাকার শান্তি-শৃঙ্খলা এবং জনমনে শান্তির জন্য পুনঃ নির্বাচন কিংবা পুনরায় ভোট গণনা করা একান্ত প্রয়োজন । অতএব, প্রার্থনা এই যে, মহোদয় দয়াবান হইয়া জামালপুর জেলাধীন দেওয়ানগঞ্জ উপজেলার ৩নং পাররামরামপুর ইউপিতে পুনরায় সুষ্ঠ নির্বাচন কিংবা সুষ্ঠভাবে ভোট গণনার আদেশ দান করিয়া এলাকায় সাধারণ জনগণের আশার প্রতিফলন ঘটাইতে মর্জি হয়। বিনীত ৩নং পাররামরামপুর ইউনিয়নের জনগণের পক্ষে (মোঃ সোহেল রানা) ইউপি চেয়ারম্যান প্রার্থী সাং- ডিগ্রীরচর, ইউপি ৩নং পাররামরামপুর, থানা- দেওয়ানগঞ্জ, জেলা- জামালপুর ।” তারিখঃ ২-৬-২০১৬” 4. After publication of the Gazette Notification on 21-6-2016, the respondent No. 3 filed Election Tribunal Case No. 27 of 2016 in the Election Tribunal, Jamalpur praying for recounting ballot papers of No. 3 Parramrampur Union Parishad, Upazila-Dewangonj, District-Jamalpur or re-election. 5. During trial of the election petition, the election-petitioner-respondent No. 3 examined 4 PWs. PW No. 1 is the election-petitioner, PW No. 2 Md Azizur Rahman is a member candidate of No. 15 Bonorampur Govt. অবস্থায় গ্রহণপূর্বক সংরক্ষণ করা হয় এবং আমিসহ দেওয়ানগঞ্জ উপজেলার অন্যান্য সকল রির্টানিং অফিসার উপজেলা পরিষদ সভাকক্ষে নির্বাচনে দায়িত্বরত ম্যাজিস্ট্রেটসহ অন্যান্য কর্মকর্তার উপস্থিতিতে ভোট কেন্দ্রের নির্বাচন অফিসারের কার্যালয়, দেওয়ানগঞ্জ সংরক্ষণ করেন । নিম্ন স্বাক্ষরকারী ১-৮-২০১৭ তারিখ আপনার দপ্তরের নথি তলবপত্র আদেশ স্বারক নং ১৯৮/এস/১মসিঃসঃজঃজাঃ/১৭ তারিখ- ১-৮-২০১৭ মোতাবেক একটি নোটিশ গ্রহণ করি এবং বিষয়টি নিয়ে উপজেলা নির্বাহী অফিসার উপজেলা নির্বাচন অফিসারের কার্যালয়ের সংরক্ষিত কক্ষের তালা খোলার পরামর্শ প্রদান করেন। অতঃপর উপজেলা নির্বাচন অফিসার বিভাগীয় কাজে দেওয়ানগঞ্জ উপজেলার বাহিরে থাকায় তার সাথে মোবাইলে বিষয়টি নিয়ে যোগাযোগ করা হয় এবং উপজেলা নির্বাহী অফিসার, দেওয়ানগঞ্জকে ৩-৮-২০১৭ তারিখ পাররামরামপুর ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ নির্বাচন/২০১৬ এর ভোট কেন্দ্রের ব্যালট পেপারস অন্যান্য নির্বাচনী সামণ্রী সরবরাহ করার অনুর��ধ জানিয়ে ২-৮-২০১৭ তারিখ উপজেলা নির্বাচন অফিসারকে একটি পত্র প্রেরণ করা হয় এবং ২-৮-২০১৭ তারিখ উপজেলা নির্বাচন অফিসার, উপজেলা নির্বাহী অফিসার মহোদয়ের উপস্থিতিতে সংরক্ষিত কক্ষের তালা খোলেন। আমি উপজেলা নির্বাহী অফিসার মহোদয়ের, পরামর্শে সংরক্ষিত কক্ষের ভিতরে রক্ষিত নির্বাচনীর সামগ্রীর ২(দুই) টি ছবি তুলি। এখানে উল্লেখ্য যে, উপজেলা নির্বাচন অফিস দেওয়ানগঞ্জ একটি কক্ষেই উপজেলার সকল ইউনিয়নের সকল ভোট কেন্দ্রের নির্বাচনী সামগ্রী সংরক্ষণ করেন। কিন্তু তালা খোলা অবস্থায় কক্ষের ভেতরে রক্ষিত পাররামরামপুরসহ অন্যান্য ইউনিয়নের নির্বাচনী সামগ্রীর বস্তা সমূহের মধ্যে অনেক বস্তাই ছেড়া অবস্থায় দেখা যায় (ছবি সংযুক্ত দুই কপি)। ৩-৮-২০১৭ ইং তারিখ উপজেলা নির্বাচন অফিসার দেওয়ানগঞ্জকে সকাল ৮-০০টার সময় উপজেলা নির্বাচন অফিসারের কার্যালয় দেওয়ানগঞ্জ হতে পাররামরামপুর ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ নির্বাচন/২০১৬ এর ১২টি ভোট কেন্দ্রের ব্যালট পেপারসহ অন্যান্য নির্বাচনী সামগ্রী সরবরাহ করার অনুরোধের প্রেক্ষিতে উপজেলা নির্বাচন অফিসার (স্বারক নং ২৩৪ তারিখ ৩-৮-২০১৭) দেওয়ানগঞ্জ থানা হতে প্রেরণকৃত পুলিশ ফোর্সের উপস্থিতিতে উক্ত ইউনিয়নের ১২টি কেন্দ্রের নির্বাচনী মালামাল আমার নিকট সীলগালাকৃত (তিনটি পুরাতন বস্তা ও নয়টি নতুন বস্তা) সরবরাহ করেন। অতঃপর উপজেলা নির্বাহী অফিসার মহোদয়ের উপস্থিতিতে পাররামরামপুর ইউনিয়নের উক্ত ১২টি কেন্দ্রের সকল নির্বাচনী সামঘ্রী ৩-৮-২০১৭ ইং তারিখেই উপজেলা নির্বাচন অফিসারের কার্যালয় দেওয়ানগঞ্জ হতে পুলিশ ফোর্সের সহায়তায় আপনার দপ্তরে প্রেরণ করা হয়। যেহেতু বস্তা সমূহের অধিকাংশই ছেড়া ছিল বিধায় উক্ত বস্তাসহ গ্যানিব্যাগ সিলগালা না থাকা নিন্ন স্বাক্ষরকারীর সম্পূর্ণ অগম্য। এমতাবস্থায় উপরোক্ত বিবৃতি ও হেতুর প্রতি সদয় বিবেচনা পূর্বক ব্যাখ্যা After concluding trial, the Election Tribunal by its judgment and order dated 8-3-2018 declared the respondent No. 3 as elected Chairman: of No. 3 Parramrampur Union Parishad, Upazila-Dewangonj, District-Jamalpur. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 8-3-018 passed by the Election Tribunal, Jamalpur in Election Tribunal Case No. 27 of 2016, the writ-petitioner filed Election Appeal No. 3 of 2018 before the Election Appellate Tribunal, Jamalpur. After hearing the parties, the Election Appellate Tribunal, Jamalpur by judgment and order dated 1-8-2018 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the said judgment and order passed by the Election Tribunal, Jamalpur, against which the petitioner moved this Court under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the instant Rule Nisi. 10. Mr Probir Neogi the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the writ-petitioner submits that the Election Appellate Tribunal is constituted under section 23 of স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ)নির্বাচন বিধিমালা, ২০০৯ by a Judicial Officer and an Officer of the Executive Department and as per provision of section 23(6) of the said Ain, decision of the Appellate Tribunal is final. Therefore, the instant writ petition is maintainable in law as no other alternative remedy is available under section 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure against the judgment and order passed by the Election Tribunal. 11. Mr M Amin Uddin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the writ-petitioner submits that secrecy of the ballot papers is sacrosanct and before recounting ballot paper, the Election Tribunal did not arrive at a definite finding as to whether the concerned authority produced the intact ballot papers before the Tribunal. He further submits that at the time of recounting ballot papers the gunny begs was found open, unsealed and torn and on the basis of the result of recounting tempered ballot papers kept in torn gunny begs the Tribunal below declared the respondent No. 3 as Chairman. He also submits that no application has been made to the Presiding Officer for recounting ballot papers and respondent No. 3 failed to prove the factual foundation of recounting ballot papers. In support of his submission, he cited some decision reported in 1986 BLD (AD) 236, 19 BLD (AD) 156, 20 BLD (AD) 2000, 21 BLT (HCD) 66 and 15 BLD (AD) 245. 12. Mr Moudud Ahmed appearing along with learned Advocate Mr Mohammad Mizanur Rahaman Sihab on behalf of the respondent No. 3 having raised objection as to the maintainability of the writ-petition submitted that judgment and order passed by the Election Appellate Tribunal can only be called in question under section 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. He then submits that exercising the writ jurisdiction analogous to certiorari the High Court Division cannot interfere with the concurrent finding of facts arrived at by Tribunals below on proper assessment of evidence unless it is shown that serious illegality apparent on the face of the records has been committed by the Tribunals below. He further submits that at the time of election, supporters of the writ-petitioner forcibly driven out the agents of the respondent No. 3 from the election centers and illegally cast votes in favour of the writ petitioner. He also submits that no objection has been raised by the writ-petitioner at the time of recounting ballot papers and in exercising the writ jurisdiction the High Court Division should not go beyond the terms of the Rule. At the very outset it is required to adjudicate the issue of maintainability of the writ petition for which it is required to see the provision of section 23 of স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ)নির্বাচন বিধিমালা, ২০০৯ which runs as follows: “২৩।(১)এই আইনের অধীনে নির্বাচন সম্পর্কিত বিরোধ নিষ্পত্তির ক্ষেত্রে নির্বাচন কমিশন, সরকারী গেজেটে প্রজ্ঞাপন দ্বারা, একজন উপযুক্ত পদমর্যাদার বিচার বিভাগীয় কর্মকর্তার সময়ে প্রয়োজনীয় সংখ্যক নির্বাচনী ট্রাইব্যুনাল এবং একজন উপযুক্ত পদমর্যাদার বিচার বিভাগীয় কর্মকর্তা ও একজন উপযুক্ত পদমর্যাদার নির্বাহী বিভাগের কর্মকর্তার সমন্বয়ে প্রয়োজনীয় সংখ্যক নির্বাচনী আপিল ট্রাইব্যুনাল গঠন করিবে । (২) কোন সংক্ষুব্ধ ব্যক্তি নির্বাচিত চেয়ারম্যান বা সদস্য বা সদস্যগণের নাম সরকারী গেজেটে প্রকাশের পরবর্তীতে ৩০(ত্রিশ) দিনের মধ্যে নির্বাচনী ট্রাইব্যুনালে নির্বাচনী দরখাস্ত দায়ের করিতে পারিবেন। (৩) উপ-ধারা (১) অনুযায়ী গঠিত ট্রাইব্যুনাল পরিষদের নির্বাচন সংক্রান্ত যে কোন দরখাস্ত, উহা দায়ের করিবার ১৮০(একশত আশি) দিনের মধ্যে নিষ্পত্তি করিবে। (8) নির্বাচনী ট্রাইব্যুনালের রায়ের বিরুদ্ধে সংক্ষুব্ধ ব্যক্তি ৩০ (ত্রিশ) দিনের মধ্যে নির্বাচনী আপিল ট্রাইব্যুনালে আপিল দায়ের করিতে পারিবেন। (৫) উপ-ধারা (১) অনুযায়ী গঠিত নির্বাচনী আপিল ট্রাইব্যুনাল আপিল দায়ের করিবার ১২০(একশত বিশ) দিনের মধ্যে উহা নিষ্পত্তি করিবে। (৬) নির্বাচনী আপিল ট্রাইব্যুনালের রায় চূড়ান্ত বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে।” 15. On a bare reading of section 23 of স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) আইন, ২০০৯ it reveals that the Election Appellate Tribunal is consists of one competent Judicial Officer and one Officer of the Executive Department. On a careful reading of Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, it appears that the High Court Division may revise any decree or order passed by the District Judge, Additional District Judge or a decree passed by the Joint District Judge, Senior Assistant Judge or Assistant Judge from which no appeal lies. Be that as it may, the revisional application under section 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 is not maintainable before the High Court Division against the judgment and order passed by the Election Appellate Tribunal as the said Tribunal is consists of one competent Judicial Officer and one Officer of the Executive Department. As per provision of Sub-section 6 of section 23 of the said Ain, the decision of the Election Appellate Tribunal is final and no other alternative remedy is available against the judgment and order passed by the Election Appellate Tribunal. Therefore, we are of the opinion that the instant writ petition is maintainable in law. 16. On perusal of the judgment and order passed by the Election Tribunal, it appears that by order of the Tribunal, the Sheristadar of the Tribunal below with the help of other staffs of the Tribunal recounted ballot papers in presence of the writ-petitioner and the respondent No. 3. After recounting ballot papers, the Sheristadar of the Tribunal submitted a report on 9-8-2017 to the Election Tribunal, Jamalpur stating that out of 12 centers, the gunny begs of 9(nine) centers is found open, unsealed and torn. 17. On perusal of the judgment and order passed by the Tribunal below, it further appears that the Election Tribunal without proper assessment of the evidence of the parties relying on the report of the Sheristadar passed the impugned judgment dated 28-5-2016 declaring the respondent No. 3 as elected Chairman of No. 3 Parramrampur Union Parishad, Upazila-Dewangonj, Jamalpur without setting aside the election result of the said Union Parishad published in Bangladesh Gazette on 21-6-2016. In the memo of appeal, the writ-petitioner has taken specific grounds regarding open, unsealed and torn gunny begs. Although the Election Appellate Tribunal is the final Court of fact but the Election Appellate Tribunal without assessment of the evidence of the parties mechanically affirmed the judgment and order passed by the Election Tribunal. Therefore, we are of the view that both the Tribunals below without assessment of the evidence passed the impugned judgment and order and failed to discharge judicial duty in accordance with law. 18. It is well settled that a writ of certiorari can be issued against an order passed by any Court or Tribunal subordinate to the High Court Division or any quasi-judicial authority on the ground that the same is quorum non-judice or mala fide or is violative of rules of natural justice or is contrary to any law or is vitiated by an error of law apparent on the face of the records. In exercise of certiorari, the High Court Division cannot act as a court of appeal to re-assess the evidence unless it is found that the decision of the Courts below or tribunal is not warranted by evidence on records. If the Election Tribunal failed to exercise its jurisdiction vested in it or exceeded the jurisdiction or acted mala fide or in bad faith, the decision of the Courts or Tribunals below can be called in question under Article 102 of the constitution. 19. In the case of Civil Service Unions vs Minister for the Civil Service reported in (1984) 3 All ER 935 at 949 Lord Diplock enunciated principles on 'judicial review' adding that: "Judicial review has I think developed to a stage today when without reiterating any analysis of the steps by which the development has come about, one can conveniently classify under three heads the grounds upon which administrative action is subject to control by judicial review. The first ground I would call "illegality," the second "irrationality" and the third "procedural impropriety." By "illegality" as a ground for judicial review, I mean that the decision-maker must understand correctly the law that regulates his decision-making power and must give effect to it. Whether he has or not is par excellence a justiciable question to be decided, in the event of dispute, by those persons, the judges, by whom the judicial power of the state is exercisable. By "irrationality" I mean what can by now be succinctly referred to as "Wednesbury unreasonableness" (Associated Provincial Picture Houses Ltd vs Wednesbury Corporation [1948] 1 KB 223). It applies to a decision which is so outrageous in its defiance of logic or of accepted moral standards that no sensible person who had applied his mind to the question to be decided could have arrived at it. Whether a decision falls within this category is a question that judges by their training and experience should be well equipped to answer, or else there would be something badly wrong with our judicial system. To justify the court's exercise of this role, resort I think is today no longer needed to Viscount Radcliffe's ingenious explanation in Edwards vs Bairstow [1956] AC 14 of irrationality as a ground for a court's reversal of a decision by ascribing it to an inferred though unidentifiable mistake of law by the decision-maker. "Irrationality" by now can stand upon its own feet as an accepted ground on which a decision may be attacked by judicial review. I have described the third head as "procedural impropriety" rather than failure to observe basic rules of natural justice or failure to act with procedural fairness towards the person who will be affected by the decision. This is because susceptibility to judicial review under this head covers also a failure by an administrative tribunal to observe procedural rules that are expressly laid down in the legislative instrument by which its jurisdiction is conferred, even where such failure does not involve any denial of natural justice. But the instant case is not concerned with the proceedings of an administrative tribunal at all." 20. In the case of Fariduddin Ahmed vs Election Tribunal and Munsif, 1st Court, Barisal reported in 1979 BSCR 455, para 8 judgment dated 20-6-1979 Ruhul Islam J has held as under: "We have already indicated above that the High Court Division has disturbed the finding of the Election Tribunal as it was sitting on appeal. In exercising the Writ Jurisdiction the High Court Division in a matter analogous to certiorari should not interfere against the decision of the Tribunal which is based on clear findings of fact supported by evidence. A special forum having been created under the special statute to adjudicate upon election disputes and the special forum is required to decide it summarily, it is not expected that the Election Tribunal should meticulously follow the procedure of trial of a suit as provided under the Code of Civil Procedure. Unless it is found that the decision of the Election Tribunal is not warranted by the evidence on record or the decision is contrary to any provisions of law, Writ Jurisdiction should not be exercised and thereby interfering in the decision of the Election Tribunals." 21. In the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Md Jalil reported in 48 DLR (AD) 10 (judgment dated 23-8-1995), his Lordship ATM Afzal CJ has formulated some guidelines to be followed by the High Court Division in interfering with the finding of fact under its extraordinary jurisdiction and has held that; "The High Court Division was not a Court of appeal required to make a determination of facts on its own. It could interfere with the findings of a tribunal of fact under it extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 102, only if it could be shown that the tribunal had acted without jurisdiction or made any finding upon no evidence or without considering any material evidence facts causing prejudice to the complaining party or that it had acted mala fide or in violation of any principle of natural justice. In the absence of these conditions the interference by the High Court Division will itself be an act of without jurisdiction." 22. In the case of Professor Muhammad Yunus vs Bangladesh, reported in VIII ADC (2011) 837 (judgment dated 15-5-2011), SK Sinha J. as his Lordship was then, emphasized 'not to substitute its own decision for that of the Court below' in exercising extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution and has held as under: "Judicial review is different from an appeal. The Court bearing an appeal will normally have the right to decide the whole case again and, if it wishes to substitute its own decision for that of the Court below. This is precisely where a judicial review differs from an appeal. The Court conducting a review is concerned to determine the lawfulness, but not the merits of the decision under review. The natural corollary to this is that though the Court could quash the impugned decision, it could not substitute its own decision for that of the concerned Authority, the original decision maker." 23. The jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102 of the constitution was again examined by our Apex Court in the case of Shahidul Haque vs Court of Settlement reported in 69 DLR (AD) 241 (judgment dated 16-8-2016) wherein his lordship SK Sinha CJ has held as under: "A writ of certiorari is maintainable only if it can be shown that the tribunal erroneously held that the property was illegally declared as abandoned property without admitting legal evidence or rejected the legal evidence or it has misconstrued the law. In other words, a writ of certiorari does not lie for an erroneous decision in respect of a matter which is within the jurisdiction of the inferior tribunal. Unless such erroneous decision relates to anything collateral, an erroneous decision upon which might affect jurisdiction and the statute does not confer upon the tribunal final jurisdiction to decide such question. A writ of certiorari is maintainable only in a case where erroneous decision within its jurisdiction. Even if there is mere error of law that will not confer any power on the High Court Division to issue a writ of certiorari except where there is an error apparent on the face of the record, that means, the error must be something more than a mere error. The High Court Division can issue writ of certiorari only if it can be shown that the judgment has been obtained by fraud, collusion or corruption or where the tribunal has acted contrary to the principles of natural justice or where there is an error apparent on the face of the record or where the tribunal's conclusion is based on no evidence whatsoever or where the decision is vitiated by malafide." 24. There is no denial of the fact that at the time of counting ballot papers, the Presiding Officers found that out of total 25,860 votes, 21,900 votes were cast in 12 (twelve) centers and the Presiding Officers found total 20,910 valid votes out of 21,900 votes and 910 (nine hundred and ten) invalid votes. On perusal of the recounting report dated 9-8-2017 submitted by the Sheristadar, it appears that at the time of recounting ballot papers, all those ballot papers were not produced before the Tribunal and the Sheristadar of the Election Tribunal only recounted ballot papers of the writ-petitioner and respondent No. 3 kept in open, unsealed and torn gunny begs of 9(nine) centers and intact gunny begs of 3(three) centers. 25. In the above facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that the recounting has not been done by the Election Tribunal and election materials which have been produced before the Election Tribunal was kept in open, unsealed and torn gunny begs violating the provision of Rule 45 of স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) নির্বাচন বিধিমালা,২০১০ and the Election Tribunal failed to discharge judicial duty properly, and mala fide shifted the responsibility of recounting ballot papers to the Sheristadar and the Appellate Tribunal without assessment of evidence and also without adjudicating the grounds taken in the appeal mechanically affirmed the judgment and order passed by the Election Tribunal. Therefore, the decision of the Tribunals below is not justified and warranted by evidence on records. 26. Since both the Tribunals below failed to assess the evidence of the parties causing prejudice to the petitioner in declaring the respondent No. 3 as Chairman of No. 3 Parramrampur Union Parishad on the basis of the result of the recounting ballot papers kept in open, unsealed and torn gunny begs violating the provision of Rule 45 of the স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) নির্বাচন বিধিমালা, ২০১০ it is required to see the evidence adduced by the parties. 27. During trial of the case, OPW Nos. 6 to 15 stated that they have deposited the intact sealed packets of result sheets and ballot papers kept in sealed gunny begs as per Rule 40 of স্থানীয় সরকার(ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) নির্বাচন বিধিমালা, ২০১০ but during cross-examination statement of those witnesses has not been denied by the respondent No. 3. During cross-examination of OPW Nos. 6, 9, 11, 13 and 14 the respondent No. 3 affirmed that the Presiding Officers have handed over intact ballot papers keeping those in sealed gunny begs to the concerned authority. But the Election Tribunal did not arrive at any finding as to whether the torn gunny begs is the post-election manipulation i.e. after handing over the election materials to the Election Officer and before handing over the election materials to the Election Tribunal although the Election Tribunal held that there was no scope to tamper with the election materials in the record room. It is found that the Presiding Officers have handed over the intact ballot papers to the staffs of the Election Officer, Dewangonj. Therefore, we are of the view that after handing over the election materials to the Election Officer, Dewangonj, Jamalpur ballot papers were tampered in the record room of the Election Office, Dewangonj along with ballot papers of other Union Parishads before producing those gunny begs to the Election Tribunal. 28. Another issue involved in the Rule as to whether the Election Tribunal is legally empowered to recount ballot papers and the Tribunals below legally declared the respondent No. 3 as elected Chairman of Parramrampur Union Parishad on the basis of the result of recounting ballot papers. 29. On a careful reading of স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) নির্বাচন বিধিমালা, ২০১০ it appears that in Rule 39(2) of স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) নির্বাচন বিধিমালা, ২০১০ provision has been made for recounting ballot papers by the Presiding Officer. Under Rule 41(5)(a) of স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) নির্বাচন বিধিমালা, ২০১০ after filing any objection by any contesting candidate or his agent against the counting of ballot papers by the Presiding Officer, the Returning Officer may recount ballot papers. Rule 41(5)(6) also empowered the Election Commission to direct Returning Officer to recount ballot papers. 30. In Rule 62 of স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) নির্বাচন বিধিমালা, ২০১১ the legislature empowered the Election Tribunal or Election Appellate Tribunal to pass an order to open the packets containing election documents for inspection maintaining secrecy of the ballot papers. No specific provision has been made for recounting ballot papers by the Tribunal. 31. Recounting ballot papers is the inherent power of the Tribunal. In an appropriate case, for proper adjudication of the dispute between the parties the Tribunal can pass an order for recounting ballot papers. A recounting will not be granted as a matter of right but only on the basis of evidence of good grounds for believing that there has been a mistake in counting. The reasons are that such order affects the secrecy of ballots which is under law is not to be likely disturbed. The secrecy of the ballot papers is sacrosanct and shall not be permitted to be violated merely for asking on vague and indefinite allegations or averment of general nature. Recounting ballot papers is the judicial function of the Tribunal to decide the election dispute which cannot be delegated to its staffs. 32. When the result of the election declared by the Election Commission is called in question, the same is subject to scrutiny of the Tribunal. If the gunny begs containing ballot papers is found tampered or torn, there is no scope to scrutiny ballot papers by the Tribunal. In the instant case, out of 12 (twelve) centers, gunny begs of 9 (nine) centers is found open, unsealed and torn but the Tribunals below did not arrive at any definite finding as to whether open, unsealed and torn gunny begs were the post-election manipulations, i.e. after dispatch of ballot papers by the Presiding Officers and before recounting ballot papers by order of the Tribunal. Therefore, there was no scope to scrutiny the intact ballot papers by the Tribunal. In the above facts and circumstance of the case, we are of the view that serious illegality apparent on the face of the records was committed by the Tribunal below in recounting ballot papers kept in open, unsealed and torn gunny begs. Since gunny begs containing ballot papers of 9(nine) polling centers is found open, unsealed and torn, Tribunal below ought to have refuged recount those ballot papers. 33. The objection raised on behalf of the writ-petitioner regarding recounting ballot papers has been decided in the case of Nurul Islam Talukder vs Munsif reported in 28 DLR 375 Para 15 judgment dated 14-6-1976 wherein Shahabuddin Ahmed J as his Lordship was then, has held as under: The Tribunal acted with material irregularity when it proceeded to examine the ballot papers ignoring the broad fact that the gunny begs containing the election papers were tampered with having a number of stitched up holes." 34. Subsequently in the case of Md Shajahan vs Md Sadeq, reported in 1986 BLD (AD) 236 Para 13 = 38 DLR (AD) 275, (Judgment dated 5-3-1986) Shahabuddin Ahmed J, as his Lordship was then, has reiterated the same view regarding recounting ballot papers and emphasized 'to maintain the special sanctity of ballot papers' and observed that; "In Election cases, it is often found that a defeated candidate brings a number of allegations including vague charges of his opponent influencing the Presiding Officer, but ultimately fails to prove, or abandon all the allegations and insist on only recounting of ballot papers. On recounting, it is found that the result has gone in his favour by some mysterious means. That is why recounting of the ballot papers by a Tribunal long after the election should not be resorted to simply mere asking by an interested party. Ballot papers have special sanctity of their own and their secrecy should not be infringed by reopening the sealed packets unless the recounting becomes indispensably necessary to determine the dispute. When recounting would become so necessary depends on circumstances in each case. In the absence of clear justifications, no recounting should be ordered or made. Some finality must attach to the counting of votes. The groundwork for recounting must be prepared: recounting should be refused if no prayer for recounting had been made to the Presiding Officer who is alone empowered to recount on the spot either on his own motion or on requests of any candidate. Recounting of ballot-papers by the Tribunal is not specifically provided in the Election Rules, but it falls within the inherent powers of the Tribunal to decide the election dispute. In the instant case when the Tribunal itself was not in a position to say whether the double marks were post-election acts or were the doings of the respective voters election of the returned candidate should not have been interfered with. It is not a case of benefit of the doubt going to a defeated candidate feeling aggrieved like the accused in a criminal case. Here, the presumption is in favour of the returned candidate whose election shall not be declared a nullity unless the Tribunal is satisfied" as laid down in rule 49 that the election has been materially affected by some illegal acts or contravention of some rules." 35. In the case of Ansaruddin Ahmed vs Senior Assistant Judge and Election Tribunal, Barguna reported in 46 DLR (AD)181, (Judgment dated 14-6-1993), MH Rahman J, as his Lordship was then, considered the issue of recounting ballot papers and held that; "As there exists a factual foundation and the Election Tribunal found that a decision on these allegations cannot be given without recounting the ballots, the High Court Division rightly discharged the Rules Nisi." 36. In the case of Muzaffar Hossain vs Md Humayun Kabir, reported in 15 BLD (AD) (1995) 245 = 48 DLR (AD) 59 (Judgment dated 13-8-1995), his lordship Mohammad Ismailuddin Sarker J has held that; "When it is found that the petitioner made no written prayer before the Presiding Officer for recounting of the ballot papers on the ground of any malpractice and he did not raise any objection before the Returning Officer alleging double seals on a large number of ballot papers or other malpractices, it is to be held that no valid ground for recounting of votes has been made out for proving that the election was materially affected due to corrupt practices or violation of Election Rules. 37. In the case of Abdul Mutalib vs Md Mostakim Ali, reported in 19 BLD (AD) 156 (1999), (Judgment dated 30-5-1996), Mohammad Abdur Rouf J has held as under; "It is now well-settled that in an appropriate case the Election Tribunal in the interest of justice may recount ballot papers for proper resolution of an election dispute. But in order to make out a case for recounting the person who challenges the counting has to prove that at the time of counting of votes by the presiding officer a contesting candidate or his election agent upon raising specific objection specifically requested the presiding officer to recount the ballot papers, provided in Rule 38(4)(b) of the Union Parishads (Election) Rules, 1983 briefly "the Rules" and that the same was improperly refused or was not done in accordance with law." 38.1n the Case of Abdul Latif Bepari vs Md Nurul Islam Howlader, reported in 20 BLD (AD) 264 (2000) = 5 BLC (AD) 152 (judgment dated 4-7-2000), Bimalendu Bikash Roy Chowdhury J has held that; "Recounting is not to be granted as a matter of course. It is only to be allowed when the tribunal is satisfied on the basis of the evidence before it that recounting is indispensably necessary for complete and effectual justice." 39. In the case of SM Fazlul Haque Manik vs Md Habibullah Bahai; reported in 61 DLR (AD) 66, (Judgment dated 3-10-2007), Md Abdul Matin J has held that; "It appears that the High Court Division has correctly held that the Election Tribunal is competent to order for recounting of the ballot papers for proper adjudication of the Election Tribunal case. This finding of the High Court Division being based on correct appreciation of facts and law does not call for any interference by this Court." 40. In the case of Md Afzal Hossain vs The Government of Bangladesh, reported in 21 BLT (HC) 66 (2013) Para 28 (Judgment dated 7-11-2012) High Court Division considered the issue of 'recounting ballot papers' and set-aside the judgment and order passed by the Tribunals below and emphasized to 'maintain the sanctity of ballot papers' holding that; "A recount will not be granted as a matter of right but only on the basis of evidence of good grounds for believing that there has been a mistake in counting. The reasons are that such order affects the secrecy of ballots which is under the law is not to be lightly disturbed. The secrecy of the ballot is sacrosanct and shall not be permitted to be violated and merely for asking on vague and indefinite allegations or averments of general nature. Our view is that the averments made in the petition and the material brought on record by the respondent No.7 did not make out a case of recount. The allegations of irregularity or improper counting of ballots have not been pleaded adequately and specifically and the evidence adduced by the election petitioner regarding improper counting of ballots each of the Polling Centres are insufficient and the allegations are not at all proved. Both the Tribunals acted unlawfully in passing the order of inspection and recounting the ballot papers inasmuch as the respondent No.7 failed to establish the factual foundation of it by adducing sufficient evidence bringing specific allegation of improper counting of each of the Polling Centres; 41. In the case of Abdul Mannaf vs Election Commission reported in 23 BLC 837 Para 48. (Judgment dated 7-5-2018) AKM Abdul Hakim J has held that; "It appears that the Rule 62 of the Election Rules, 2010 clearly provides that the Election Tribunal or Election Appellate Tribunal has jurisdiction to open the ballot box and inspect the counted ballot papers and passed an order for recounting." 42. In Indian jurisdiction, in the case of Suresh Prasad vs Jai Prakash Mishra and others reported in AIR 1975 (SC) 376, RS Sarkaria J has also expressed the similar view and formulated guidelines to allow 'recounting ballot papers' and held that; "Before dealing with these contentions, we may recall, what this Court has repeatedly said, that an order for inspection and recount of the ballot papers cannot be made as a matter of course. The reason is twofold. Firstly such order affects the secrecy of the ballot which under the law is not to be lightly disturbed. Secondly, the Rules provide an elaborate procedure for counting of ballot papers. This procedure contains so many statutory checks and effective safeguards against trickery, mistakes, and fraud in counting, that it can be called almost fool-proof. Although no hard and fast rule can be laid down, yet the broad guidelines, as discernible from the decisions of this Court may be indicated thus: "The Court would be justified in ordering a recount of the ballot papers only where: (i) The election petition contains an adequate statement of all the materials facts on which the allegations of irregularity or illegality in counting are founded; (ii) On the basis of evidence adduced such allegation are prima-facie established, affording a good for believing that there has been a mistake in counting; and (iii) That Court trying the petition is prima-facie satisfied that the making of such an order is imperatively necessary to decide the dispute and to do complete and effectual justice between the parties." 43. On perusal of the evidence of OPW 16 and report dated 12-9-2016 submitted by the Returning Officer it is found that when the record room was opened to collect the election material. in compliance of the order of the Tribunal, the gunny begs containing election materials of No. 3 Parramrampur Union Parishad, Dewangonj, Jamalpur along with other gunny bags of other Union Parishad was found open, unsealed and torn and at the time of recounting ballot papers the Returning Officer produced open, unsealed and torn gunny begs before the Election Tribunal and the Sheristadar of the concerned Tribunal below by order of the Tribunal recounted ballot papers kept in open, unsealed and torn gunny begs. 44. In the election petition, respondent No. 3 has specifically mentioned that the supporters of the writ-petitioner forcibly driven out the agents of the respondent No. 3 from the polling centers and illegally cast votes in favour of the writ-petitioner. During cross-examination of OPW No. 1, the writ-petitioner affirmed that his supporters forcibly driven out the agents of respondent No. 3 from the polling centers and there was election violence in 12 (twelve) centers and thereafter the supporters of the writ-petitioner illegally cast votes in his favour. During cross-examination of PW No. 4 it has been affirmed that supporters of the writ-petitioner illegally cast votes in his favour. The Election Tribunal allowed recounting on the ground that none of the election agents of the respondent No. 3 signed the election result. 45. It is also found that after holding election, respondent No. 3 filed an application to the Chief Election Commissioner on 2-6-2016 for setting aside the result declared by the Returning Officer or to recount ballot papers but the Election Commission did not dispose of the said application. It is our considered view that after holding election, if an application is filed by any contesting candidate alleging corrupt practice adopted by the returned candidate or by any other person for which the election was allegedly materially affected, the Election Commission shall dispose of such application before publication of the election result in the Bangladesh Gazette assigning reason. 46. Although the Election Tribunal declared the respondent No. 3 as elected Chairman of No. 3 Parramrampur Union Parishad but the election result published by the Election Commission in Gazette Notification on 21-6-2016 has not been set-aside. 47. We are of the view that an inquiry should be held by the Election Commission to take appropriate action against the person/ persons responsible for tempering election materials after handing over ballot papers by the Presiding Officers to the Election Officer, Upzila-Dewangonj, District-Jamalpur and before producing those to the Tribunal. 48. In the above facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that at the time of holding election on 28-5-2016, the supporter of the writ-petitioner forcibly driven out agents of the respondent No. 3 from the polling centers and illegally cast votes in favour of the writ- petitioner for which election was materially affected and during recounting ballot papers, the intact gunny begs was not produced before the Tribunal and the Tribunals below committed serious error of law apparent on the face of the records in declaring the defeated candidate as Chairman of No. 3 Parramrampur Union Parishad on the basis of the result of recounting ballot papers kept in open, unsealed and torn gunny begs. Therefore, the judgment and order passed by the Tribunals below are liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 49. In the result, the judgment and order dated 1-8-2018 passed by respondent No. 1, the Election Appellate Tribunal, Jamalpur, in Election Appeal No. 3 of 2018 affirming those dated 28-5-2016 passed by the respondent No. 2, the Election Tribunal, Jamalpur, in Election Tribunal Case No. 27 of 2016 declaring the respondent No. 3 as Chairman of No. 3 Parramrampur Union, Upazila-Dewangonj, Jamalpur and the election result of No. 3 Parramrampur Union, Upazila -Dewangonj ,Jamalpur published by the Election Commission in Bangladesh Gazette on 21-6-2016 are hereby set-aside. 50. We direct the Election Commission to hold re-election of No. 3 Parramrampur Union Parishad, Dewangonj Upazila, Jamalpur afresh within 4 (four) months from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment and order. 51. With the above direction, the Rule is disposed of. There will be no order as to costs. End.

full_judgment:
Md Ashfaqul Islam J : This Rule under adjudication, issued on 26-11-2017, at the instance of the petitioners, was in the following terms:

"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order No. 65 dated 17-9-2011 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No.3, Dhaka in Artha Rin Suit No. 382 of 1990 (Annexure '1-3') and the order Nos. 12, 16 and 95 dated 31-10-2012, 10-1-2013 and 12-11-2017 respectively passed in the Artha Zari Case No.277 of 201 land initiation proceedings of the Artha Zari Case No.277 of 2011 (Annexure `J-8') should not be declared illegal and have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

Pending hearing of the Rule, let the order Nos. 12, 16 and 95 dated 31-10-2012, 10-1-2013 and 12-11-2017 respectively passed in the Artha Zari Case No. 277 of 2011 and proceedings of the Artha Zari Case No. 277 of 2011 (Annexure ',1-8') pending before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka be stayed for a period of 3(three) months."

2. And also the parties were directed to maintain status-quo.

3. Averments leading to the Rule which are relevant would only be narrated. The facts are as follows:

In this petition if we summarise the Rule we find that the petitioners have mainly challenged the initiation of the proceedings of Artha Zari Case No. 277 of 2011 (hereinafter referred to as Zari Case) and also challenged order No. 65 dated 17-9-2011 passed by Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as Adalat) in Artha Rin Suit No. 382 of 1990 and also Order Nos. 12, 16 and 95 dated 31-10-2012, 10-1-2013 and 12-11-2017 respectively in the said Zari Case. The petitioners in the petition has asserted in paragraph 4 that they are the legal owners and possessors of Schedule 'A' property that is 300 square yard of land wherein a six-storied residential building is situated at Mirpur under Mouja—Senpara Parbata, PS—Mirpur, Dsitrict-Dhaka, under Plot No. 7, Avenue No. 1, Block-F, Section-2, Plan No. 131/2 of 60/61 dated 23-11-1961.

4. In paragraph 5 of the petition a genealogy has been given how the petitioners became the owners of the property. It has been stated that father of the instant petitioners namely Sheikh Ismail Hossain vide registered sale deed No. 8859 dated 2-10-2007 got the property from one Mrs. Anjuara Begum. The petitioner's father by registered hiba deed being Nos. 11089, 11090, 11091, 11092 and 11100 all dated 19-8-2010 gifted the property to the petitioners. Thereafter, he died.

5. On 20-3-2013 petitioner No. 2 got information from his father-in-law that respondent No. 2, Pubali Bank Ltd. Bangabandhu Avenue Branch, Dhaka has filed the Artha Zari case No. 277 of 2011 (in question) to execute the decree passed in favour of the bank against respondent Nos. 3 to 8 in Artha Rin Suit No. 382 of 1990.

6. It has also been stated in the petition that in the said Zari Case respondent No. 3, M/s Rony Construction Ltd. took a loan from Pubali Bank, that is respondent No. 2 and subsequently bank filed Artha Rin Suit No. 382 of 1990 before Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka against respondent Nos. 3 to 9 for recovery of outstanding dues amounting to Taka 3,26,083.86 from the borrower that is respondent No. 3. The suit was decreed in favour of Pubali Bank and the bank being dissatisfied with the decretal amount and the rate of interest till 25-11-1986 preferred First Appeal No. 170 of 1992 before this Division and upon hearing on 20-10-2009 the appeal was allowed and the decretal amount was increased to Taka 4,16,611.07 with 15½% interest from 25-11-1986.

7. Be it mentioned that the judgment of First Appeal was passed on 20-10-2009 and decree was drawn up on 20-5-2010 and the Execution Case was filed on 28-11-2011. These are all admitted facts. The bank then filed an application before the Adalat for modification of decree on 11-8-2011 and the Adalat on 17-8-2011 by Order No. 65 modified the decree and thereafter, of course on 28-11-2011 the bank filed Zari Case No. 277 of 2011.

8. However, in the meantime the respondent No. 10 on 31-10-2012 participated in the auction bid and succeeded. Subsequently, on 31-1-2013 Bainanama was executed in his favour by the Adalat (consideration money was 25 lac).

9. Now comes the second aspect of the factual matrics that is how the instant writ-petitioners have entered into the scene. It has been stated that after filing of the Zari Case the instant petitioners filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2013 under Order XXI, rule 90 read with section 151 of Code of Civil Procedure and section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. 2003 (hereinafter referred to as Ain) on 27-3-2013 and also filed an application for staying the further proceedings of the Zari Case and on 3-4-2013 the Adalat stayed the further proceedings of the Zari Case till disposal of the said Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2013 and on 19-3-2017 the Adalat passed an order to start the proceedings of the Zari Case without vacating the earlier order of stay dated 3-4-2013 and on 9-10-2017 the Adalat passed an order to issue a letter to the authority of the police for fixing a date for handing over the possession in favour of the respondent No. 10 and on 7-11-2017 the writ-petitioners filed an application under section 33(7)(Kha) read with section 57 of the Ain and on 9-11-2017 the bank filed written objection and the auction purchaser filed an application for handing over the possession after breaking the gate-lock and on the same day Adalat fixed the date on 12-11-2017 for hearing of those applications and on 12-11-2017 the respondent No. 10 filed application for handing over the possession of the case property and also filed a written objection to the application of the writ-petitioners dated 7-11-2017 and the bank also filed an application to call for record of the Artha Rin Suit and the writ-petitioners filed objection against the application for handing over possession and on the same day the acting judge without considering the earlier order dated 9-11-2017 issued the দখলী পরওয়ানা and on 13-11-2017 the Adalat rejected the application for recalling the order of দখলী পরওয়ানা as well as the application for handing over the possession after breaking the gate-lock (Annexure-T to `J-8').

10. It has been stated that since the petitioners were not aware of the Artha Rin Suit No. 382 of 1990 and the Zari Case No. 277 of 2011 before 20-3-2013 and they were not party in the Suit, they could not participate in the auction and property was sold at a shockingly low price.

11. It has also been stated that admittedly after 19 years of passing of the judgment and decree by the Adalat Zari Case No. 277 of 2011 was filed on 28-11-2011 which is barred by law. It has been also stated that the petitioners by mistake and due to ill advice filed writ petition No. 10576 of 2017 before this Division and ultimately it went to the Hon'ble Appellate Division and the Hon'ble Appellate Division sent the case for disposal to this Division and eventually on 2-11-2012 the said writ petition was discharged for non-prosecution since the subject-matter of the same was pending before the Adalat in Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2013 filed by the petitioners.

12. Be that as it may that being the factual aspects of the case, the petitioners as it has been mentioned above filed this writ petition and obtained the Rule and order of stay and status-quo.

13. Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr Sk Reajul Haque, the learned Advocate for the petitioners after placing the petition and other materials on record mainly contended that this Division in First Appeal No. 170 of 1992 enhancing the claim of the bank allowed the appeal and passed Judgment and decree on 20-10-2009 and after obtaining the certified copy of the judgment and decree on 20-5-2010 did not file any execution case within the statutory period as per section 28 of the Ain for which the Zari Case No. 277 of 2011 is ex-facie barred by limitation and, as such, the proceedings of the Zari case is liable to declare to have been passed without lawful authority.

14. He further elaborates his submissions that the provision of section 28 is a mandatory one which should be interpreted strictly. The learned senior Advocate further submits that the order No. 65 dated 17-8-2011 by which the decree itself was modified by the Adalat was not at all necessary and was a futile exercise and also without lawful authority in as much as after pronouncement of the judgment and decree by this Division in the First Appeal, and the modification since done by this Division itself, the decision merged in the decree of the Adalat.

15. Mr Ahsanul Karim, the learned Advocate appears as amicus curie in the instant writ petition. He has further elaborated the arguments of senior Advocate Mr Mahbubey Alam and submitted that the point of limitation as argued by Mr Mahbubey Alain should be construed strictly. Further he added that section 29 of the Ain if be read gives a clear picture that the law under section 28 should be interpreted strictly. In support of his submissions he has cited an unreported decision of the Appellate Division in the Case of Agrani Bank limited vs Mrs Rina Humayun in Civil Appeal No. 164 of 2015.

16. He also submits that the second argument of Mr Mahbubey Alam has also force, relying on the decision of M Majid vs Iqbal Bahar Chowdhury, 5 BLC AD 7. He has drawn our notice to paragraph 5, 6 and 10 of the reference and submitted that the executing Court cannot give any decision when admittedly the High Court Division itself has modified the decree passed by the Adalat modifying the same.

17. Mr Imam Khaled Rahim appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 10 and Mr Abdullah-Al-Mubin appearing for the respondent No. 2 bank by filing two separate affidavit-in-opposition opposes the Rule. Mr Rahim submits that section 28 certainly should be applied strictly but at the same time provision of section 29 has to be taken into consideration. He further submits that section 29 has given a flexibility in respect of payment of installments since it clearly enjoins that at the time of passing of the decree if Adalat directs payment to be made by installment and fix a particular time then provisions of section 28(1) of the Ain shall apply after the period of installment so directed by the Adalat in overall or it has become ineffective. Thereby he wants to mean that in the instant decree since there was an order by the Adalat allowing the judgment-debtor to pay of the decretal amount by four equal installments, by implication of section 29, limitation prescribed in section 28(1) shall apply after the expiry of the said time fixed by the Adalat. In support of his contention he placed reliance in the decision of M/s MM Steel Limited vs the Judge, 1st Court of the Artha Rin Adalat, Chattogram, 19 BLT AD 184 and another decision of Md Shamsul Alam Talukdar vs Bangladesh, 16 BLT 440. He also submits that the writ-petitioners have no locus standi to file this writ petition on the ground that they were not a party to the original proceedings and further, as he submits, Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2013 at the instance of this writ-petitioners is still pending in which the petitioners will be able to establish their case as a third party.

18. Be that as it may we have heard the learned Counsels of both sides and considered their submissions at length. We have gone through the writ petition, supplementary-affidavit filed by the petitioners, affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent No. 2 bank and respondent No. 10, different citations by the parties and of course other materials on record.

19. The only question that calls for consideration by us in this petition is whether under the facts and circumstances of the case conjunct with the interpretation of section 28, 29 and 49(3) of the Ain this writ petition would sustain.

20. At the very outset it would be expedient to note that genealogy that has been given in the writ petition has not been denied by the respondent. The real controversy starts in respect of interpretation regarding the scope of section 28 read with 29 and section 49(3) of the Ain. Two different submissions we have received from the Bar. Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned senior Advocate has emphatically argued that this writ petition is expressly barred since after obtaining the decree on 20-5-2010, Artha Zari Case No. 277 of 2011 which was filed on 28-11-2011 was expressly filed after the statutory period of limitation prescribed in section 28(1) of the Ain. His contention is that this cannot be interpreted in isolation but conjunctly with section 29. Mr Ahsanul Karim reiterating the submissions of the learned senior Advocate further contends that section 29 by implication has rather made the provision of section 28(1) to be construed strictly. He also submits that the decision referred by Mr Rahim, the learned Counsel appearing for the respondent No. 10 does not apply since the same was not delivered after granting leave. For better understanding let us quote the relevant law having bearing on the issue in verbatim. Section 28(1) of the Ain runs thus:

“২৮।- The Limitation Act, 1908 এবং The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 এ ভিন্নতর যে বিধানই থাকুক না কেন, ডিক্রীদার, আদালতযোগে ডিক্রী বা আদেশ কার্যকর করিতে ইচ্ছা করিলে, ডিক্রী বা আদেশ প্রদত্ত হওয়ার অনূর্ধ্ব [১ (এক) বৎসরের মধ্যে), ধারা ২৯ এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে জারীর জন্য আদালতে দরখাস্ত দাখিল করিয়া মামলা করিবে ।”

Next section 29 enjoins:

“২৯ । আদালত, রায় প্রদানের সময় ডিক্রীকৃত টাকা এককালীন অথবা কিস্তিতে পরিশোধের জন্য কোন সময়সীমা নির্ধারণ করিয়া থাকিলে, অনুরূপ সময়সীমা অতিক্রান্ত বা অকার্যকর হইবার পর হইতে ধারা ২৮১) এ উল্লিখিত সময়সীমা কার্ধকর হইবে ।”

Finally section 49(1) states:

“৪৯ ।-(১) উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে অর্থ খণ আদালত, বিবাদী-দায়িকের আবেদনের প্রেক্ষিতে বা স্বীয় উদ্যোগে উপর্যুক্ত মনে করিলে, ডিক্রীকৃত টাকা ১ (এক) বৎসরে ৪ চোর) টি সম কিস্তিতে পরিশোধের জন্য দায়িককে সুযোগ প্রদান করিতে পারিবে ।

(২) বাদী-ডিক্রীদার সম্মত থাকিলে, উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, ডিক্রীকৃত টাকা ৩ (তিন) বৎসরে ১২ বোর) টি সমকিস্তিতে পরিশোধের জন্য আদালত, দায়িককে সুযোগ প্রদান করিতে পারিবে ।

(৩) উপ-ধার (১) বা (২) এ উল্লিখিত কোন একটি কিস্তি বকেয়া হওয়া মাত্রই সমুদয় বকেয়া তখনই পরিশোধিতব্য হইবে এবং তদৃউদ্দেশ্যে জারী কার্যক্রম যথাবিধি অনুসৃত হইবে ।”

21. His submission is that section 28 and 29 supplements one and other. In the unreported decisions of Civil Appeal No. 164 of 2015 Agrani Bank Limited vs Mrs Rina Humayun my lord Justice Hasan Foez Siddique in clear terms observed:

"First appeal was dismissed on 17-11-2001. There was no order of stay of the execution of the decree. The said appeal was dismissed for non-payment of Court-fees. Execution case was filed on 01-9-2003. As per provision of section 28(1) and (2) of the Ain the decree holder had to file execution case within 180 days of the decree (In 2008, amending the Ain one year was provided in place of 180 days) subject to provision of section 29 of the Ain. The Adalat directed the judgment-debtor to pay the decretal dues by 6 installments. First installment was to be paid by 10-9-1991. It was mentioned in the decree that, in case of failure to deposit any installment, the decree holder would be entitled to take steps for realization of the amount. The decree holder bank did not file the execution case within the stipulated time. Section 28(2) of the Ain provides that:

“(২) উপ-ধারা (১) এর বিধানের ব্যত্যয়ে, ডিক্রী বা আদেশ প্রদানের পরবর্তী [১ (এক) বৎসর] অতিবাহিত তামাদিতে বারিত হইবে এবং অনুরূপ তামাদিতে বারিত মামল৷ আদালত কার্ধার্থে গ্রহণ না করিয়া সরাসরি খারিজ করিবে ।”

In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, it appears to us that the instant execution case was hopelessly barred by limitation and the Adalat ought to have dismissed the execution case".

22. What we have found in the said decision? First installment was to be paid by 10-9-1991 failing which it was incumbent upon the decree holder bank to initiate execution case in which it failed and it was observed that the Adalat ought to have dismissed the execution case simply on that score. His Lordship mentioned section 29 of the Ain while interpreting the same. This decision is a subsequent one from which it can be safely inferred that section 29 is indeed in its implication should be interpreted strictly with section 28(1).

23. In the instant case the modified decree as it appears in order No. 65 dated 17-8-2011 of Artha Rin Suit No. 382 of 1990 clearly says that—

“অত্র দেওয়ানী মোকদ্দমাটি দোতরফা সূত্রে ৪ নং বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে এবং একতরফা সূত্রে ১-৩ ও ৫-৭ নং বিবাদীগণের বিরুদ্ধে খরচাসহ আংশিক প্রাথমিক ডিক্রী দেওয়া হইল । ডিক্রীর ১ (এক) বছরের মধ্যে সমান ৪ (চার) কিস্তিতে বিবাদীগণের ২৪-১১-৮৬ ইং তারিখ পর্যস্ত পাওনা ৩,২৬,০৮৩.৮৬ €তিন লক্ষ ছাবিবশ হাজার তিরাশি টাকা ছিয়াশি পয়সা) ৪,১৬,৬১১.০৭ (চার লক্ষ ষোল হাজার ছয়শত এগার টাকা/সাত পয়সা) এবং ২৫-১১-৮৬ তারিখ হইতে আদায় কালতক ১৫/% হারে সুদ- টাকা এবং মামলার খরচ বাদী ব্যাংক বরাবরে প্রদান করিবে । অন্যথায় বাদী এই ডিক্রী চূড়ান্ত করানোর মাধ্যমে আদালত যোগে নালিশী সম্পত্তি বিক্রয় করিয়া পাওনা আদায় করিতে পারিবে ।”

24. From the wordings of decree itself we find that a positive prohibition has been clearly spelt out. It has stated that decretal amount should be paid in four equal installments. Therefore, for all practical purposes it can be interpreted that legislature intended that if a particular installment has been defaulted, it is incumbent upon the decree-holder bank to file execution case from the said date of default. The word and phrases " অকার্যকার " in section 29 of the Ain fortifies this aspect. In the instant case when not a single installment was paid then how can it be said that section 29 of the Ain will give a flexibility to the bank? Because we cannot read section 29 of the Ain without the word " অকার্যকার " if we could so read then the things would have been different. And if the decree was passed without any installment then also the interpretation may have been different. If now we add the provisions of section 49(3) then the proposition of law as we have interpreted becomes all the more fortified.

25. Fiscal law should be interpreted and construed in its strict application. In the renowned decision of Director of Taxation and Excise of Government of East Pakistan vs Mehdi All Khan Panni 32 DLR (AD) 138 our Appellate Division came down heavily in interpreting fiscal statutes alongside doctrine of laissez-faire and welfare economy. His Lordships Justice Kemaluddin Hossain observed as under:

"In interpreting a taxing statute a controversy often arises and learned authorities are cited in support of the proposition that a taxing statute is to be construed strictly in favour of the subject. But this view though not abandoned in case of unresolved ambiguity, does no longer get the one-sided support from the judicial authorities. The view of strict construction prevailed at a time when the doctrine of laissez faire was the ruling principle of economy of a state, but almost all the leading States of the world have long abandoned the doctrine, and adopted the welfare doctrine of economy. Even a country like England where the doctrine of laissez-faire originated has abandoned it in favour of welfare economy. The newly emerging nations like ours have mostly adopted the welfare doctrine.

A taxing statute is to be interpreted on the language used in the statute. No tax can be imposed on the citizen without the word in an Act of the Legislature clearly showing the intention to lay a burden on him. When that intention is sufficiently shown, it is not open to speculate on what would be the fair and most equitable mode of levying tax.

In a fiscal or taxing statute on has to look merely at what is clearly said therein, for there is no room for any intendment, nor for any equity or for any presumption. In case of unresolved ambiguity, it may be interpreted favorably to the citizen but nothing more. The attempt of the Court in case of justice and fairness and to try to arrive at a true meaning of the word."

Harping on the same tune and fortified with the latest unreported decision of the Appellate Division as mentioned above we are also of the view that the submissions of the learned senior Advocate Mr Mahbubey Alam and Mr Ahsanul Karim (appeared as amicus curie) in the instant case merit substance on the point of limitation.

<u>26. To address the second argument we want to reiterate the settled principle of laws that once a decree has been modified by the Court of appeal there cannot be a subsequent interference by the court below. Since the said decree have had merged in the decision of the trial court, anything done subsequent to that would be absolutely void. Reflection can be found in the decision reported in 5 BLC (AD) 7 wherein it has been observed by his lordship Justice Latifur Rahman:</u>

<u>“It is to be stated a the outset that the decree of the trial Court as passed in the Title Suit No. 4 of 1994 was modified by the High Court of the then East Pakistan on 22-3-1960. The decree of the trial Court having been modified by the High Court it merged into the decree of the High Court. Hence, the question of drawing up of a modified decree on 9-8-1993 in the light of the judgment and decree of the High Court in First Appeal is wholly illegal and without jurisdiction. It is found that the modified decree was passed on 22-3-1960 and to avoid the question of limitation a modified decree was again drawn up by the trail Court on 9-8-1993 and which is so obvious that it was obtained from a court by fraudulent means. Even if, it is admitted that a mistake was committed by the executing court itself even then there are innumerable authorities of this court to hold that any error or wrong committed by the court itself can be corrected in exercise of its jurisdiction under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to secure the ends of Justice and to prevent the abuse of process of court. Thus, the execution proceeding is apparently barred under Article 182 of the Limitation Act. The plaintiff did not take any steps within three years from the modified decree of the High Court nor he kept alive the decree by taking modified decree. Thus in order to avoid the bar of limitation the plaintiff fraudulently got the modified decree drawn up by the trial Court. Hence the application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is maintainable in the facts of the present case."</u>

27. Therefore, on that count also the submissions of the learned senior Counsel has sufficient force.

<u>28. On the question of locus stanch, we want to observe that the suit was decreed back in the year of 1992 but from the writ petition we have found that the subject-matter which is a part of A-schedule of the property of plaint was given to the writ-petitioners by their father in the year 2010 of course their stakes in the subject-matter in the writ petition will be decided in the miscellaneous case which is pending before the trial Court and therefore, we refrain from making any comments on that issue. But fact remains that if this writ petition could not have brought by the instant petitioner then certainly there would have been a gross miscarriage of justice in respect of a preliminary point which is the point of limitation. Therefore, owing to that reason we are of the view that the writ-petitioners have locus standi to file this petition.</u>

29. That being the position it is our considered view that this writ petition merits substance which should succeed.

In the result the Rule is made absolute, however, without any order as to cost. The order impugned is declared to have been passed without lawful authority having no legal effect and hereby set-aside.

End.
