(ii) In order to impose a right, the same would have to be founded on legal basis and that since the petitioners' right of getting "User Fees" is not sanctioned by law, the same cannot be imposed or given validity.

(iii) Drawing our attention to the Syndicate meeting of 2007, Mr. Alam contends that although the decision of the Syndicate was to sharing "User Fees" as per ratio 70-30 only from the profit excluding the maintenance costs but that has not been executed by the concerned departments which have been reflected in the audit reports and thus, the petitioners have not come with the clean hand. Therefore, they are not entitled to get any equitable relief under the constitutional jurisdiction of this Court.

(iv) The petitioners are getting all allowances and benefits under the terms and conditions of their service and the sharing of "User Fees" is not being including in their service terms, question of curtailment of such sharing without giving opportunity of being heard, does not arise and at the same time the cited cases of the petitioners are not applicable in this particular case.

22. We have gone through the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondents Nos. 2-4 and the supplementary affidavits filed by both the contending parties and other materials on record.

23. The basic issue centers upon a term, namely, "User Fees" which are being collected from the patients relating to their health related investigations. At the very outset, Mr. Tanjib ul Alam, in his submissions, emphasized on a particular point that sharing of "User Fees" has not been sanctioned legally by the Act, 1998. To consider his submission, we have gone through the University Act, 1998 as well as the previous orders relating to sharing of "User Fees". In the writ petition, the petitioners have stated that since 1937 the "User Fees" are being shared among the employees of the concerned departments of the respective hospitals. We find a Government order issued by the then Ministry of Health and Population Control being memo No.এমএইএইচ/১এম-১৫/৮৩/৭৮৮ dated 5-2-1984 (Annexure-C to the writ petition) whereby the teachers and the employees of the concerned departments of the respective hospitals have been sharing the "User Fees". At the relevant time, the University was a government establishment and accordingly, its employees and teachers had been enjoying the said sharing in accordance with the said office order. Subsequently by the Act, 1998 the University has been established and an office order was issued on 21-7-1998 (Annexure-N to the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioners) relevant portions of which are as follows:

“বঙ্গবন্ধু শেখ মুজিব মেডিক্যাল বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের চাকুরীতে আত্নীকৃত (যাহারা বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের শিক্ষক, চিকিৎসক, নার্স, কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারী হিসাবে থাকিবেন) শিক্ষক, চিকিৎসক, নার্স ও অন্যান্য সকল শ্রেণীর কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারীদের দেয় সুযোগ সুবিধা ১লা আগষ্ট ১৯৯৮ ইং হইতে কার্যাকারী হইবে-

25. From the aforesaid office order, it appears that existing salary, allowances and other financial benefits given by the Government to the employees shall continue in respect of absorbed employees of the University after its establishment by the University Act, 1998. Relying upon the said office order, Mr Chowdhury submits that subsequently the University issued the office orders dated 27-12-1998 and 24-3-1999 relating to sharing of "User Fees" and thereby it has got legal sanction. But these office orders are not enough to adopt the previous benefits by the employees of the University. Since the Act, 1998 does not incorporate any such provision, certainly there should be a Syndicate decision. However, in this regard, we find that the Syndicate by its meeting dated 27-5-2007 took decision relating to sharing of "User Fees" by the concerned departments of the University. The relevant portion of the minutes of the said Syndicate meeting are as follows:

“আলোচ্য সূচী-৬:

ল্যাবরেটরী ও অন্যান্য পরীক্ষা-নিরীক্ষা এবং বিভিন্ন Operational Procedure থেকে প্রাপ্ত অর্থ থেকে Reagent ও অন্যান্য খরচ বাদে লভ্যাশের ৩০% শিক্ষক, চিকিগসকু কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারীগণের মধ্যে বন্টনের বিষয়ে বিবেচনা ।

সিদ্ধান্তঃ

ল্যাবরেটরী ও অন্যান্য পরীক্ষা-নিরীক্ষা Operational Procedure থেকে প্রাপ্ত অর্থ সংশ্লিষ্ট বিভাগের শিক্ষক,

চিকিৎসক কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারীগণের মধ্যে বন্টনের বিষয়ে কয়েকজন সদস্য আলোচনায় অংশগ্রহণ করেন।

অধ্যাপক এ.কে.এম আজিজুল হক কোন কোন বিভাগের অর্জিত অর্থ থেকে নির্ধারিত অংশ কোন কোন বিভাগের শিক্ষক,

চিকিৎসক কর্মকর্তা ও কমচারীর মধ্যে বন্টন করা হয় তা তিনি সভায় জানতে চান।

বেসিক মেডিক্যাল সায়েস অনুষদের বিভাগ সমূহ রেডিওলজি এন্ড ইমেজিং, কার্ডিয়াক সার্জারি ইত্যাদি বিভাগের

অর্জিত অর্থ সংশ্লিষ্ট বিভাগের শিক্ষক, চিকিৎসক কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারীগণের মধে বন্টন করা হয় বলে মাননীয় ভাইস চ্যান্সেলর সভাকে অবহিত করেন । বিস্তারিত আলোচনার শেষে ল্যাবরেটরী ও অন্যান্য পরীক্ষা এবং বিভিন্ন perational Procedure থেকে অর্জিত অর্থ থেকে বিভিন্ন Reagent এবং পরীক্ষা-নিরীক্ষা সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রচলিত ও অন্যান্য খরচ বাদ দিয়ে লভ্যাংশের ৩০% শিক্ষক, চিকিৎসক কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারীর আনুপাতিক হারে বন্টনের সিদ্ধান্ত গৃহিত হল।”

26. On a plain reading of the aforesaid decision of the Syndicate, we find that the distribution of "User Fees" got sanction by the Syndicate through its meeting dated 27-5-2007. As such, we are unable to accept submission of Mr. Alam that the "User Fees" are distributed among the concerned departments without any legal sanction. Moreover, it is not the issue in this Rule and if this is the position then why the University by the impugned decision are sharing it among more other departments instead of stopping distribution of the same.

27. Now let us examine the impugned decision as to whether it has been taken in accordance with law. First of all "User Fees" are the University Fund within the meaning of section 48 of the University Act, 1998. Section 48 of the Act, 1998 describes the University Fund (বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের তহবিল) which are as follow:

৪৮। বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের তহবিল ।-

(১) বঙ্গবন্ধু শেখ মুজিব মেডিক্যাল বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় তহবিল নামে বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের একটি তহবিল থাকিবে ।

(২) বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের তহবিলে নিন্ললিখিত অর্থ জমা হইবে।

যথাঃ

(ক)-(জ)।

(ঝ) বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় কর্তৃক ধার্যকৃত বিভিন্ন ফি, চার্জ ইত্যাদি ।

(ঞ) ……………………………….

28. On perusal of aforesaid provision it is clear that "User Fees" collected by the University are part of the University Fund and it is determined by the University i.e the Syndicate, the chief executive organ of the University in accordance with section 23 of the Act, 1998. The impugned order, challenged under this Rule refers to the 70th Syndicate meeting of the University held on 12-6-2018 (Annexure-2 to the affidavit-in-opposition). Referring to the minutes of the said meeting, Mr. Chowdhury submits that section 23(2)(Ga) of the Act, 1998 has been violated by the Syndicate in taking the impugned decision. To appreciate his submission, let us see the relevant provisions which are quoted herein below:

“২৩। সিন্ডিকেটের ক্ষমতা ও দায়িত্বঃ

১ সিন্ডিকেট বিশ্ববিদ্যলয়ের প্রধান নির্বাহী সংস্থা হইবে এবং আইন ও মঞ্জুরী কমিশন আদেশের বিধান এবং ভাইস-চ্যান্সেলরের উপর অর্পিত ক্ষমতা সাপেক্ষে, বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের কার্যাবলী, প্রতিষ্ঠানসমূহ এবং সম্পত্তির উপর সিন্ডিকেটের সাধারণ, ব্যবস্থাপনা ও তত্বাবধানের ক্ষমতা থাকিবে এবং এই আইন, সংবিধি, বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের অধ্যাদেশ এবং প্রবিধানের বিধানসমূহ যথাযথভাবে পালিত হইতেছে কিনা, সেইদিকে লক্ষ্য রাখিবে।

২। উপ-ধারা (১) এর অধীনে প্রয়োগযোগ্য ক্ষমতা ও সামগ্রিকভাবে ক্ষুন্ন না করিয়া সিন্ডিকেট বিশেষত-

(ক)-(খ) ……………………………..।

(গ) অর্থ সংক্রান্ত বিষয়ে অর্থ কমিটির পরামর্শ গ্রহণ করিবে।

29. On perusal of the aforesaid provisions, it appears that relating to financial matters the Syndicate can take decision but subject to consultation with the Finance Committee. Since the issue as to sharing of "User Fees" involved financial matters, the Syndicate should consult and take advice from the Finance Committee before taking decision but here the respondent University has failed to show any such consultation with the Finance Committee and that from the minutes of the Syndicate meeting (Annexure-2 to the affidavit in opposition), we find that no such consultation was ever made with the Finance Committee which was a legal requirement in accordance with section 23(2)(Ga) of the Act, 1998. Therefore, we are led to hold that decision was not taken in accordance with law and hence it is liable to be declared without lawful authority.

30. Moreover, the petitioners and other employees of the concerned departments have been enjoying sharing of "User Fees" by 70-30 ratio for a longtime and this privilege cannot be curtailed without giving them an opportunity of being heard. Admittedly, no opportunity of hearing was given to the petitioners before taking the impugned decision reducing their share ratio to the "User Fees" and therefore, the impugned decision cannot sustain in the eye of law. This view of ours finds support from the case of Bangladesh vs Md. Abul Hossain, reported in 23 BLD (AD) 129 = 9 BLC (AD) 119; and the case of Agragami Engineers vs Bangladesh Bank, reported in 45 DLR.134. As we held above that the sharing of "User Fees" has got legal sanction, the case cited by Mr. Tanjibul Alam reported in 61 DLR (AD) 28 is not applicable in this particular case.

31. Further, if we look at the decision of Syndicate meeting dated 27-5-2007, it appears that the 70-30 ratio of the "Use! Fees" would be distributed only from the profit to be determined deducting the incurred costs on account of purchase of reagents, relevant materials for the tests and other infrastructural development and equipment’s and machineries maintenance costs but surprisingly, we find that 30% of the "User Fees" have been distributed from the total earned proceeds without deducting the incurred costs and thereby the costs were absolutely borne from the 70% ratio i.e part of the University Fund. Thus, the aforesaid decision of the Syndicate has not been followed and thereby violating this decision since 2007, the "User Fees" are being distributed beyond the said decision. The Court of law is always a vigilant guard against any abuse/misuse of power/authority by the state functionary in dealing with the state property and to see that the fundamental principles of state policy are preserved in furtherance of the protection of the rights and interests of its citizens. Therefore, the recipients who are sharing 70-30 ratio in the University beyond decision of the Syndicate are liable to refund the excess received amount in violation of the decision taken by the Syndicate of the University. Henceforth, the "User Fees" shall be shared by the concerned departments of the University after deducting the expenditures/ costs (i.e purchase of reagents and other ancillary costs associated with the tests, infrastructural establishment, development and purchase of equipment’s and machineries and maintenance thereof and also other miscellaneous costs) to be incurred for conducting the investigations.

32. Although the petitioners asserts that the prices of tests are cheap in comparison with private establishments. This comparison is very ridiculous and irrational inasmuch as the University laboratories are fully established by the State Fund, all concerned men powers are paid by the State (University Fund) while private concerns are being established by the private individuals in order to make profit by investing a huge amount and incurring a large amount of salary and other costs for the employees. Therefore, the citizens of the state are entitled to get service from the state owned and managed organizations at a much cheaper price keeping in mind about the article 18 of the Constitution which describes that the state shall regard the improvement of Public Health among its primary duties. Article 18 being one of the fundamental principles of state policy incorporated in part II of the constitution and that regarding part II of the Constitution article 8(2) of this part provides as follows:

৮।(২)  এই ভাগে বর্ণিত নীতি বর্ণিত নীতিসমুহ বাংলাদেশ-পরিচালনার মূলসূত্র হইবে, আইন-প্রণয়নকালে রাষ্ট্র তাহা প্রয়োগ করিবেন, এই সংবিধান ও বাংলাদেশের অন্যান্য আইনের ব্যাখ্যাদানের ক্ষেত্রে তাহা নির্দেশক হইবে এবং তাহা রাষ্ট্র

ও নাগরিকদের কার্ষের ভিত্তি হইবে, তবে এই সকল নীতি আদালতের মাধ্যমে বলবৎযোগ্য হইবে না।”

33. Therefore, for the better interest of the citizens of the state as well as towards ensuring public health, the price rates of the tests under management of the University must be cheaper and affordable by the mass people.

34. Given the aforesaid scenario, let us see how the price for the tests are fixed? In this regard, Mr. Chowdhury submits that a Committee has been constituted in accordance with the Ordinance, namely, “বঙ্গবন্ধু শেখ মুজিব মেডিক্যাল বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় (BSMMU)এর ল্যাবরেটরি সার্ভিস পরিচালনা অধ্যাদেশ।” and that the said Committee is empowered to fix the price of tests from time to time. To consider his submission, we have gone through the said Ordinance which was framed under the Act, 1998. We do not find that by this Ordinance the concerned departments or the Committee are authorized to fix the price of tests to be conducted by the aforementioned departments. Moreover, except a member nominated by the Finance Committee all other members of the said Committee are chairmen of the concerned departments and Dean of the Basic Science Faculty and so, if this Committee is allowed to fix the price of tests, they are being interested by sharing the profit ratio that would not be fair and reasonable. Moreover, it being a financial matter, the price of all tests under the University must be determined by the Syndicate having consultation with the Finance Committee after proper assessment relating to incurred expenditures on account of reagents purchase, development and maintenance of Laboratory equipment’s and all other related expenditures and also keeping in mind about citizens' interest as a whole, in particular, a matter involving public health, one of the fundamental principles of state policy under the Constitution of the country. Therefore, all tests price at present, have to be revised in accordance with the aforesaid observations.

<u>35. Every employees of the University including teachers are getting their salary and other service benefits in accordance with law in lieu of their service rendered to the University and so they should not be allowed to share an extra income/allowances beyond their service benefits in the garb of incentive or bonus sharing the "User Fees". Therefore, the employees and teachers of the University who are not involved with the concerned departments, cannot be allowed to share "User Fees". However, the teachers and employees of the concerned departments, since enjoying the "User Fees" from 1937 they are allowed to continue the same in a limited manner with condition. In this regard, the petitioners categorically state in the affidavit-in-reply that they have to work whole day in the University, in particular, from 8-30 am to 8-00 pm of the day. We appreciate their hard working duty and certainly they are entitled to get remuneration as they have been enjoying. At the same time, they are not supposed to have any extra time for private practice and it is also not humanly possible for a man to work more, after performing duty from 8-30 am to 8 pm of the day. Therefore, the petitioners as well as all the concerned persons (Technician, Staff and Teachers) of all concerned departments, who are getting incentive from the income of "User Fees", they should not be allowed to do private practice outside the University.</u>

36. In view of above discussions, we find merit in this Rule and hence the Rule is made absolute. The impugned office order bearing No. BSMMU/2018/8911 dated 7-8-2018 (Annexure-A to the writ petition) so far as it relates to paragraph No. 2, regarding distribution of "User Fees" is hereby declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect with the aforesaid observations and following directions:

(i) After decision of the Syndicate by the meeting dated 27-5-2007 the "User Fees" have to be distributed with the ratio 70:30 after deducting the costs incurred for purchasing reagents and

other ancillary materials, maintenance and development costs of laboratory. In this regard, the University after making calculation shall ensure refund of the amount which were distributed in excess among the employees and teachers.

(ii) From now distribution of "User Fees" shall be continued at the ratio 70:30 after deducting reagents costs and all other incidental costs to be incurred on account of earning "User Fees" including infrastructural development and maintenance of the Laboratories and its machineries and equipment’s.

(iii) The University shall review all prices of the medical examinations (tests) by the Syndicate with consultation of the Finance Committee keeping in mind the constitutional mandate as to public health, one of the fundamental principles of state policy.

(iv) All the teachers, technicians and employees of the departments of Microbiology, Virology, Biochemistry and Molecular Biology and the teachers and employees of the other departments of the University who enjoy/share "User Fees" are hereby restrained from doing any private practice and all the "User Fees" must be distributed after deducting the applicable taxes under the prevailing law.

37. The University is directed to formulate a Rule relating to sharing of "User Fees" in the concerned departments in the light of the observations made in this judgment.

38. Communicate a copy of this judgment and order to the respondents at once.

End.

caseno: Income Tax Reference Application No.05 of 2004
lawyer:
Mr. A. K. M. Shafiuddin, Advocate, For the Applicant. 
Ms. Nurun Nahar, A. A. G., For the Respondent.
parties:
Bangladesh Commerce Bank Ltd.
Vs.
The Commissioner of Taxes
full_judgment:
Borhanuddin, J: This application has been preferred by the applicant under section 160 of the Income Tax Ordinance (hereinafter stated 'the ordinance') in the year 2004 without referring any question of law. Today when the matter is taken up for delivering judgment, learned advocate for the applicant filed two supplementary affidavits. The supplementary affidavit sworn on 11.07.2011 contained three questions of law. Another supplementary affidavit sworn on 04.11.2018 clarifying factual and legal position for not formulating question of law in the original reference application.

<u>2. Preliminary question is that whether income' tax reference application filed by the applicant without formulating any question of law can be treated as an application under section 160 of the ordinance. It will be profitable to quote relevant provisions of law from the ordinance for filing reference application before the High Court Division, which are as follows:</u>

<u>Section 160. Reference to the High Court Division: "(1) The assessee or the Commissioner, may within ninety days from the date of receipt of the order of the Appellate Tribunal communicated to him under section 159, by application in the prescribed form, accompanied, in the case of an application by the assessee, by a fee of (two thousand taka), refer to the High Court Division any question of law arising out of such order." (4) On receipt of the notice of the date of hearing of the application, the respondent shall, at least seven days before the date of hearing, submit in writing a reply to the application; and he shall therein specifically admit or deny whether the question of law formulated by the applicant arises out of the order of the Appellant tribunal.  (5) If the question formulated by the applicant is, in the opinion of the respondent, defective, the reply shall state in what particulars the question is defective and what is the exact question of law, if any, which arises out of the said order, and the reply shall be in triplicate and be accompanied by the documents which are relevant to the question of law formulated in the application and which were produced before the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes, the Inspecting Joint Commissioner, the Appellate Joint Commissioner (or the Commissioner Appeals) or the Appellate Tribunal, as the case may be in the course of any proceedings relating to any order referred to in sub-section (2)(a) or (b). (6) Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 (IX of 1908) shall apply to an application under sub-section (1).</u>

3.  Section 161. Decision of the High Court Division:-(1) Where any case has been referred to the High Court Division under section 160, it shall be heard by a bench of not less than two judges and the provisions of section 98 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 (V of 1908), shall, so far as may he, apply in respect of such case. (2) The High Court Division shall, upon hearing any case referred to it under section 160, decide the question of law raised thereby and shall deliver its judgment thereon stating the grounds on which such decision is founded and shall send a copy of such judgment under the seal of the Court and signature of the Registrar to the Appellate Tribunal which shall pass such orders as are necessary to dispose of the case in conformity with the judgment".

(3) ------

(4) ------

4. On perusal of the above sections, it is plain that it is the duty of the applicant to set forth in the application the question of law arising out of the order of Tribunal which the applicant require under sub-section (1) of section 160 of the ordinance to be referred to the High Court Division. Clearly, an application under section 160(1) of the ordinance should specify the question of law which the applicant considers ought to be referred for decision to the High Court Division. Directions under section 161(2) of the ordinance are in the nature of `mandamus' and as a general rule such directions will not be issued unless the question of law brought before the High Court Division in any of the modes prescribed by law. We are of the view that under the ordinance, there is no scope to formulate question of law by way of filing supplementary affidavit swearing affidavit seven years after submitting original reference application. We cannot, therefore, admit the question of law by the assessee in this court. Mr. A. K. M. Shafiuddin, learned advocate tried to impress us by quoting sub-section (6) of section 160 of the ordinance that this Division has power to condone the delay if question of law formulated at any time subsequent to filing original reference application. From the language of sub-section (6) of section 160 of the ordinance it is clear that section 5 of the limitation act shall apply only to an application under sub-section (1) of section 160 of the ordinance. By sub-section (6) of section 160 it cannot be construed that after filing original application without referring any question of law, the applicant can formulate question of law by swearing supplementary affidavit after seven years. Learned advocate argued that Article 109 and 110 of the constitution empowers this Division to accept the question of law formulated subsequently by the applicant. Article 109 of the Constitution relates to Superintendence and control of this Division over courts and tribunal subordinate to it and Article 110 relates to transfer of cases from sub-ordinate courts to High Court Division. These Articles of the constitution has no manner of applicability in this case. Article 83 of the constitution as referred by the learned advocate relates to merit of the case but since no question of law brought before the High Court Division as prescribed by section 160(1) of the ordinance, we are of the view that instant reference application is not maintainable in the eye of law.

6. In such premises above, we are inclined to reject the reference application as being incompetent.

7. The connected rule is hereby discharged.

8. The registrar of the High Court Division is hereby directed to take step in accordance with section 161(2) of the ordinance.

End.

lawyer: Mr. Goutam Kumar Roy, Advocate, For the Petitioners
parties:
Sukchand Kirtonia and another
Vs.
Rajubala Pramanik and others
full_judgment:
Mahmudul Hoque, J: In this revision Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 08.09.2009 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Rajbari, in Title Appeal No. 76 of 2007 disallowing the same and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 25.05.2007 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Baliakandi, Rajbari, in Title Suit No. 37 of 2004 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioner, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 37 of 2004 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Rajbari, against the opposite party No. 1 for a decree of permanent injunction stating inter alia, that one Sridas Pramanik owned 102.25 sataks of land under schedule Ka-1, 12 sataks of land under schedule Kha-1, 155.18 sataks of land under schedule Ga-1, 26 sataks of land under schedule Gha-1, totaling 295.98 sataks or 2.96 acres. While said Sridas Pramanik was in possession and enjoyment of the same died leaving defendant No. 1, Rajubala Pramanik. She as wife of late Sridas Pramanik got life interest in the property. In her absence the plaintiff being grandson of Sridas Pramanik will get the property as reversionary. After the death of Sridas Pramanik all the maintenance of defendant No. 1 are being met from the income of the suit property. Recently, at the ill advise of her paternal relatives the defendant No. 1 took step on 18.04.2004 for transferring the suit property to some persons and threatened the plaintiff that she will dispose of the suit property at any time, hence the present suit.

3. Defendant No. I contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia that the suit has no cause of action; barred by limitation and defect of parties. Further case of the defence are that, she is the wife of late Sridas Pramanik and the suit property belonged to her husband and after the death of her husband she inherited the property as widow for life time. It is also stated that the plaintiff did not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit property since the defendant No. 1 is still alive. The defendant No. 1 has been possessing the same on payment of rent to the government and she purchased 27 sataks of land under S.A. khatian No. 370 by a registered deed dated 16.04.1988 from some co-sharers and she is 8 annas share holder in the suit property by purchase and 8 annas by inheritance. The alleged cause of action for filing the suit is false and fabricated. The defendant No. 1 did not utter a single word regarding transfer of the property on 18.04.2004 as stated in the plaint. The plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit property and has not yet inherited the property in any way and as such, the suit is not maintainable as the plaintiff has no prima facie case and balance of convenience and inconvenience in their favour.

4. The trial court framed four issues for determination of the dispute between the parties. In course of hearing, the plaintiff examined two witnesses as P.Ws. and the defendant No. 1 examined two witnesses as D.Ws. Both the parties submitted some documents in support of their respective claim which were duly marked as exhibits. The trial court upon hearing dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 25.05.2007.

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court, the petitioner preferred Title Appeal No. 76 of 2007 in the court of District Judge, Rajbari. Eventually, the said appeal was heard by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Rajbari, on transfer who upon hearing disallowed the appeal by the impugned judgment and decree dated 08.09.2009. At this juncture, the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

6. Mr. Goutam Kumar Roy, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner at the very outset submits that a widow may transfer the property left by her husband as limited owner for legal necessity only. In the instant case the defendant No. 1 enjoying the property left by her husband Sridas Pramanik and has been maintaining her life well from the income of the property. Income from the property being surplus to her maintenance she purchased some property from other co-sharers with the income of the property. Therefore, there is no question of legal necessity of the defendant No. 1 calling transfer of property left by her husband. In the absence of any legal necessity of a widow she cannot transfer the property to anybody in which she has only limited interest, affecting the interest of the reversionary.

7. He further submits that the defendant No. 1 earlier transferred some property to other persons without any legal necessity and now taking step being ill advised by her paternal relatives to dispose of the remaining property with a malafide intention to deprive the plaintiff from inheriting the property as reversionary. It is also submitted that from the income of the property defendant No. 1 acquired some property in her own name. As such, from the facts and circumstances of the case it is apparently clear that the defendant has no legal necessity to transfer the property. To prevent multiplicity of judicial proceeding and to protect the property from wishful alienation by defendant No. 1 the plaintiff filed the suit for injunction for restraining her from transferring the property by any means to any person detrimental to the interest of the plaintiff, but both the courts below dismissed the suit as well as the appeal observing that the plaintiff has no prima facie case, no possession in the suit property and balance of conveniences are not in their favour. It is also argued that both the courts below failed to consider the case of the plaintiff and also failed to observe that in the event of transfer of the property by the defendant No. 1 without any legal necessity, the prospective right, title and interest of the plaintiffs will be in jeopardy and there will be multiplicity of judicial proceedings. He further submits that the contention of defendant No. 1 that she wants to build a moth for her husband and her father-in-law are all false and fabricated and in the concern locality there are no moth exists for any deceased. As such, only to substantiate her claim she has taken the stand that she will transfer the property for the purpose of building moth of her husband and father- in-law.

8. Mr. Roy further submits that earlier, the defendant No. 1 also transferred some property, but from the sale proceeds she did not do anything as alleged but she used the money for other purposes not for legal necessity. As such, the trial court ought to have decreed the suit restraining the defendant No. 1 from transferring the property to the detriment of the plaintiffs.

9. No one appears for the opposite party in the Rule.

10. Heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner, have gone through the revisional application, plaint and written statement, evidences both oral and documentary available in the lower court records and the impugned judgment and decree of both the courts below.

11. Admittedly, the defendant No. 1 is a widow of late Sridas Pramanik and there is no dispute that the schedule property belonged to Sridas Pramanik who died leaving defendant No. 1 to inherit him for limited period. As per, provision of Hindu Law, a widow can transfer the property inherited from her husband as life interest for her legal necessity. Legal necessity is a relative word having wide meaning, but in the instant case we need not discuss about legal necessity of defendant No. 1 as no transfer of the suit property has yet been made by defendant No. 1. The question of legal necessity may come and be decided if a widow transfer her life interest to any person and in that case the court can decide whether the transfer made by a widow was for any legal necessity and in the absence of legal necessity the transfer made by widow can be declared void.

12. It has been settled by the apex court that, to get a decree of permanent injunction the plaintiff is to prove, apparently, a good prima facie case in their favour. Likely, apparent title over the property and possession of the same and they have been threatened by defendant with dispossession or by any other means. In the instant suit, the cause of action is only limited to the fact that the defendant No. 1 took step for transferring the suit property on the ill advise of her relatives from paternal side. No tangible evidences has come before the court by any way to show or believe that on the date mentioned in the plaint, the defendant No. 1 took any visible step to transfer the property to any person having no legal necessity at all.

<u>13. Nowhere in the plaint as well as in the evidence adduced by the plaintiff before the trial court they disclosed name of any person to whom the property is going to be sold. There is also no allegation against defendant No. 1 that the suit property is under damage and waste and unless the defendant is prevented by a decree of injunction, the value of the property or quality of any goods will be diminished and the property in question will be damaged. The only allegations that the defendant No. 1 trying to dispose of the suit property to the detriment of the plaintiff's interest who will get the property on the death of the defendant No. 1 as reversionary. The anticipated right and interest to the property cannot come within the definition of prima facie case as the plaintiffs may die before the defendant and in the event of such incidence how the plaintiff can claim their anticipated right to be acquired in future. Law does not permit any person to seek any relief against any person anticipating future right. Moreover, the plaintiff stands in chance of succession ("Spes Succession's") during life time of the defendant, widow to be owners in future.</u>

<u>14. Learned Advocate for the petitioners referring to a case of Sharashibala Sarkar and others vs. Patani Sundari Dassaya and another reported in 6 BLT (AD) 131 tried to impress upon the court that in that case it was observed by the apex court that the reversionary heirs after the death of widow for the protection of the property can pursue legal remedies if occasion arises for damage, waste or alienation in any manner.</u>

<u>15. I have gone through the decision referred to, by the petitioners. In the said case widow Patani Sundari Dassaya transferred the property on the ground of legal necessity and the said deed dated 10.10.1984 was challenged by the plaintiff. The said suit was decreed. On appeal, the judgment of the trial court was affirmed with the modification that in view of provision of section 205 of Hindu Law, alienation of the suit land to the transferee Shibonath is valid during the life time of the transferor Patani Sundari Dassaya and the same will not be binding upon the plaintiff after her death and the apex court also decided that the transfer was valid. In the present case also the plaintiffs have opportunity to challenge the transfer to be made by widow without any legal necessity. But at this stage anticipating their future right in the property and in the absence of any tangible action on the part of the defendant No. 1 no decree of permanent injunction can be entertained under any provision of law. It is true that reversionary can initiate legal proceedings against the widow if the property in question is under danger being damaged and wasted. But in the present suit there is no such allegation, but only allegation that the defendant No. 1 may transfer the property to any person without any legal necessity to the detriment of the plaintiffs. For such uncertain allegation a person who is in enjoyment of the property and who may have a legal necessity in future cannot be restrained permanently by a decree of permanent injunction. As such, both the courts below rightly dismissed the suit as well as the appeal.</u>

<u>16. It is of this Court's view that if there be any transfer made by defendant No. 1 without legal necessity, the plaintiff have scope to challenge the transfer before the court of law, if there be any and in that suit the plaintiff can pray for order of injunction, restraining further transfer by the defendant No. 1 till disposal of that suit and in the event of decreeing the suit and declaring the transfer void or illegal then the widow can be restrained by a decree of permanent injunction not to make any further transfer of the property to any person without legal necessity. But an independent suit merely on speculation, praying for a decree of permanent injunction, like the present one, is not at all maintainable in view of the observations made hereinabove.</u>

17. Moreover, right of transfer is a legal right given by law to a widow for her legal necessity, that legal right under law cannot be infringed or restrained by a decree of permanent injunction.

18. Taking into consideration the above, this Court finds no merit in this Rule.

19. In the result, the Rule is discharged, however, without any order as to costs.

20. Communicate a copy of this judgment to the court concerned and send down the lower court record at once.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1221 of 2018
lawyer:
Mr. A.M. Aminuddin, Senior Advocate, instructed by Ms. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ------------ For the Petitioner 
Mr. Md. Harunur Rashid, Advocate instructed by Mr. Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-On-Record. ------- For Respondents
parties:
Md. Mitul Mollah son of late Pachu Mollah, of Village-Tangrakhola, PO and PS-Muksudpur, District-Gopalgonj. ------ Petitioner.
-Vs-
Abul Khayer Mollah and others ------- Respondents.
case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated 15.12.2016, passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 364 of 2013)
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 15.12.2016, passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 364 of 2013 heard along with connected Rule No. 840(F) of 2013 allowing the appeal and disposing of the connected Rule and there-by setting aside the judgment and decree dated 14.08.2013, passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Gopalgonj, in Title Suit No. 2 of 2005 by which the High Court Division decreed the suit subject to the conditions that the plaintiffs shall pay TK.22,86,666/- to the respondent No.3 within 30(thirty) days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment and decree failing which the appeal shall stand dismissed.

2. Facts leading to filing of this civil petition for leave to appeal, in brief, are that:

<u>3. The predecessors of present respondent Nos. 1(ka) to 1(ta) and respondent Nos. 2 to 3, as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 02 of 2005 in the 2nd Court of learned Joint District Judge, Gopalganj, for declaration that the auction sale of the suit land described in schedule-Ka to the plaint, through advertisement, in favour of the so called defendant No.3, is illegal, malafide, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs. It is stated that the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 got the suit land, described in Schedule-Ka to the plaint, by purchase and also by inheritance and had been possessing the same by constructing two storied building therein. That Md. Hasan Ali, son of the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 is carrying on his proprietorship business under the name and style "Habib Enterprise" (plaintiff No.3) in the ground floor of the said building. For the purpose of the said business Hasan Ali initially took loan from the defendant No.1- bank twice and after repayment of the same, he on 19.01.2001, again he took loan of TK. 8,00,000/- (Eight lac) from the defendant Bank upon mortgaging the 'Ka' schedule property of plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 as security to the defendant-bank wherein plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 stood as guarantor by putting their signatures in the guarantee forms.. It is stated that the plaintiffs in 2001, 2002 and 2003 paid off the entire interest accrued on the said loan and was ready to pay off the entire amount of loan money. But the defendant-bank being influenced by defendant No.3, a locally influential and greedy person, and in connivance with each other to grab the said property, refused to receive the due payment of loan from the plaintiff No.3. Accordingly, the defendant bank without informing anything to the plaintiffs, published tender notice in the "Daily Bhorer Kagoj" on 21.05.2005 under section 12 of the Artharin Adalat Ain, 2003 for selling the mortgaged properties in auction fixing 04.06.2005 as the date of auction. On 2.7.2005, the plaintiffs came to know about the said auction and also came to know that though in the tender notice last date of depositing 25% of the bid money by the intended participants was fixed on 3.6.2005 but the defendant No.3 deposited the same on 4.6.2005 quoting TK.12,50,000/= as the bid money in violation of the terms and condition of the tender notice. However, the defendant No.3's bid was accepted as the highest. Since the auction was held in violation of sections 12,33 and 48 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, the plaintiffs were compelled to institute the instant suit.</u>

4. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statements, denying all material allegations made in the plaint, contending, inter alia that the auction was held in compliance with the provisions of law. The defendant No.3's bid having been found to be the highest the same was accepted and the mortgaged property was legally sold to him in auction.

5. The trial Court after hearing the parties dismissed the suit by judgment and decree dated 21.08.2013 against which the plaintiff-respondents preferred First Appeal No. 364 of 2013 before the High Court Division, which was ultimately allowed upon setting aside the judgment and decree dated 21.08.2013 passed by the trial Court and thereby the suit was decreed on condition as stated hereinabove, by the impugned judgment and order dated 15.12.2016. Hence, the defendant No.3, the auction purchaser, filed this civil petition for leave to appeal before this Division for redress.

6. Mr A.M. Aminuddin, the learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the defendant No.3 petitioner submits that Section 12(VIII) of the Artharin Adalat Ain, 2003 contemplates that the suit property being mortgaged to the bank and the bank having sold the same in auction in accordance with law such sale has constituted legal title in favour of the purchaser which cannot be put to any controversy under any circumstances and under the proviso to that section the debtor executing the bond (i.e. the mortgagor) can claim compensation against the bank only if any illegality or procedural irregularity in the sale process is done by the financial institution then the debtor executing bond will be entitled to claim compensation against the financial institution. In this respect he relied on the case of Banesa Bibi Vs. Senior Vice President and others, (63 DLR(AD) 160). Thus he submits that challenging the auction sale of the mortgaged property in suit is not maintainable in view of the aforesaid provision of law. He next submits that the plaintiffs cheated the bank as well as the auction purchaser as the plaintiff No.1 transferred the properties to different persons knowing fully well that certain portion of the same is mortgaged to the defendant bank against loan thus they are not entitled to get any relief. He submits that although elaborate description was given by filing supplementary affidavit but the High Court Division, did not consider the same and as such the judgment and order impugned herein is required to be interfered with.

7. Mr. Md. Harunur Rashid, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondents submits that the defendant respondent bank published the auction notice under section 12 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in the newspaper on 20.5.2005 fixing 04.06.2005 as the date for holding auction giving 15(fifteen) days time out of which 4 days were government holidays. But section 48 of the said Ain provides that for the purpose of limitation only the working days are to be counted and as such, the bank violated the law in publishing the auction notice which the trial court failed to consider and most erroneously held that the bank followed the provisions of law in publishing the auction notice. The High Court Division on the other hand rightly decided the issue and decreed the suit. Thus, the impugned Judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division does not call for interference. He next submits that defendant No.3 in collusion with defendant No. 1, bank managed to submit 04(four) quotations showing one of them to be the highest bidder who purchased the mortgaged property at a shockingly low price keeping the plaintiffs in dark. Referring to the evidence of DW.2, former Manager of the bank, learned Advocate for the respondent submits that DW.2 in his cross Examination, admitted that the auction notice was published only giving only 12 days time which is completely violative of the provisions of the said Ain. Referring to the decisions in the case of Abdul Jalil Vs. Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation and another reported in 41 DLR(AD)109 and in the case of Md. Moklesur Rahman and another Vs. Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 23 BLT(AD)210, the learned Advocate for the respondent prays for dis-missing the civil petition.

8. On hearing the learned Advocates for both the sides, it appears that the present petitioner (the auction purchaser) relying on the proviso to section 12(8) of the Ain, 2003 raised the legal question of maintainability of the suit. Whereas the owner of the property (judgment debtor) respondents herein raised the question of irregularity in publishing the auction notice and thereby provided insufficient time which is vilative of sections 33(1) and 48 of the said Ain. They also raised the question of collusion between the bank and the auction purchaser meaning there was illegality, irregularity and collusion in holding the auction sale. Maintainability of a suit is a question which hits the 2007 of the suit. Unless the suit is not maintainable noting can be looked into or determined. In this respect, it is required to see section 12(8) of the Ain, 2003 which deals with auction sale by the financial institution, having power of attorney to sell a property under mortgage. The said provision provides as under:

“১২। (১)………………

(২) ………………

(৩) ………………

(৪) ………………

(৫) ………………

(৫ক) ………………

(৬) ………………

(৭) ………………

(৮)আপাততঃ বলবৎ অন্য কোন আইনে ভিন্নরুপ যাহা কিছুই খাকুক না কেন এই ধারায় অধীন প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক lien, pledge, lypothecation অথবা Mortgage এর অধীন প্রাপ্ত মতাবলে কোন জামানতী স্থাবর বা অস্থাবর সম্পত্তি বিক্রয় করা হইলে, উক্ত বিক্রয় ক্রেতার অনুকূলে বৈধ স্বত্ব সৃষ্টি করিবে এবং ক্রেতার ক্রয়কে কোনভাবেই তর্কিত করা যাইবে নাঃ

তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক বিক্রয় কার্যক্রমে কোনরুপ অবৈধতা বা পদ্ধতিতে অনিয়ম থাকিলে, জামানত প্রদানকারী ঋণ গ্রহীতা আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের বিরুদ্ধে ক্ষতিপূরণ দাবী করিতে পারিবেন।

9. On reading the aforesaid provision of law it is clear that the statute debarred challenging any auction sale held under section 12 of the Ain 2003 in any Court of law rather the proviso to that section, as quoted above, clearly shows that in respect of any illegality or procedural irregularity the mortgagor has the remedy against the financial institution to seek compensation only, nothing else. In the instant case, the facts show that the mortgagor (petitioners herein) specifically alleged illegality and procedural irregularity in publishing notice as well as holding the auction sale. So, the point raised squarely falls within the ambit of section 12(8) specifically the proviso to the said section. Since the mortgagee bank has sold the mortgaged property in auction under section 12 of the Ain 2003 the auction sale cannot be put into question so far section 12(8) of the Ain 2003 is concerned. Thus, the auction sale in question in protected under section 12(8) of the Ain and as such the High Court Division erred in law in allowing the appeal and thereby decreeing the suit.

10. At this stage, Mr. Harunur Rashid, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the mortgagor respondent submits that he has received instruction from his client to negotiate with the bank as well as with the auction purchaser to settle the matter out of Court and thereby retain the ancestral property of the mortgagor and accordingly prayed for doing complete justice by exercising this Division's power under article 104 of the Constitution. Upon taking instruction from his client Mr. Rashid submits that the High Court Division allowed the appeal and decreed the suit on condition to pay TK.22,86,666/= to the auction purchaser (petitioner herein) with-in 30 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment and as such the present respondent is ready to pay the said amount.

11. On the other hand Mr. Aminuddin, the learned Advocate for the auction purchaser-petitioner submits that the auction purchaser deposited the entire bid money and obtained boinama from the court on 29.06.2006 and by now the said money deposited with the bank remained unutilized for more than 14 years. The present respondent even did not comply with the order of the High Court Division dated 15.12.2006. So, Mr. Aminuddin submits that if complete justice is to be done then it should also be done in favour of the present petitioner.

<u>12. Considering all these aspects, since admittedly the mortgagor respondent, is still in possession of the auction sold property and since for more than 14 years the petitioner is deprived of enjoying the property after depositing the entire bid money in Court immediately after the auction sale and got the registered sale deed in his favour and since the mortgagor respondents are in possession of their ancestral property and they want to retain the same we feel it reasonable to direct the mortgagor respondent-deposit TK.40,00,000/=(Taka forty lacs) as solatium to the auction purchaser petitioner within 45 days and file compliance thereof and thereby settle the matter once for all. However, on payment of the said solatium amount of TK. 40,00,000/- by the mortgagor respondent to the auction purchaser petitioner the bank will release the property from mortgage and handover the title documents to the mortgagor and as such the auction purchaser shall have no right, title and interest on the suit property pursuant to auction sale. In case any deed of transfer is registered in favour of the auction purchaser the same will stand redundant.</u>

<u>13. The bank as well as the auction purchaser are directed to handover the title deed of the mortgaged property to the mortgagor-respondent on payment of the aforesaid amount of TK.40,00,000/- (Taka forty lacs).</u>

<u>14. With the aforesaid observation and direction this civil petition is disposed of without any order as to costs.</u>

End.
