full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim, J : Defendant as appellant preferred the present appeal against the Judgment and Final decree dated 19-2-2012 (decree signed on 22-3-2016) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Third Court, Chittagong in Other Suit No. 241 of 2005 decreeing the suit on the basis of the Advocate Commissioner report dated 22-6-2009. 

2. The respondent Nos. 1-4 as defendant Nos. 1-4 instituted Other Suit No. 241 of 2005 in the Third Court of Joint. District Judge, Chittagong on 24-7-2005 for partition impleading the appellant as sole defendant. In the suit the plaintiffs claimed saham of 11 gondas, 3 karas excluding 10 gondas transferred in favour of the defendant out of the suit lands. 

3. The facts relevant for determining this appeal may be summarized as follows: The plaintiffs purchased 21 gondas, 3 karas of land by 12 registered deeds from the BS recorded owners, Mohram Ali, Nowhser Ali and Fayez Ahmed and others. While they were holding and possession of the suit lands by mutating their name in BS khatian, the plaintiffs by registered kabala dated 10-2-2003 transferred 10 gondas of land towards the northern side with a specific boundary in favour of the defendant and the remaining 11 gondas, 3 karas lands remained in their possession. The plaintiff No. 1 subsequently transferred 2 gondas, 1 kara lands in favour of the plaintiff Nos. 3 and 4 by different deeds, they are in ejmali possession of their respective lands. The defendant has been possessing beyond 10 gondas of land by force and since there has been quarrel between the parties over the boundary, the plaintiffs are constrained to institute the suit for partition of the lands by metes and bounds. 

4. The sole defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint stating, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and is barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, Order VII, rule 11 and Order II, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The case of the defendant is that the plaintiffs were the owner of the suit land by way of purchase and while was in possession of the land, transferred 10(ten) gondas of land to the defendant by registered kabala dated 10-2-2005, but it claims that it does not possess beyond 10 gondas land. The defendant after purchase mutated his name in BS khatian and started construction of multi-storied building with the approved plan of CDA, upon taking loan from bank and entered into contract with various persons for sale of apartment from the said 14-storied building. The plaintiffs had no right, title, interest on the said land while purchased by the defendant and as the plaintiffs are not the co-sharers of the said jote the suit for partition is not maintainable and, as such, prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

5. After conclusion of the trial, learned Joint District Judge, Third Court, Chittagong decreed the suit in preliminary form by judgment and decree dated 25-9-2006 to the effect that except 0.20 sataks of land from the Northern side of RS plot No. 639, RS khatian No. 11 corresponding to BS khatian No. 907, BS plot Nos. 1170, 1171, 1172 and 1173 which was sold by the plaintiffs to the defendant, the plaintiffs are entitled to get the rest land. The trial court further directed that—
“অত্র রায় প্রকাশের পরবর্তী চল্লিশ দিনের মধ্যে বিবাদীর বাউন্ডারী ওয়াল দ্বারা চিহ্নিত, মতে দখলকৃত অংশ ব্যতীত বাদবাকী সম্পত্তি দাগের দক্ষিনাংশে আপোষে বাদি বিবাদী উভয় পক্ষকে বুঝাইয়া দেওয়ার ও বুঝিয়া নেওয়ার বিষয়ে উভয় পক্ষকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হইল।” The preliminary decree was drawn up accordingly. 

6. The plaintiffs being aggrieved by and dissatisfied 'with the judgment and preliminary decree dated 25-9-2006 preferred First Appeal No. 124 of 2007 before this court, At the: time of hearing of the appeal learned Advocate for both the parties agreed that appeal may be disposed of after deleting the following paragraph from the operating portion of the judgment viz: “অত্র রায় প্রকাশের পরবর্তী চল্লিশ দিনের মধ্যে বিবাদীর বাউন্ডারী ওয়াল দ্বারা চিহ্নিত, মতে দখলকৃত অংশ ব্যতীত বাদবাকী সম্পত্তি দাগের দক্ষিনাংশে আপোষে বাদি বিবাদী উভয় পক্ষকে বুঝাইয়া দেওয়ার ও বুঝিয়া নেওয়ার বিষয়ে উভয় পক্ষকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হইল ।”Accordingly, disposed of the appeal by judgment dated 27-2-2008 deleting the aforesaid observations from the judgment and also directed to make amicable partition their respective lands within 30 days from the date of receipt of the records in accordance with the judgment, failing which the plaintiffs will be entitled to get their saham allotted by appointing of an Advocate Commissioner in accordance with the judgment of the trial court. 

7. That after disposal of the appeal, the plaintiffs applied for appointment of an Advocate Commission which was allowed. Mr Abdul Gani, learned Advocate was appointed as an Advocate Commissioner, who after survey, submitted his report on 22-6-2009 along with a hand sketch-map. Against the report of the Advocate Commissioner, defendant filed objection on 30-9-2009, after hearing the parties the trial court by order No. 107 dated 19-2-2012 accepted the report of the Advocate Commissioner and made the decree final treating the report as part of the decree.

8. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order dated 19-2-2012, the defendant as petitioner filed a revisional application before the High Court Division challenging the acceptance of the report of the advocate commissioner and obtained Rule and Stay in Civil Revision No. 753 of 2012. After hearing the parties, the Rule was discharged as not maintainable by the judgment and order dated 16-5-2013 with the finding that filing of civil revision after drawing final decree upon accepting the report of the commissioner or preferring an appeal before preparing and signing of final decree is not maintainable but there is no bar to prefer appeal after signing of final decree. 

9. After drawing and signing the final decree on 22-3-2016 and 28-3-2016 respectively, the defendant has now preferred the present appeal on 18-5-2016 impugning the judgment and final decree dated 19-2-2012 signed on 22-3-2016. 

10. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, learned Senior Advocate appeared with Mr Mohammad Ziaul Haque, Advocate on behalf of the defendant-appellant. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, firstly submits that the court below failed to take notice that Advocate Commissioner did not prepare his report as per observation and direction of the trial court. 

11. He further submits that the Advocate Commissioner has not determined the actual boundary between RS plot No. 10 and 11 and ought to have given to the defendant purchased land 10 gondas equivalent to 0.20 sataks from southern side of boundary but the Advocate Commissioner without fixing the boundary allotted land to the plaintiffs on mere assumption which would found from the field Book. The trial court completely overlooked the aforesaid vital point and illegally accepted the commissioner's report and drawn up the final decree. 

12. He next submits that the learned Advocate Commissioner failed to comply with the preliminary decree without measuring the portion of roads and allotted saham to the plaintiffs for 11 gondas without deducting the land encroached by the road and without satisfying the defendant's share acquired by purchase from the plaintiffs and accepted the report and made the decree final thereby committed error of law. 

13. He also submits that the learned Joint District Judge accepted the report of the Advocate Commissioner and passed the final decree without considering the written objection filed by the defendant against the commissioner's report and evidence of Advocate Commissioner and, as such, the impugned final decree is liable to be set-aside. In support of his submissions, learned Advocate for the appellant cited the decisions reported in AIR 1990 (Orissa) 32, 4 BLC 460, 3 CLR (AD) 209, 19 BLT (HC) 14 and 11 BLT (HC) 508. 

14. On the other hand, Mr Mustafa Niaz Muhammad, learned Advocate for the plaintiffs-respondents submits that the learned Advocate Commissioner followed the direction and observation made in the judgment and preliminary decree and submitted his report on 22-6-2009. He has further contended that if there is minor discrepancy in the report of Advocate Commissioner, for that the report should not be rejected and furthermore there was a bar to measure RS plot No. 10, admittedly which is not suit plot. He has also contended that the suit land was measured as per RS Survey and to ascertain the suit land learned Advocate Commissioner fixed RS plot No. 84 as fixed point in presence of the learned Advocate of the parties, their representatives and survey personnels and the said report was proved by him as CW 1. He has finally submitted that learned Joint District Judge after considering and appreciating the written objection and evidence of the learned Advocate Commissioner rightly accepted the report and thus committed no illegality in passing the final decree. Mr Mustafa Niaz Muhammad, learned Advocate for the respondents referred a decision reported in 58 DLR 81.

15. That moot question law to be determined in this appeal whether filing of the present appeal by the defendants without filing any appeal against the preliminary decree is maintainable. 

16. Before we enter into the merit of appeal, first of all we are to determine the preliminary point namely, as to the maintainability of the appeal. 

17. There is no dispute that the plaintiffs are the owners of the suit land by way of purchase and out of the suit land plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 have sold away 10 (ten) gondas of land to the defendant. In view of the above admitted case of the parties, the trial court decreed the suit in preliminary form as prayed for. 

18. It appears that the trial court decreed the Other Suit No. 241 of 2005 in preliminary form by judgment and decree dated on 25-9-2006. Against the said judgment and preliminary decree, the plaintiffs preferred First Appeal No. 124 of 2007 and appeal was disposed of by the judgment dated 27-2-2008 maintaining the decree of the trial court with some modification in the operative portion of trial court's judgment. A preliminary decree passed in a partition suit is not a tentative decree it is a conclusive decree until it is reversed by the higher courts. 

19. That after disposal of the First Appeal No. 124 of 2007, Advocate Commissioner was appointed, who filed his report dated 22-6-2009 against which defendant filed written objection on 30-9-2009. Thereafter, the trial court by order No. 107 dated 19-2-2012 accepted the report and made the preliminary decree final and report of the commissioner was made as part of the final decree. The defendant filed Civil Revision No. 753 of 2012 against the order dated 19-2-2012 and rule was discharged by judgment and order dated 16-5-2013. The defendant being aggrieved with the aforesaid judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, filed Civil Petitioner for Leave to Appeal No. 1992 of 2013, same was also dismissed by the Appellate Division by judgment and order dated 3-11-2013. 

20. After disposal of the Civil Revision on 16-5-2013, the plaintiffs filed an application on 29-9-2013 in the trial court for drawing up final decree as per report of the Advocate Commissioner, to which the defendant filed written objection on 31-3-2014. The defendant also filed an application for separate saham on 31-3-2014, against the said application plaintiffs filed written objection on 24-4-2014 and additional objection on 10-9-2014 stating that during pendency of the suit, defendant out of his purchased 10 gondas land sold away 0.0284 acre land to Chattogram Development Authority (CDA) by registered kabala No. 18769 dated 8-11-2012 for extension of Hathazi Road out of BS plot Nos. 1170 and 1171. As such, after sale the defendant is now owner of 0.899 gondas land only but the defendant completely concealing this fact, prayed for saham for 10 gondas. On the other hand, plaintiff also transferred 0.195 decimal to CDA out of their 11 gondas saham by registered kabala No. 21863 dated 29-12-2011 from BS plot No. 1170 for extension of Hathazi Road. 

21. It further appears that the learned Advocate Commissioner in his report mentioned that the defendant made construction on 10 gondas land of the plaintiffs beyond its purchased land. That the defendant is a developer company and since it was preparing to sell and handover flats constructed on the portion of the plaintiffs land to different purchasers, the plaintiffs on 5-7-2009 prayed for temporary injunction and also ad-interim injunction before the trial court but since the court fixed a date for hearing those applications without granting ad-interim injunction which in effect, was rejection of the prayer of ad-interim injunction, the plaintiffs filed FMA No. 223 of 2019 before the High Court Division and obtained an order of status-quo. The High Court Division ultimately dismissed the appeal and vacated the order of status-quo by judgment and order dated 4-3-2010. Against the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the plaintiffs-appellants filed CMP No. 181 of 2010 and obtained an order of status-quo for a period of I (one) week on 14-3-2010 with direction to file regular leave petition and the plaintiffs filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 524 of 2010 within time and also filed an application for extension of the order of status-quo. During pendency of the said leave petition and while the status-quo order passed by the Appellate Division in force in respect of transfer and/or handing over the flats, the defendant showing utter disregard to the order of status-quo passed by the Appellate Division on 14-3-2010, sold out flats to different persons and handed over possession of those flats to those purchasers in gross violation of the order of Appellate Division. Accordingly, the plaintiffs filed Contempt Petition No. 6 of 2013 before the Appellate Division and after hearing their lordships of the Appellate Division by judgment dated 26-5-2014 found that the defendant-contemnor has not denial having transferred the 29 fiats after the order of status-quo dated 14-3-2010 as alleged by the plaintiffs. Thus it appears that defendant-contemnor has transferred as many as 29 flats constructed on the land in question in gross violation of the order of this court dated 14-3-2010. By this act violation of this courts order the contemnor-defendant has committed contempt of court. Therefore, their lordships, found that the contemnor-defendant Mahfuzul Huq, Director Equity Property Management (Pvt) Ltd. guilty of contempt of this court and sentence him to suffer simple imprisonment for 1(one) Month. 

22. It further appears that the plaintiff filed an application on 30-9-2013 for preparing final decree and on same date the defendant filed an application for separate saham and also filed written objection on 31-3-2014 against drawing of final decree and both the application was fixed for hearing. The plaintiffs filed written objection on 24-4-2014 against the defendant's application for saham dated 31-3-2014 and further filed additional written objection on 10-9-2014. On perusal of order-sheet it appears that last chance were given for hearing both the application on 10-9-2014. The defendant took so many adjournments and on 29-9-2014 defendant's application for saham was heard in part and next date was fixed on 5-1-2015 for further hearing, on that date after hearing, same was fixed for order on 21-1-2015. The defendant again filed an application for further hearing without serving any copy to plaintiff's learned Advocate annexing the copy, the learned Joint District Judge fixed 15-2-2015 for further hearing subject to serve the copy of the application -upon the plaintiffs but on that date hearing was adjourned and next date was fixed on 19-3-2015 for applications hearing. On 19-3-2015, on the prayer of the defendant the application dated 21-1-2015 was rejected as not pressed. Later on, the court entertained another application for further hearing, same was fixed on 9-4-2015 and 14-6-2015 for hearing without cancelling the order dated 19-3-2015. 

23. Thereafter, the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No. 1748 of 2015 on 24-5-2015 impugning the Order No. 132 dated 19-3-2015 so far it relates to entertaining the application of the defendant for further hearing of the application of the plaintiffs to make/prepare the final decree and the defendants application for saham and Order No. 133 dated 09-4-2015 fixing 14-6-2015 for applications hearing without passing order as per Order No. 130 dated 27-1-2015 passed by the Joint District Judge, Third Court, Chittagong in Other Suit No. 241 of 2005. Rule was issued on 14-6-2015 and pending hearing of the rule further proceedings of Other Suit No. 241 of 2005 was stayed. Subsequently, rule was disposed of by judgment and order dated 15-11-2015. In the judgment it was observed that—From 27-1-2015 to 19-3-2015 it will appear that the application was made for saham. On query to the learned Advocate whether the final decree has been passed on 19-2-2012 then why those applications in that context. They submits that if the saham is being given as per final decree in that case they have no objection. Therefore, we now direct the Court below to follow the procedure in distributing saham in accordance with the final decree within 7 days from the date of receipt of this order.

24. That on close scrutiny of the judgment dated 15-11-2015 passed in Civil Revision No. 1748 of 2015, it appears that rule was disposed of directing the court below to follow the procedure in distributing saham as per final decree dated 19-2-2012 within 7 days from the date of receipt of the order. Later on, final decree was prepared on 22-3-2016 and signed by the learned Joint District Judge on 28-3-2016. 

25. To appreciate the point involved, we have perused the entire records. As stated above the suit was decreed in the preliminary form on 25-9-2006 against the sole defendant decreeing the rest of land of RS plot No. 639, RS khatian No. 11 corresponding to BS khatian No. 907, BS plot Nos. 1170/1171/1172 and 1173 excepting 0.2000 sataks of land from the Northern side, which was sold by the plaintiffs to the defendant. The trial court further directed that: 
“অত্র রায় প্রকাশের পরবর্তী চল্লিশ দিনের মধ্যে বিবাদীর বাউন্ডারী ওয়াল দ্বারা চিহি্ত, মতে দখলকৃত অংশ ব্যতীত বাদবাকী সম্পত্তি দাগের দক্ষিনাংশে আপোষে বাদি বিবাদী উভয় পক্ষকে বুঝাইয়া দেওয়ার ও বুঝিয়া নেওয়ার বিষয়ে উভয় পক্ষকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হইল ।” 

26. The plaintiffs being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and preliminary decree dated 25-9-2006, preferred First Appeal No. 124 of 2007. At the time of hearing of the appeal learned Advocate for both the parties agreed that appeal may be disposed of after deleting the following paragraph from the operating portion of the judgment viz: “অত্র রায় প্রকাশের পরবর্তী চল্লিশ দিনের মধ্যে বিবাদীর বাউন্ডারী ওয়াল ছারা চিহিত, মতে দখলকৃত অংশ ব্যতীত বাদবাকী সম্পত্তি দাগের দক্ষিনাংশে আপোষে বাদি বিবাদী উ���য় পক্ষকে বুঝাইয়া দেওয়ার ও বুঝিয়া নেওয়ার বিষয়ে উভয় পক্ষকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হইল ।”Accordingly, disposed of the appeal by judgment dated 23-2-2008 after deleting the aforesaid observations from the judgment and also directed to make amicable partition their respective lands within 30 days. from the date of receipt of the records in accordance with the judgment, failing which the plaintiffs will be entitled to get their saham allotted by appointing an Advocate Commissioner in accordance with the judgment of the trial court. 

27. After disposal of the First Appeal No. 124 of 2007, Advocate Commissioner was appointed on 3-6-2008 to affect partition. Learned Advocate Commissioner went to the suit land on several dates for holding commission after due service of notice upon the learned Advocate of the parties, then he submitted his report dated 22-6-2009 (Exhibit- 11 series). in the report it is stated that after ascertaining the suit properties he measured the suit properties. On the proposal of the representatives present, RS plot No. 84 (Road) was referred to be as fixed point and carried out the measurement commencing it from the fixed point and reach the suit RS plot No. 11. After holding commission allotted saham of 9 gondas 2 kranti — 0.1834 sataks to the plaintiffs. (shown in Yellow colour) and 10 gondas = 0.2000 sataks to the defendant (shown in Pink colour) and also give 1 ganads = 0.0298 sataks of land which was encroached by the defendants (shown in Green colour) which was found in possession of the defendant in excess of its purchased 10 gondas land from the plaintiff. The defendant opposed the report of Advocate Commissioner by filing written objection on 31-3-2014. The court examined the commissioner as CW 1 and he was cross-examined by the defendant. In cross-examination, the commissioner denied the suggestion that he did not conduct the commission as per direction of Hon'ble High Court. As per preliminary decree, the plaintiffs were given saham of rest of the land excepting 10 gondas land sold by the plaintiffs to the defendant. In the preliminary decree there is no mention of specific saham of the plaintiffs. 

28. It appears that the learned Advocate Commissioner after ascertaining the fixed point and clearly mentioned RS plot No. 84 as fixed point, which tallied with RS sheet. To ascertain correct measurement, Commissioner also measured the adjacent other RS plot as per RS sheet. In the suit plaintiffs claimed partition of 11 gondas i.e. 0.2200 sataks out of total 21 gondas = 0.4200 sataks out of suit RS plot No. 11, plaintiffs sold 10 gondas i.e. 0.2000 sataks to the defendant from the northern side of suit RS plot No. 11. After physical measurement, in the southern part of suit RS plot No. 11 there was path way measuring North-South 8' x East-West 127' = 00.50 satak of the suit RS plot 11.
 
29. As per preliminary decree plaintiff is entitled to get decree the balance area of land excluding land of 10 gondas situated in northern side of suit RS plot No. 11, which was sold to defendant. Since the plaintiff sold 10 gondas of suit RS plot No. 11 out of total area of 21 gondas i.e. 0.4200 sataks. So, plaintiffs are entitled to get a decree rest 11 gondas of suit land. During physical measurement of the suit plot, learned Advocate Commissioner found there is existing road in southern side of suit RS plot No. 11 North — South 8', East — West 127' measuring an area of 0.0050 satak land. As such plaintiff's are now in possession of 9 gondas, 2 kranti equivalent to 0.1834 sataks out of 11 gondas = 0.2200 sataks which was allotted to the plaintiffs. It was also found that the defendant are physically possessing 0.2300 sataks out of its purchased 10 gondas i.e. 0.2000 sataks and they were constructing Multi-Storied Building on 11½ gondas i.e. in excess of 1½ gondas = 0.0298 sataks of land. In fact defendant is entitled to get its 10 gondas = 0.2000 sataks purchased land and excess 1½ gondas is not owned by the defendant. Defendant is constructing building by encroaching 1½ gondas lands of the plaintiffs, which is specifically shown in "Green Colour" in the case Map of the Advocate Commissioner's report. 

30. The plaintiff's are in possession of 9 gondas, 2 kranti land = 0.1834 sataks, which is shown in yellow colour and defendants purchased 10 gondas land was shown in Pink colour respectively. The land measuring 1½ gondas encroached by the defendant are specifically shown in "Green colour" in the case Map submitted by the Advocate Commissioner with the report. 

31. It is pertinent to note, in the purchase deed of defendant dated 10-2-2005, Northern boundary of RS plot No. 11 was mentioned East — West 127'40" and North — South I6'-6" but physically Northern Boundary area was found East — West 130'-0" —North — South 20'-0" i.e. = 2,600 square feet and 127' x 16' = 2,037 square feet. 

32. A reference to the report of the Commissioner shows that after identified the properties, fixed point was set up in presence of the learned Advocates and the officer and karjakarak of the defendant's company and took measurement of the suit properties with reference to fixed point, RS plot No. 84 available near the suit RS plot No. 11. The survey have been made by chain method. The measurement was carried out with reference to such fixed point set up by the commissioner and prepared case Map `Ica' and `Icha' as per RS sheet and details measurement was noted in the field Book. During commission, Advocate Commissioner recorded deposition of the plaintiff No. 1 and one Nurul Islam Khoka, representive and karjakarak of defendant in respect of identifying fixing the pillar point and measurement of the suit RS plot No. 11 and filed the same with the report annexing the Notices, Share Table, Field Book, Case Map (Exhibit-11 series). 

33. Learned Advocate for the appellant vehemently contended that the learned Joint District Judge without applying his judicial mind has drawn up the final decree on 22-3-2016 in pursuance of the Advocate Commissioner's report which has been submitted not in conformity with the preliminary decree. Learned Advocate Commissioner without determining the actual boundary between RS plot No. 10 and 11 illegally allotted land to the plaintiffs on mere assumption. 

34. Before we consider the Advocate Commissioner report, at first we have to examine the purchased Deed dated 10-2-2003 (Exhibit- 8) of the defendant, same was sold within specific boundary and the schedule of land was clearly specified in the deed by annexing hand map shown in yellow colour.
After taking delivery, the defendant has been in possession of its purchased land by errecting pucca boundary wall and mutating its name by filing Mutation Case No. 4-0254 of 2003. Accordingly, by order dated 28-3-2003 BS Mutation Khatian No. 907/1 of 2001 (Exhibit- kha) was prepared in its name. In the said BS Khatian, two BS plots i.e. BS plot No. 1170(p), 1171(p), their total share was recorded 0.2000 sataks out of total area of 0.3598 sataks. Although defendant purchased 10 gondas out of RS kbatian No. 639, plot No. 11 (southern side) corresponding to PS Khatian No. 365, PS plot Nos. 25/26/28, corresponding to BS Mutation Khatian No. 907, BS plot Nos. 1170(p), 1171(p), 1172(p) and 1173(p). Since the defendant had been in possession of specific 10 gondas = 0.2000 sataks out of its purchased land, but primarily did not pray for saham in the suit land, as such the plaintiffs are entitled to get saham in the suit by maintaining the boundary of Southern side of the suit plot RS plot No. 11. The Advocate Commissioner submitted his report in conformity with the preliminary decree in as much as, he performed the commission work after serving notice upon the learned Advocates of both the parties. He conducted survey, in presence of the learned Advocates and representatives of both the parties with the help of their surveyors. From the statements of the plaintiffs and the report of the commissioner, written objection of the defendant against the Advocate Commissioner report and the evidence on record, there is no doubt that the final decree has been drawn up in conformity with the preliminary decree. It is worthy to mentioned here that there was no necessity to determine the boundary between RS plot No. 10 and 11, since the land of RS plot No. 10 is no way connected in this suit. To ascertain the suit land, learned Advocate Commissioner fixed RS plot No. 84 as fixed point in presence of the learned Advocate and representatives of both the parties and after taking deposition of the plaintiff No. 1 and defendant's karjakarak and representative, Nurul Islam Khoka (Exhibit-11 series). 

35. In the present case, we have already seen, after preliminary decree, the plaintiffs filed First Appeal No. 124 of 2007 and same was disposed of by modification in the ordering portions of trial court judgment dated 23-2-2008. Thereafter, trial court by order dated 19-2-2012 rejected the objection and accepted the report and made the preliminary decree final and made the commissioner's report as part of the final decree. Against the order dated 19-2-2012, defendant filed Civil Revision No. 753 of 2012 and Rule was discharged by judgment and order dated 16-5-2013, which was also affirmed by the Appellate Division by judgment and order dated 3-11-2013. 

36. There is no dispute that in the present case as per preliminary decree dated 25-9-2009, the plaintiff got a saham of 0.22 sataks from the rest of the land except 0.20 sataks = 10 gondas from northern side of the schedule suit land, which was sold by the plaintiffs to the defendant. The preliminary decree has been affirmed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 124 of 2007 with modification. Since the dispute has finally been adjudicate upon by the highest court the same cannot be reopened again. Though a preliminary decree passed in a partition suit is not a tentative, it is conclusive until it is reversed by the higher courts. The court must carry out directions in preliminary decree and dispose of the suit completely particularly when such preliminary decree is affirmed by the apex court. In the instant case, the trial court after due consideration of the Advocate Commissioner report made the preliminary decree final on 19-2-2012. 

37. Order XX deals with the judgment and decree. Rule 6(1) of Order XX, the Code provides that—the decree shall agree with the judgment; it shall contain the number of the suit, the names and description of the parties, and particulars of the claim, and shall specify clearly the relief granted or other determination of the suit. Rule 7 of Order XX of the Code further provides that—the decree shall bear date the day on which the judgment was pronounced and when the judge has satisfied himself that the decree had been drawn up in accordance with the judgment he shall sign the decree. Rule 13 of Order XXVI of the Code speaks about the power of Court to issue a commission to such person to make the partition or separation according to the rights as declared in a preliminary decree. The provision of Rule 14 of the said order has provided the procedure in details as to how a commissioner who will be appointed to make partition as per preliminary decree will perform his duty, submit his report and how the objection if any, filed against the commissioner's report will be dealt with and dispose of. In order to decide the points raised by the learned Advocates of the parties we feel it necessary to quote the entire provisions of rule 14 of Order XXVI of the Code which is as under: 
"14(1) The Commissioner shall, such inquiry as may be necessary, divide the property in to as may shares as may be directed by the order under which the commission was issued, and shall allot such shares to the parties and may, if authorized thereto by the said order, award sums to be paid for the purpose of equalizing the value of the shares. 
(2) The Commissioner shall then prepare and sign report or the commissioners (where the commission was issued to more than one person and they cannot agree) shall prepare and sign separate reports appointing the share of each party and distinguishing each share (if so directed by the said order) by metes and bounds. Such report or reports shall be annexured to the commission and transmitted to the (Court which such time not exceeding there months as may be fixed by the court); and the court after hearing any objections which the parties may make to the report or reports shall confirm, very or set-aside the same. 
(provided that the court may on the prayer of the commissioner and on sufficient cause being shown, extend the time) 
(3) Where the court confirms or varies the report or reports its shall pass a decree in accordance with the same as confirmed or varied; but where the court sets aside the report or reports it shall either issue a new commission or other order as it shall think fit." 

38. Thus from rule 6(1) and 7 of XX the Code, it is clear that the decree shall always follow the judgment. From the reading of sub-rule (3) of rule 14 of the Order XXVI of the Code it is clear that where the court confirms or varies the report or reports it shall pass a decree in accordance with the same as confirmed or varied, but where the court sets aside the report or reports it shall either issue a new commission or make such other as it shall think fit. 

39. It is worthy to note here that in the present suit preliminary decree was passed on 25.9-2006 and the preliminary decree was made final on 19.2-2012 after rejecting the objection of the defendant against the report of Advocate Commissioner dated 30-9-2009. At this stage of the suit, the defendant long after 9 years filed an application for separate saham on 31-3-2014 disclosing the fact that after purchased the suit land they have mutated their names by opening BS Mutation Khatian No. 907/1 of 2001, creating Municipal holding arid paying rent and taxes to the authority. Defendant then took permissions and approved plan from the CDA on 27-12-2011 for constructing 14-storied residential building in its purchased BS plot Nos. 1170(p) and 1171(p) corresponding to RS plot No. 11(p) and in the meantime constructed 14-storied residential building and sold some flats to different buyers. The plaintiffs filed written objection on 24-4-2014 and additional written objection on 10-9-2014 against the defendants application for saham stating that during pendency of the suit, the defendant out his purchased land sold away 0.0284 sataks land to CDA by registered Kabala No. 18769 dated 8-12-2012 for extension of Hathazari road out of BS plot No. 1170(p) and 1171(p). As such, after sale the defendant now remained owner of 0.899 sataks only but the defendant totally concealed this fact, prayed for saham for entire 10 gondas land. 

40. The learned Advocate for the appellant Mr Kamal-ul-Alam argued forcefully that the Advocate Commissioner failed to comply with the preliminary decree without measuring the portion of roads and illegally allotted saham to the plaintiffs without satisfying the defendant share acquired by purchase from the plaintiffs. We find that this submission is not based on materials and evidence on record. It is evident from the Advocate Commissioner report that—After measuring the suit plot physically, it appears there is existing road in southern side of suit RS plot No. 11, North-South - 8', East - West 127' measuring an area of 0'0050 acre land. As such plaintiff's are now in possession of 9 (nine) gondas, 2 (two) kranti equivalent to 0.1834 sataks out of 11 (eleven) gondas = 0.2200 sataks which was allotted to the plaintiffs. 

41. As we have already found that the learned Joint District Judge after accepting the Advocate Commissioner's report made the preliminary decree final on 19-2-2012 and same was duly signed on 28-3-2016 and thereby nothing remained to be followed or passed to make the preliminary decree final as per provisions rule 6(1) and 7 of Order XX, and Order XXVI, rule 14(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure. The direction to submit stamp and the drawing and signing of the final decree are mere ministerial act to be performed by the court staff and that cannot have any bearing to make the decree final. The provisions of sub-rule (3) of rule 14 of Order XXVI, of the Code had made it obligatory upon the court confirms or varied the report. 

42. Here in the present case, the learned Joint District Judge after considering the Commissioner's report and objection filed by the defendant against the Commissioner's report as well as the evidence of CW-1 made the preliminary decree final on 19-2-2012. Since the defendant-appellant did not file any appeal against the preliminary decree dated 25-9-2006, as such the defendant now debarred from preferring any appeal against the final decree dated 19-2-2012 signed on 22-3-2016. The object of section 97 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that questions which had been urged by the parties and decided by the court at the stage of preliminary decree will not be open for re-agitation at the stage of the preparation of final decree and would be taken, as finally decided if no appeal had been preferred against the preliminary decree. In the present case as has been noticed that admittedly the defendant-appellant did not prefer any appeal against the said preliminary decree, the correctness of the preliminary decree cannot now be questioned by the defendant in this appeal in view of the clear mandate of section 97 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In other words in the event of failure to prefer an appeal against a preliminary decree, the preliminary decree is deemed to have attained finality. It is also admitted position that the preliminary decree has been affirmed by the High Court Division in the judgment dated 23-2-2008 in First Appeal No. 124 of 2007 with modification. The trial court after due consideration of the Advocate Commissioner report made the preliminary decree final on 19-2-2012. 

43. We have gone through the decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the appellant reported in AIR 1990 (Orissa), 4 BLC 460, 3 CLR (AD) 209 and 19 BLT (HCD) 14. There is a marked point of, distinction between the facts of the case now before us and the facts of the cited cases. 

44. Accordingly, we hold that the instant appeal is barred under section 97 of the Civil Procedure Code. 

45. In the result appeal not being maintainable and is hereby dismissed without any order as to cost. The connected Rule being Civil Rule No. 423(F) of 2016 is discharged. 

Send down the Lower Court Records at once and a copy of the judgment be sent to the concerned court expeditiously. 

End.

Md Humayun Kabir with M Muntasir Shahin, Md Sharif Khan and Haripada Barman, Advocates—For the Petitioner 
Md Mizanur Rahman, AAG—For the Respondent No. 1. 
None Appears—For the Respondent No. 4.
