full_judgment:
JBM Hassan, J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the office order dated 6-1-2019 contained in memo No. ইআবি/রেজি/প্রশা/কা.গ.ব/র-১৪/২০১৬/৭৩৮৫ issued under the signature of the Registrar (In-Charge), Islamic Arabic University, Dhaka (respondent No.3) nominating the respondent No.4 as the President (সভাপতি) of the Governing Body of the Sonakhuli Munshipara Kamil Madrasha, Syedpur, Nilphamari (Annexure-A to the writ petition) should not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect And further as to why the respondents should not be directed to nominate the President of the Governing Body of the Sonakhuli Munshipara Kamil Madrasha, Syedpur, Nilphamari in compliance with the section (Kha)(1)(1.2)(i) of "প্রাথমিক পাঠদান ও অধিভুক্ত মাদ্রাসা সমূহের গভর্ণিং বডি ও এডহক কমিটি সংক্রান্ত নীতিমালা" of the "ফাজিল ও কামিল মাদ্রাসা অধিভুক্ত সংক্রান্ত অর্ডিন্যান্স, ২০০৬" and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

2. Relevant facts leading to issuance of the Rule Nisi are that the petitioner is a donor member of the Governing Body of the Sonakhuli Munshipara Kamil Madrasha, Syedpur Nilphamari (the Madrasha) and also a well wisher of the said Madrasha being native of the locality. In order; to constitute a Governing Body of the Madrasha, the election was held relating to different categories of members and thereafter Principal of the Madrasha by his letter dated 2-12-2018 sent proposal to the Islamic Arabic University, Dhaka (the University) for nominating the President of the Governing Body of the Madrasha. Pursuant to said proposal, the-University issued the impugned office order bearing memo No. ইআবি/রেজি/প্রশা/কা.গ.ব/র-১৪/২০১৬/৭৩৮৫ dated 6-1-2019 nomina-ting the respondent No. 4 as President of the Governing Body of the aforesaid Madrasha. 

3. It is further stated that the respondent No.4, namely, Md Moklesur Rahman has obtained only Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC). The said respondent is not a renowned educationalist and so he does not have the requisite qualification to get nomination as the President of the Governing Body of the Madrasha in accordance with clause 1.2(i) of "প্রাথমিক পাঠদান ও অধিভুক্ত মাদ্রাসা সমূহের গভর্ণিং বডি ও এডহক কমিটি সংক্রান্ত নীতিমালা" under "ফাজিল ও কামিল মাদ্রাসা অধিভুক্ত সংক্রান্ত অর্ডিন্যান্স, (the Nitimala). It is also stated that the Principal of the Madrasha sent the name of the respondent No. 4 along with a Demi Official (DO) letter of the local member of parliament on the basis of which the impugned nomination was made. In this backdrop, the petitioner filed this writ petition challenging the aforesaid nomination and obtained the present Rule Nisi. 

4. Mr Md Humayun Kabir, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that clause 1.2(i) of the Nitimala for constitution of the Governing Body of the Fazil and Kamil Madrasha provides that the Vice-Chancellor shall nominate either Additional Deputy Commissioner or any eminent educationalist "বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ" as the President of the Governing Body of a Madrasha for the area beyond district headquarter but here the Vice-Chancellor has nominated a person who is neither Additional Deputy Commissioner nor an eminent educationalist and, as such, the nomination was made in violation of the Nitimala. In support of his submission, Mr Kabir refers to a number of dictionaries to show literal meaning of "বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ" and that he also refers to the case, of Ashis Kanungo and others vs State of Orissa reported in 199611 OLR 348, the case of Narendra Kumar vs State of Orissa reported in AIR 1999 Orissa 71 and the Case of Padmanav Dehury vs State of Orissa reported in AIR 999 Orissa 97. Mr Kabir further submits that the name of respondent No.4 was proposed by the Principal of the Madrasha along with a DO letter of the local member of parliament and that pursuant to said proposal the nomination being made, the Vice-Chancellor could not exercise his own discretion and consideration in the nomination process in accordance with the Nitimala and so the, impugned nomination has not been passed in accordance with law. In support of his submission, Mr Humayun Kabir refers to the case of Badruzzaman Khan (Md) vs Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh reported in 20 BLC 658 and the case of Golam Kibria slabbar vs Mohammad Badruzzaman Khan reported in 2017 (25) BLT (AD) 114 by which the earlier case of the High Court Division (reported in 20 BLC) was affirmed. 

5. None appears for the respondent No. 4 when the matter is taken up for hearing. 

6. However, Mr Md Mizanur Rahman, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the respondent No.1 contends that the criteria given in the Nitimala i.e "বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ" although literally means an expert in education filed but it is very difficult in a practical scenario of the country relating to the thousands educational institutions to find out and nominate to a person within strict meaning of eminent educationalist and so, the learned Assistant Attorney-General prays for an interpretation about the word "বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ" in order to make nomination in accordance with this particular Nitimala. 

7. We have gone through the writ petition and other materials on record as well as the cited cases. 

8. One of the issues in this Rule is the required qualification of a person to be nominated as President of the Governing Body by the Vice-Chancellor of the University for the Fazil and Kamil Madrasha of the country in the alternative of the Government Officer (Deputy Commissioner or Additional Deputy Commissioner). To get answer about the said issue, let us first peruse the relevant provisions for nominating President of the Governing Body of the Fazil and Kamil Madrasha which is incorporated in clause 1.2(i) of the 

"প্রাথমিক পাঠদান ও অধিভুক্ত মাদ্রাসা সমূহের গভর্ণিং বডি ও এডহ�� কমিটি সংক্রান্ত নীতিমালা"
“(i) সভাপতি
ভাইস-চ্যান্সেলর মহোদয় জেলা সদরে অবস্থিত মাদ্রাসার ক্ষেত্রে সংশ্লিষ্ট জেলা প্রশাসককে, জেলা সদরে বাইরে অবস্থিত মাদ্রাসার ক্ষেত্রে সংশ্লিষ্ট অতিরিক্ত জেলা প্রশাসককে অথবা উভয় ক্ষেত্রে কোন বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদকে মনোনয়ন দিবেন (এই সংশোধনী ২৬-৬-২০১১ইং তারিখ অনুষ্ঠিত ফাজিল ও কামিল মাদ্রাসা শিক্ষা বিষয়ক একাডেমিক কমিটির ১৪তম সভার সুপারিশ মোতাবেক ২৯-৬-২০১১ইং তারিখ অনুষ্ঠিত সিন্ডিকেটের ২১২তম সভায় অনুমোদিত) । তবে সময়ে সময়ে সরকার কর্তৃক এতসংক্রান্ত বিষয়ে জারীকৃত প্রজ্ঞাপন/নীতিমালা এ ক্ষেত্রে প্রযোজ্য হবে।”
 
9. On a plain reading of the aforesaid provision, it appears that Vice-Chancellor of the University shall nominate the respective Deputy Commissioner as the President of the Governing Body in the District Headquarters and out of District Headquarters to the respective Additional Deputy Commissioner. Besides, in both the situations, Vice-Chancellor may also nominate an eminent educationalist “বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবি” in the alternative of aforementioned government officer. 

10. In the present case, by the impugned memo the Vice-Chancellor took second option i.e “বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ” in nominating the respondent No. 4 having educational qualification of HSC. Drawing our attention to his such academic qualification, Mr Humayun Kabir vehemently submits that bearing this academic career he can not qualify himself as an eminent educationalist “বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ” for nomination as President of the Governing Body of a Kamil Madrasha in accordance with clause 1.2(1) of the Nitimala. In this regard, we have gone through the cited cases of Indian jurisdiction and perused the meaning of “বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ”provided in different dictionaries. 

11. In the Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary meaning of Educationalist is "a specialist in theories and methods of teaching", Students Favourite Dictionary by AT Dev shows meaning of Educationalist is "on versed in the methods of education". Wharton's Law Lexicon (16th Edition) incorporates meaning of Educationalist referring to case laws as under:

"Educationalist, a person skilled in methods of educating of teaching, a person who promotes education. 
[Chambers Dictionary, as cited in Teachers Association Madaris Arabia vs State of UP (2009) 5 ALI 164 (168-169), para-21] 
A person, who receives education, cannot be treated as educationalist unless he is specialist in theory and methods of teaching. [Teachers Association of Madaris Arabia vs State of UP (2009) 5 ALJ 164 (169), para-24] [UP Board of Madrasa Education Act (29 of 2004), section 3(3)(a)]" 

12. Analyzing the meaning from the above mentioned dictionaries, we are led to hold that an educationalist means a specialist/expert/ skilled in theories and methods of teaching. From the aforesaid meanings, it is clear that educationalist means an expert in teaching both theories and methods and it ultimately indicate an experienced or retired Teacher, who can be considered as an expert in teaching. Thus, ordinary dictionary meaning of Educationalist indicates a Teacher being an experienced person in the Profession of teaching. From here it can be inferred that an educationalist must be an expert in the education field. 

13. It further appears that in the aforementioned cited cases of Indian jurisdiction, question of qualification of President of the Governing Body was raised in; accordance with the relevant prevailing laws requiring eminent educationalist for nomination as President of the Governing Body. In the case of Ashis Kanungo vs State of Orissa reported in 1996 II OLR 348 their Lordships held as under: 
1. who can Be regarded as an "eminent Educationalist" for the purpose of being nominated as the president of the Governing Body of an aided college is the sole question 
that arises for consideration in this writ petition." 
2-8 ………. 
Paragraph 9—In our considered opinion, a person to be nominated as the President of the Governing Body must be one who has distinguished himself in the study of the science and methods of education. For the reasons aforesaid, the nomination of opposite party No. 3 as President of the Governing Body of the college in question is vitiated and is liable to be quashed." 

14. The said view has also been reflected in the cases of Giridhari Gochhayat vs State of Orissa reported in 1998 II OLR 522, Narendra Kumar Rout vs State of Orissa reported in AIR 1999 Orissa 71 and the case of Radmanav Dehury vs State of Orissa, reported in AIR 1999 Orissa 97. 

15. However, regarding the expression "eminent educationalist" “বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ”, there is no yard stick or definition in tire Nitimala and considering the district level practical social scenario of our country, it is very difficult to consider the eminent educationalist by its ordinary dictionary meaning as provided in the dictionaries (mentioned above) in order to nominate a President of the Governing Body of the Fazil/Kamil madrasha within the purview of the Nitimala. Yet, we have to keep in mind that the purpose of constitution of Governing Body is for smooth management of the respective institutions and for-development of educational atmosphere of the institutions and of course, it has to be done with the cooperation of the teachers of the respective institutions. 

16. Similarly, It has to be kept in mind that what is the real purpose of nominating an eminent educationalist as the President of the Governing Body. Certainly the purpose is to bring in an academic atmosphere in the educational institutions. The students are at the threshold of higher educational careers. If the atmosphere in the institutions are not conducive for proper study, the only result will be pollution of academic atmosphere of the institutions. However, in nominating President of the Governing Body of a Dakhil/ Kamil Madrasha, the expression “বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ” provided in the Nitimala may not always be possible to follow in the social context of our country. 

17. Therefore, a person who would be head of the Governing Body has to be at least an educated person. As such, considering all aspects, an explanation is required to be reflected in the Nitimala about the expression “বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ”. The respondent No.1 shall consider this aspect amending the Nitimala relating to qualification-of the President of the Governing Body/Managing Committee of the educational institution within the meaning “বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ”. 

18. In the absence of such explanation of the expression we are of the view that President of the Fazil Madrasha and Kamil Madrasha have to be a graduate and master degree holder respectively in consonance with the academic courses of the respective madrasha. 

19. Since here in this case, the respondent No.4 has got the academic qualification of HSC, we are of the view that the respondent No. 4 is not a qualified person for nomination as President of Governing Body of this Kamil Madrasha within the meaning of “বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ” under the Nitimala. 

20. The next point raised by Mr Humayun Kabir that Nitimala provides absolute authority of the Vice-Chancellor of the University to nominate the President of the Governing Body. Nevertheless, it being not possible on the part of the Vice-Chancellor to find out the qualified person in accordance with the Nitimala from the concerned locality, there is a long practice that Principal of the concerned institution sends the proposal of the persons to be nominated. Here in this case, the Principal sent the name of the respondent No. 4 along with a DO letter of the local member of parliament due to which the learned Advocate submits that nomination of the respondent No. 4 was followed by the influence of the DO letter sent by the local member of parliament proposing respondent No. 4. 

21. In this regard, we have gone through the cited cases reported in 20 BLC 658 relevant portions of which are as follows: 
"Apparently this letter of the MP appears to be innocent. But the result of this letter that it indirectly influenced the Principal and also the Madrasha Board not to make their own judgment for selection of the President of the Governing Body, and ultimately the Madrasha Board nominated the Respondent No. 6 as recommended by the local MP. 
Thus the nomination of respondent No. 6 as the President is the result of an indirect influence of the local MP and the resultant failure of the Principal and Madrasha Board to comply with the requirement of regulation 5(3) of the Regulations, 2009. 
The local MP can at best make a recommendation to the Principal of the Madrasha in the consultative process under regulation 5(3). But the Principal is not legally bound to follow that recommendation and he is required to make his own judgment and to prepare a panel of three persons. The power to take the decision lies with the Chairman of the Madrasha Board. Thus the impugned nomination is a clear violation of law." 

22. Against the said judgment while the respondents filed civil petition for leave to appeal, the Appellate Division by the decision reported in 25 BLT (AD) 114 dismissed the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal relevant portions of the said judgment are as follows:
"Eventually the Principal has failed to comply with the requirement of regulation 5(3) by sending a panel of three persons. The reference to regulation 5(1) and 5(2) in his letter gives a clear indication that the Principal misread those provisions. These provisions allow the MP to express his desire to be the president himself, only for four Madrashas. These provisions do not allow a MP to make recommendation to the Chairman of the Madrasha Board. 
By reference to the letter from the MP dated 6-11-2014 addressed to the Chairman of the Bangladesh Madrasha Sikkha Board the High Court Division noted that this letter indirectly influence the Principal and also the Madrasha Board not to make their own judgment for selection of the President of the Governing Body, and ultimately the Madrasha Board nominated respondent No. 6 (petitioner herein) as recommended by the local MP which is tantamount to failure of the Principal and Madrasha Board to comply with the requirement of Regulation 5(3) of the Regulations, 2009. 
The provision of Regulation 5(3) requires the Principal of the Madrasha to put forward 3 names from among the categories of persons mentioned in Regulation 5(3), in consultation with the local MP and educationalist. However, when he nominated respondent No. 6 as the only candidate as recommended by the local Member of Parliament, he has failed to comply with the provision of Regulation 5(3) of the Regulations, 2009. We are of the view that since the local Member of Parliament had no power to make such recommendation and since the provision of Regulation 5(3) was not complied, the High Court Division rightly held that the impugned letter dated 28-12-2014 is without any lawful authority and hence of no legal effect." 

23. In view of the aforesaid ratio of our apex Court, we are led to hold that since clause 1, 2(i) of the Nitimala has given absolute authority to the Vice. Chancellor, it is to be exercised by him independently by his own consideration. Therefore, the proposal of respondent No.4 as President of the Governing Body along with a DO letter of the local member of parliament made influence in the exercise of aforesaid authority of the Vice-Chancellor. Of course for selecting appropriate person from the locality the Principal shall send the proposal but it ought to have been in the form of a panel of minimum three persons along with their academic and socio activities credentials, so that the Vice-Chancellor can pick up the appropriate person at his own discretion and consideration. But that having not been done in this particular case, we are of the view that .the nomination of respondent No. 4 was not made in accordance with the Nitimala and so, it needs to be interfered. 

24. In view of above discussions, we find merit in this Rule. 

25. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned memo dated 6-1-2019 contained in memo No. ইআবি/রেজি/প্রশা/কা.গ.ব/র-১৪/২০১৬/৭৩৮৫ issued under the signature of the Registrar (In-Charge), Islamic Arabic University, Dhaka (respondent No.3) nominating the respondent No. 4 as the President (সভাপতি) of the Governing Body of the Sonakhuli Munshipara Kamil Madrasha Syedpur, Nilphamari (Annexure-A to the writ petition) is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

26. The Principal of the Madrasha shall immediately send a proposal of three persons panel to the Arabic University in accordance with the observation made in this judgment for nomination of President of the Governing Body for the remaining period of tenure of the Governing Body within 30 (thirty) days from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment and order. 

Communicate a copy of the judgment and order to the respondents at once.
 
End.

lawyer:
Md Sirajul Islam, Advocate—For the Pre-emptor-Appellant. 
Ai Mohammad Ali Senior, Advocate with NM Ahasanul Haque, Advocates—For the Pre-emptee-Respondent Nos. 1 and 2.
parties:
Serajul Islam (Md) ------ Pre-emptor-Appellant
VS
Sheikh Azad Hossain and others ------ Pre-emptee-Respondents
full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim, J: This First Appeal No. 204 of 2018 at the instance of pre-emptor-appellant, Serajul Islam is directed against the judgment and decree dated 9-4-2018 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Naogaon rejecting the plaint, of Other Class Suit No. 68 of 2013 under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure in a suit to enforce the right of pre-emption under the Muhammadan Law. 

2. Pre-emptor-plaintiff Serajul Islam is invoking right of Sufaa, stating, inter-alia, that suit properties originally belonged to Shamsuzzoha, predecessor of the plaintiff-pre-emptor, Serajul Islam and opposite party Nos. 3 -8. The plaintiff being a Shafi-i-Sharik; (co-sharer in the property), Defendant No. 3, Badruddoza, who is full brother and co-sharer transfered the suit land along with the building to the defendant No. 1, Sheikh Azad Hossain and defendant No. 2 Sree Rajesh Kumar Saha for Taka 94,00,000 (ninety four lac) by registered sale deed No. 5542 dated 11-7-2012 beyond the knowledge of the plaintiff; that the plaintiff is the Shafi-i-Sharik, Shafi-i-Khalit (participator in immunities and appendages) and Shafi-i-Jar (owner of adjacent immovable property) of the schedule property; that defendant No. 3 without giving any notice to the plaintiff sold the schedule property to the purchasers, defendant Nos. 1 and 2, pre-emptees, who are totally strangers in the suit property; that the plaintiff first came to know about the transfer on 7-1-2013 when one Muhit Talukder informed about the Kabala; that plaintiff expressed his Talab-i-Mowasibat, that he is ready to purchase the property, in this way performed his Talab-i-ishhat (demand of confirmation) for pre-emption; that the plaintiff requested the purchasers-defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to give back the schedule property but they refused. Hence the plaintiff has filed the present suit for pre-emption suit on 24-6-2013 under the Muhammadan Law. 

3. The defendant No. 2 Rajkumar Saha died on 12-12-2014 leaving wife, 3 daughters and only 1(one) son, Rakesh Kumar, who was added as defendant No. 2(a) in place of deceased Defendant No. 2 under Order I, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure by order No. 22 dated 29-7-2015. The defendant No. 3 also died and his heirs were duly substituted as defendant Nos. 3(ka)-3(ga) by order no 39 dated 19-8-2015. 

4. That when the suit was in pre-emptory stage, defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on 4-10-2017 filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint on the ground that since the substituted defendant No. 2(a) is a Hindu, as such pre-emption under Muhammadan law is not applicable for the person belonged to Hindu religion; that the transaction of sale of the suit property was supervised and negatioted through the plaintiff and he has taken an active part in bringing about the disputed transfer; that the defendant No. 3 mutated his name by filing Mutation Case No. 4757 of 2010-11 and not a co-sharer, sold away to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and delivered possession. Moreover, the present suit is not maintainable as per decision of the High Court Division reported in 2015 (23) BLT (HCD) 173 = 67 DLR. 302. That present suit is not maintainable under Article 10 of schedule I of the Limitation Act and Mohammadan law. Against the said application for the rejection of plaint, the plaintiff-appellant did not file any written objection. The learned Joint District Judge First Court, Naogaon after contested hearing allowed the application under order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and rejected the plaint by the judgment and decree dated 9-4-2018. 

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 9-4-2018, passed by the learned Joint District Judge First Court Naogaon in the suit. The order of rejection of plaint shall be deemed to be a decree within the meaning of section 2(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure. Therefore, pre-emptor-plaintiff preferred the aforesaid appeal against the judgment and decree dated 9-4-2018. 

6. Mr Md Serajul Islam, learned Advocate for the pre-emptor-appellant submits that the learned Joint District Judge failed to consider that although none of the conditions as provided under Order VII, rule 11 was not complied with but the Joint District Judge erroneously rejected the plaint which is liable to be set-aside. He further submits that the learned Court below totally failed to consider that the pre-emptor, full brother of the Vendor is a Muslim and out of two purchasers, one is Muslim and stranger to the land in question, as such filing of present pre-emption case under Muhammadan law is well maintainable. He finally submits that no statutory law has been prohibit or bar to claim Shufaa (pre-emption) against a Hindu, a non-Muslim purchaser. In support of his submissions learned advocate referred the decisions reported in 51 DLR (AD) 211 and 44 DLR (AD) 242. 

7. On the contrary, Mr NM Ahsanul Hoque, learned Advocate on behalf of the pre-emptee-respondent has contended that the court below rightly rejected the plaint on the finding that admittedly one of the pre-emptor-purchaser-defendant No. 2, Raj Kumar Saha being a Hindu and non-muslim, as such the pre-emptor cannot claim benefit of Shufaa under the Muhammadan law, thus the present suit is barred by law. He has further contented that the learned Joint District Judge, relying on the decision in the case of Sree Onil Kumar Podder vs Mostafa Unuch reported in 2015 (23) BLT (HCD) 173 = 67 DLR 302 correctly found that since in the present case vendor is a Muslim and one of the purchaser is a Hindu, the pre-emptor could easily invoke the provision of statutory secular law of pre-emption namely, State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 and Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 which came into operation giving statutory right of pre-emption. Since the pre-emptor filed the instant pre-emption case invoking right of pre-emption under the Muhammadan Law, same is clearly barred by law. Thus the court below rightly rejected the plaint. 

8. In this appeal main question for determination as to whether in a case of pre-emption, where pre-emptor and the vendor/ seller are Muhammadans and the pre-emptee-vendee is Hindu, Non Muslim, is the Muhammadan Law of pre-emption(shufaa) 'to be applied to the matters, in other words whether a Muhammadan can exercise the right of pre-emption (Shufaa) against a Hindu or non-Muslim under Muhammadan Law. 

9. We have carefully examined the plaint, application filed under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the decisions cited by the parties. 

10. The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 came into operation giving statutory right of pre-emption. The right of pre-emption is very special in character. Right of pre-emption is not right of repurchase but a simple right of substitution, entitling the pre-emptor, by reason of a legal incident to which the sale itself was subject to stand in the shoes of vendee in respect of all the rights and obligations arising from sale under which he has derived his title. Before the British regime all the citizens of India followed Muhammadan law. Full Bench decision of Allahabad in Gobinda Dayal vs Inayatullah reported in ILR VII (All) 775, a case between Muslim pre-emptor and Hindu pre-emptee-purchaser, where Muhammadan law applied according to justice, equity and good conscience. During Muslim regime Hindu Jaminders had to invoke the right of pre-emption as per Muhammadan law as during Muslim rule right of pre-emption was extended to all without any discrimination. We have seen that in 1885 there was no corresponding statutory law governing the field of pre-emption. At that time pre-emption was governed as per provisions of Muhammadan law, if pre-emptor is Hindu there also he could pre-empt the land under the provisions of Muhammadan law. But at present scenario has been changed. After creation of Pakistan and thereafter Bangladesh emerged as Independent country, State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 came into operation giving right to all to pre-empt the land. Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the right of pre-emption of the co-shares re-enacted through the new legislation called the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 2006 (Act XXXIV of 2006); provision of section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 (Act XIII of 1948) attracted in case of a land in a Municipal Area. 

11. It appears that the learned Joint District Judge rightly held that since the vendor-defendant No. 3 and the pre-emptor are Muslims and one of the purchaser-pre-emptee, defendant No. 2 is Hindu wants to invoke his pre-emption right, he can easily invoke the right of pre-emption under the provision of statutory law and not under Muhammadan Law. The right of pre-emption could not be enforced by a Muhammadan against a Hindu vendee. We do not understand why the plaintiff-pre-emptor instead of invoking statutory law jumped to personal law against a Hindu. In the instant case since the pre-emptor-appellant invoked the right of pre-emption under the Muhammadan Law, same is clearly barred by law. 

12. In the back ground of the discussions, relevant provisions of Muhammadan law, State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 and the decisions cited above, we therefore, find that the learned Joint District Judge on consideration and appreciation of the averments made in the plaint correctly found that the present suit is barred by law and rightly rejected the plaint. 

13. In the result, this appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 09-4-2018 passed by the learned First Court of Joint District Judge, Naogaon is hereby affirmed. 

14. The Other Class Suit No. 68 of 2013 is hereby dismissed and a copy of the judgment be sent to the concerned court expeditiously. 

The connected Civil Rule No. 236(F) of 2018 is discharged. The order of states-quo granted earlier by this court is hereby vacated. 

End.

lawyer:
Munsurul Haque Chowdhury, Advocate—For the Petitioner 
Syed Nazmul Karim, Advocate—For the Respondent No.12.
parties:
Rumen Miah (Md) ------ Petitioner
vs
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Education and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
JBM Hassan, J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the memo No. ইআবি/রেজি/প্রশা/ফা.গ.গ.ব/স-২০/২০১৭/৫১১৬ dated 21-3-2018 (signed on 15-3-2018) under the signature of Registrar (In Charge) of the Islamic Arabic University (respondent No.4) approving the Governing Body of the Habibur Keshobpur Fazil Madrasha so far as it relates to the post of President should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Relevant facts leading to issuance of the Rule Nisi are that the election of different categories of members was held in order to constitute a Governing Body of the Habibpur Keshabpur Fazil Madrasha, Police Station-Jagannathpur, District-Sunamgonj (the Madrasha) for a period of three years from 16-10-2017 to 15-10-2020. Thereafter, the Principal as ex-officio Secretary of the Governing Body sent a proposal by the memo dated 7-8-2017 to the Vice Chancellor of the Islamic Arabic University for nomination of one Md Akter Hossain, former Mayour of Jagannathpur Purashava (added respondent No. 13) as President of the Governing Body. Accordingly, the University by their memo dated 18-9-2017 nominated the said person as President of the Governing Body in accordance with clause 1.2(i) of "প্রাথমিক পাঠদান ও অধিভুক্ত মাদ্রাসা মসূহের গভর্ণিং বড়ি ও এডহক কমিটি সংক্রান্ত নীতিমালা under ফাজিল ও কামিল মাদ্রাসা অধিভুক্ত সংক্রান্ত অর্ডিন্যান্স” (the Nitimala). Ultimately, the University issued the impugned approval of Governing Body vide memo bearing No." ইআবি/রেজি/প্রশা/ফা.গ.গ.ব/স-২০/২০১৭/৫১১৬ তারিখ ২১ মার্চ ২০১৮" nominating the added respondent No.13 as President of the said Governing Body.

3. In the writ petition it is also stated that the aforementioned Nitimala incorporates provision to nominate an eminent educationalist “বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ” as President of the Governing Body but the President nominated by the impugned memo, does not have the said qualification inasmuch as in his election nomination paper of the Mayoral election, Jagannathpur Pourashava, Sunamgonj, he described himself as "স্বশিক্ষিত" in the column of the educational qualification. In this backdrop, the petitioner filed this writ petition and obtained the present Rule Nisi. 

4. Mr Munsurul Haque Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that clause 1.2(i) of the Nitimala for constitution of the Governing Body of the Fazil Madrasha provides that the Vice Chancellor shall nominate either Additional Deputy Commissioner or any eminent educationalist "বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ " as the President of the Governing Body of a Fazil/Kamil Madrasha for the area beyond district headquarter but here the Vice Chancellor has nominated a person who is neither Additional Deputy Commissioner nor an eminent educa-tionalist and, as such, the nomination was made in violation of the Nitimala. In support of his submission Mr Chowdhury refers to a number of dictionaries to show literal meaning of "বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ" and that he also refers to the case ofAshis Kanungo vs State of Orissa reported in 1996 II OLR 348, the case of Narendra Kumar vs State of Orissa reported AIR 1999 Ori 71 and the case of Padmanav Dehury vs State of Orissa reported in AIR 1999 Ori 97. He further submits that the respondent No. 13 was a sole proposed person by the Principal of the Madrasha along with a demi official (DO) letter of the local member of parliament and that pursuant to said proposal the nomination being made, the Vice Chancel-lor could not exercise his own discretion and consideration in the nomination process in accordance with the Nitimala and so the impugned nomination has not been passed in accordance with law. In support of his submission, Mr Chowdhury refers to the case of Badruzzaman Khan (Md) vs Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh reported in 20 BLC 658 and the case of Golam Kibria Jabbar vs Mohammad Badruzzaman Khan reported in 25 BLT (AD) 114 by which the earlier case of the High Court Division (reported in 20 BLC) was affirmed. 

5. None appears to represent the added respondent No. 13 when the Rule is taken up for hearing. 

6. However, Mr Md Mizanur Rahman, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the respondent No.1 contends that the criteria given in the Nitimala i.e "বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ" although literally means an expert in education field but it is very difficult in a practical scenario of the country relating to the thousands educational institutions to find out and nominate to a person within strict meaning of eminent educationalist and so, the learned Assistant Attorney-General prays for an interpretation about the word " বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ" in order to make nomination in accordance with this particular Nitimala. 

7. We have gone through the writ petition and other materials on record as well as the cited cases. 

8. One of the issues in this Rule is the required qualification of a person to be nominated as President of the Governing Body by the Vice Chancellor of the University for the Fazil Madrasha of the country in the alternative of the Government Officer (Deputy Commissioner or Additional Deputy Commissioner). To get answer about the said issue, let us first peruse the relevant provisions for nominating President of the Governing Body of the Fazil and Kamil Madrasha which is incorporated in clause 1.2(i) of the "প্রাথমিক পাঠদান ও অধিভুক্ত মাদ্রাসা সমূহের গভর্ণিং বডি ও এডহক কমিটি সংক্রান্ত নীতিমালা।"

“ (i) সভাপতি
ভাইস-চ্যান্সেলর মহোদয় জেলা সদরে অবস্থিত মা মাদ্রাসার ক্ষেত্রে সংশ্লিষ্ট জেলা প্রশাসককে, জেলা সদরের বাইরে অবস্থিত মাদ্রাসার ক্ষেত্রে সংশ্লিষ্ট অতিরিক্ত জেলা প্রশাসককে অথবা উভয় ক্ষেত্রে কোন বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদকে মনোনয়ন দিবেন (এ সংশোধনী ২৬-৬-২০১১ইং তারিখ অনুষ্ঠিত ফাজিল ও কামিল মাদ্রাসা শিক্ষা বিষয়ক একাডেমিক কমিটির ১৪তম সভার সুপারিশ মোতাবেক ২৯-৬-২০১১ইং তারিখ অনুস্থিত সিভিকেটের ২১২তম সভায় অনুমোদিত)। তবে সময়ে সময়ে সরকার কর্তৃক এতদ্বসংক্রান্ত বিষয়ে জারীকৃত প্রজ্ঞাপন/নীতিমালা এ ক্ষেত্রে প্রযোজ্য হবে।” 

9. On a plain reading of the aforesaid provision, it appears that Vice Chancellor of the University shall nominate the respective Deputy Commissioner as the President of the Governing Body in the District Headquarters and out of District Headquarters to the respective Additional Deputy Commissioner. Besides, in both the situations, Vice Chancellor may also nominate an eminent educationalist "বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ" in the alter-native of afore-mentioned government officer. 

10. In the present case, by the impugned memo the Vice Chancellor took second option i.e "বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ " in nominating the added respondent No.13 who himself described as "শিক্ষিত" in his nomination paper for the mayoral election of his Pourashava (Annexure-A to the writ petition). Drawing our attention to his such declaration about academic qualification, Mr Munsurul Haque Chowdhury vehemently submits that the respondent No. 13 can not qualify himself as an eminent educationalist (বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ) for nomination as President of the Governing Body of a Fazil Madrasha in accordance with clause 1.2(i) of the Nitimala. In this regard, we have gone through the cited cases of Indian jurisdiction and perused the meaning of " বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ” provided in different dictionaries. 

11. In the Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary meaning of Educationalist is "a specialist in theories and methods of teaching". Students' Favourite Dictionary by AT Dev shows meaning of Educationalist is " on versed in the methods of education". Wharton's Law Lexicon (16th Edition) incorporates meaning of Educationalist referring to case laws as under: 
"Educationalist, a person skilled in methods of educating of teaching, a person who promotes education. [Chambers Dictionary, as cited in Teachers Association Madaris Arabia vs State of UP (2009) 5 ALI 164 (168-169), para-21] 
A person, who receives education, can not be treated as educationalist unless he is specialist in theory and methods of teaching. [Teachers Association of Madaris Arabia vs State of UP (2009) 5 ALI 164 (169), para-24] [UP Board of Madrasa Education Act (29 of 2004), section 3(3)(a)]" 

12. Analyzing the meaning from the above mentioned dictionaries, we are led to hold that an educationalist (শিক্ষাবিদ) means a specialist/ expert/skilled in theories and methods of teaching. From the aforesaid meanings, it is clear that educationalist means an expert in teaching both theories and methods and it ultimately indicate an experienced or retired Teacher, who can be considered as an expert in teaching. Thus, ordinary dictionary meaning of Educationalist (শিক্ষাবিদ) indicates a Teacher being an experienced person in the Profession of teaching. From here it can be inferred that an educationalist must be an expert in the education field. 

13. It further appears that in the afore-mentioned cited cases of Indian jurisdiction, question of qualification of President of the Governing Body was raised in accordance with the relevant prevailing laws requiring eminent educationalist for nomination as President of the Governing Body. In the case of Ashis Kanungo vs State of Orissa reported in 1996 II OLR 348 their Lordships held as under: 
"1. who can be regarded as an "eminent Educationalist" for the purpose of being nominated as the president of the Governing Body of an aided college is the sole question that arises for consideration in this writ petition." 
2-8………  
Paragraph-9—In our considered opinion, a person to be nominated as the President of the Governing Body must be one who has distinguished himself in the study of the science and methods of education. For the reasons aforesaid, the nomination of opp. party No.3 as President of the Governing Body of the college in question is vitiated and is liable to be quashed." 

14. The said view has also been reflected in the cases of Giridhari Gochhayat vs State of Orissa reported in 1998 II OLR 522, Narendra Kumar Rout vs State of Orissa reported in AIR 1999 Ori 71 and the case of Radmanav Dehury vs State of Orissa reported in AIR 1999 Ori 97. 

15. However, regarding the expression "eminent educationalist" (বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ” there is no yard stick or definition in the Nitimala and considering the district level practical social scenario of our country, it is very difficult to consider the eminent educationalist by its ordinary dictionary meaning as provided in the dictionaries (mentioned above) in order to nominate a President of the Governing Body of the Fazil/Kamil madrasha within the purview of the Nitimala. Yet, we have to keep in mind that the purpose of constitution of Governing Body is for smooth management of the respective institutions and for development of educational atmosphere of the institutions and of course, it has to be done with the cooperation of the teachers of the respective institutions. 

16. Similarly, It has to be kept in mind that what is the real purpose of nominating an eminent educationalist as the President of the Governing Body. Certainly the purpose is to bring in an academic atmosphere in the educational institutions. The students are at the threshold of higher educational careers. If the atmosphere in the institutions are not conducive for proper study, the oily result will be pollution of academic atmosphere of the institutions. However, the expression "বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ" provided in the Nitimala may not always be possible to follow in the social context of our country. 

17. Therefore, a person who would be head of the Governing Body has to be at least an educated person. As such, considering all aspects, an explanation is required to be reflected in the Nitimala about the expression "বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ ". The respondent No.1 shall consider this aspect amending the Nitimala relating to qualification of the President of the Governing Body/Managing Committee of the educational institution within the meaning "বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ ". 

18. In the absence of such explanation of the expression "বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ ", we are of the view that President of the Fazil Madrasha and Kami I Madrasha have to be a graduate and master degree holder respectively in consonance with the academic courses of the respective madrasha. 

19. Since here in this case, the added respondent No.13 has declared himself as "শিক্ষিত" in his nomination form for the mayoral election (Annexure-A to the writ petition), we are of the view that the added respondent No.13 having no academic degree is not a qualified person for nomination as President of Governing Body of this Fazil Madrasha within the meaning of "বিশিষ্ট শিক্ষাবিদ " under the Nitimala.
 
20. The next point raised by Mr Munsurul Haque Chowdhury that Nitimala provides absolute authority of the Vice Chancellor of the University to nominate the President of the Governing Body. Nevertheless, it being not possible on the part of the Vice Chancellor to find out the qualified person in accordance with the Nitimala from the concerned locality, there is a long practice that Principal of the concerned institution sends the proposal of the.persons to be nominated. Here in this case, the Principal sent only the name of the respondent No. 13 along with a DO letter of the local member of parliament due to which the learned Advocate submits that nomination of the respondent No.13 was followed by the influence of the DO letter sent by the local member of parliament proposing sole person. 

21. In this regard, to appreciate his submission we have gone through the proposal sent by the Principal of the Madrasha which is quoted in the writ petition and it runs as follows: 
বরাবর,
উপাচার্য/রেজিট্রার
ইসলামী আরবী বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়
বাড়ি নং ১২৪/২২, ব্লক-এ, সড়ক-০৩
পশ্চিম ধানমন্ডি, বছিলা, মোহাম্মদপুর, ঢাকা ।
বিষয়ঃ গভণিংবড়ির সভাপতি মনোনয়নের প্রস্তাবনা প্রসঙ্গে।
জনাব,

যথাবিহিত সম্মানপূর্বক নিবেদন এই, অত্র মাদ্রাসা গভনিংবডির মেয়াদ উত্তীণের তারিখ আগামী ৩০-৮-২০১৭ খ্রিষ্টাব্দ। বিধি মোতাবেক সকল ক্যাটাগরির নির্বাচন সম্পন্ন হয়েছে। বর্তমানে গভর্নিংবডির জন্য মহোদয় কর্তৃক একজন সভাপতি মনোনয়ন আবশ্যক । এক্ষেত্রে মাদ্রাসা এলাকার বিশিষ্ট সমাজসেবি, শিক্ষানুরাপী ব্যক্তি, মাদ্রাসা গভণিংবডির বর্তমান ভাইস চেয়ারম্যান ও জগন্নাথপুর পৌরসভার সাবেক মেয়র জনাব মোঃ আক্তার হোসেন, পিতা মৃত হাছন আলী, গ্রামঃ হবিবপুর, ডাকঘর ও উপজেলা-জগন্নাথপুর, সুনামগঞ্জ কে সভাপতি মনোনয়নের জন্য প্রস্তাব পেশ করা হলো ।

উল্লেখ্য, তাকে সভাপতি মনোয়নের জন্য সুনামগঞ্জ-৩৩ আসনের মাননীয় সংসদ সদস্য, গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ সরকারের অর্থ মন্ত্রণালয় ও পরিকল্পনা মন্ত্রণালয়ের মাননীয় প্রতিমন্ত্রী জনাব এম এ মান্নান মহোদয় ২৯-৭-২০১৭ খ্রিষ্টাব্দে স্মারকয়ুক্ত ডিও লেটার প্রদান করেছেন । সদয় বিবেচনার জন্য এতদৃসঙ্গে সংযুক্ত করে দেয়া হল।

অতএব, মহোদয় সমীপে নিবেদন, প্রা্থীত ব্যক্তি জনাব মোঃ আক্তার হোসেন, পিতা মৃত হাছন আলী, গ্রাম-হবিবপুর, ডাকঘর ও উপজেলা-জগন্নাথপুর, সুনামগঞ্জকে হবিবপুর ফাজিল মাদ্রাসা গভর্ণিবডির সভাপতি মনোনয়ন দানে মহোদয়ের মর্জি হয়।

মো আব্দুল হাকীম
অধ্যক্ষ
হবিবপুর কেশবপুর ফাজিল মাদ্রাসা
জগন্নাথপুর, সুনামগঞ্জ ।”

22. On perusal of the aforesaid proposal, it appears that the respondent No.13 alone was forwarded by the Principal alongwith a DO letter issued by the local member of parliament. In this regard, we have gone through the cited cases reported in 20 BLC 658 relevant portions of which are as follows: 
"Apparently this letter of the MP appears to be innocent. But the result of this letter that it indirectly influenced the Principal and also the Madrasha Board not to make their own judgment for selection of the President of the Governing Body, and ultimately the Madrasha Board nominated the Respondent No.6 as recommended by the local MP. 
Thus, the nomination of respondent No.6 as the President is the result of an indirect influence of the local MP and the resultant failure of the Principal and Madrasha Board to comply with the requirement of regulation 5(3) of the Regulations, 2009. 
The local MP can at best make a recommendation to the Principal of the Madrasha in the consultative process under regulation 5(3). But the Principal is not legally bound to follow that recommendation and he is required to make his own judgment and to ppepare a panel of three persons. The power to take the decision lies with the Chairman of the Madrasha Board. Thus the impugned nomination is a clear violation of law." 

23. Against the said judgment while the respondents filed civil petition for leave to appeal, the Appellate Division by the decision reported in 25 BLT (AD) 114 dismissed the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal relevant portions of the said judgment are as follows: 
"Eventually the Principal has failed to comply with the requirement of regulation 5(3) by sending a panel of three persons. The reference to regulation 5(1) and 5(2) in his letter gives a clear indication that the Principal misread those provisions. These provisions allow the MP to express his desire to be the president himself only for four Madrashas. These provisions do not allow a MP to make recommendation to the Chairman of the Madrasha Board. 
By reference to the letter from the MP dated 6-11-2014 addressed to the Chairman of the Bangladesh Madrasha Sikkha Board the High Court Division noted that this letter indirectly influence the Principal and also the Madrasha Board not to make their own judgment for selection of the President of the Governing Body, and ultimately the Madrasha Board nominated respondent No.6 (petitioner herein) as recommended by the local MP which is tantamount to failure of the Principal and Madrasha Board to comply with the requirement of Regulation5(3) of the Regulations, 2009. 
The provision of Regulation 5(3) requires the Principal of the Madrasha to put forward 3 names from among the categories of persons mentioned in Regulation 5(3), in consultation with the local MP and educationalist. However, when he nominated respondent No.6 as the only candidate as recommended by the local Member of Parliament, he has failed to comply with the provision of Regulation 5(3) of the Regulations, 2009. We are of the view that since the local Member of Parliament haci.no power to make such recommendation and since the provision of Regulation 5(3) was not complied, the High Court Division rightly held that the impugned letter dated 28-12-2014 is without any lawful authority and hence of no legal effect." 

24. In view of the aforesaid ratio of our apex Court, we are led to hold that since clause 1.2(i) of the Nitimala has given absolute authority .to the Vice Chancellor, it is to be exercised by him independently by his own consideration. Therefore, the proposal of a sole name along with a DO letter of the local member of parliament made influence in the exercise of aforesaid authority of the Vice Chancellor. Of course for selecting appropriate person from the locality the Principal shall send the proposal but it ought to have been in the form of a panel of minimum three persons along with their academic and socio academic credentials, so that the Vice Chancellor can pick up the appropriate person at his own discretion and consideration. But that 'having not been done in this particular case, we are of the view that the nomination was not made in accordance with the Nitimala and so, it needs to: be interfered. 

25. In view of above discussions, we' find merit in this Rule. 

26. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned memo No. memo No. ইআবি/রেজি/প্রশা/ফা.গ.ব/স-২০/২০১৭/৫১১৬ dated 21-3-2018 under the signature of Registrar (In Charge) the respondent No.4 (signed on 15-3-2018) approving the governing body so far as it relates to the post of President of the Habibur Keshobpur Fazil Madrasha is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

27. The Principal of the Madrasha shall immediately send a proposal of three persons panel to the. Islamic Arabic University in accordance with the observation made in this judgment for nomination of President of the Governing Body for the remaining period of tenure of the Governing Body within 30 (thirty) days from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment and order. 

Communicate a copy of the judgment and order to the respondents at once. 

End.

lawyer:
AKM Shamsul Haque, Advocate—For the Petitioner. 
Mahfuzur Rahman Roman, Advocate—For the Opposite-Party.
parties:
Rajendra Kumar Agorwala ------ Plaintiff-Petitioner
Vs
Kazi Dowed Ibrahim and others Defendant ------- Opposite-Party
full_judgment:
This Rule on an application filed by the plaintiff petitioner under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the Code) was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 20-11-2018 passed by the learned District Judge, Joypurhat in Civil Revision No. 14 of 2018 so far as it relates for allowing the application dated 15-11-2018 arising out of the order dated 7-5-2018 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Akkelpur, Joypurhat in Other Class Suit No. 4 of 2018 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The short facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, is that the present petitioner Sree Rajendra Kumar Agorwala along with 4 others filed Other Class Suit No. 4 of 2018 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Akkelpur, Joypurhat for permanent injunction restraining the defendant from disturbing their peaceful possession into the suit land. The suit land has been described as 0.42 acres of land of hall plot No. 46 of SA khatian No. 89 corresponding to CS khatian No. 56. 

3. During the pendency of the suit all the defendants appearing in the suit prayed for local investigation of the suit land under Order 26 Rule 9 of the Code. The trial Court upon taking hearing from both the sides rejected the said prayer by his order dated 7-5-2018. 

4. The defendants as against the said order of rejection of the learned Assistant Judge preferred Civil Revision No. 14 of 2018 and the matter was heard by the learned District Judge herself who by his impugned judgment and order dated 20-11-2018 allowed the revision partly and made an order for local inspection instead of local investigation in the terms of an application filed for local inspection. 

5. The plaintiff No. 1 Sree Rajendra Kumar Agorwala being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said order of the First Revisional Court below moved this Court filing an application under section 115(4) of the Code and obtained the present Rule as stated earlier. 

6. On the date of the issuance of the Rule, the operation of the impugned judgment and order dated 20-11-2018 was stayed for 06 months, later on it was extended on 30-7-2019 for one year an within the extended period of the said stay order the Rule is going to be disposed of. 

7. The Rule is resisted by the defendant opposite parties filing a counter affidavit. 8. Mr AKM Shamsul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner assailing the impugned judgment and order dated 20-11-2018 submits that the learned District Judge committed serious illegality in passing the order of local inspection, the District Judge had no jurisdiction to act as the Court of trial, the District Judge sitting and exercising the Revisional jurisdiction cannot perform the act of the trial Court. 

9. He adds that the District Judge will adjudicate whether the order of the trial Court in rejecting the prayer for local investigation was lawful or not but the First Revisional Court without examining the said order passed an order of local inspection, as such, the 1st Revisional Court committed an error of law resulted an error in decision occasioning failure of justice to the plaintiff petitioner. 

10. The learned Advocate also submits that plaintiffs filed the original suit for permanent injunction comprising an area of 0.42 acres of land which is the part and parcel of the extended portion of the dwelling but of the plaintiffs where there is now horticulture and garden but the defendants under the garb of either by the local investigation or local inspection have been trying to establish their possession into the suit land which is not permissible in law as the possession of a particular land should be ascertained by the oral evidence adducing in Court and not by any investigation or inspection report. 

11. The learned Advocate also submits that between the same parties there were litigations where the defendants had lost their case but even then since they have been disturbing the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs, the plaintiffs under some compelling circumstances filed the suit. 

12. The learned Advocate also submits that the First Revisional Court allowed the prayer for a local inspection without assigning any reasons whatsoever. She simply articulated in the impugned order that the learned Advocate for the plaintiffs have no objection if the prayer for local inspection is allowed but in fact, the engaged Advocate for the plaintiffs did not give his such consent for passing an order of local inspection and the said engaged Advocate has sworn an affidavit to that effect. 

13. The learned Advocate in his concluding submissions submits that the 1st
Revisional Court by a very nonspeaking order allowed the prayer for local inspection, so the order is liable to be set-aside. 

14. On the other hand, Mr Mahfuzur Rahman Roman, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant opposite parties submits that the 1st Revisional Court in the impugned order assigned sufficient reasons as to why she allowed the prayer for local inspection. The 1st Revisional Court categorically stated that for the quick disposal of the suit and as well as for a proper adjudication of the suit she allowed the prayer for local inspection instead of local investigation filed by the defendants, so in no way the impugned order can be designated as a non-speaking order. 

15. He next submits that the 1st Revisional Court in exercising its revisional jurisdiction can pass any order for the proper adjudication of the dispute between the parties and the 1st Revisional Court in exercising of its lawful jurisdiction very rightly allowed the prayer for local inspection for the determination of the disputes between the parties of the suit. 

16. The learned Advocate also submits that the plaintiffs have been claiming very strongly that the suit land measuring an area of 0.42 acres is the part and parcel of their homestead while the defendants have been claiming from the very beginning of the suit that the suit land is the part and parcel of a local school and there are some establishment of the school in question within the suit land. Since regarding the nature and character of the suit land there is a gulf of difference in the claim the plaintiffs and defendants the 1st Revisional Court for not assessing the possession of the parties rather for the assessing of the nature and character of the suit land allowed the prayer for local inspection and it is the settled principle of law that through the local inspection the nature and character of the suit land can be ascertained, so the 1st Revisional Court below did not commit any error of law and fact in passing the order of local inspection in exercising her revisional jurisdiction, so the impugned order does not call for any interference from this Court. 

17. I have considered the above submissions of the learned Advocates of both the parties and have gone through the materials on record. At the time of hearing of this Rule many submissions have come from both the parties. The plaintiff petitioner submits that between the same parties there was a previous suit where the present defendants had lost the said case but thereafter since they were disturbing in the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land, they have been constrained to file the present suit. 

18. On the other hand, the learned Advocate for the defendant opposite parties contended that the suit land is not specified and for a non specified land there cannot be any permanent or temporary injunction. 

19. It is also submitted very strongly on behalf of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that since before the 1st Revisional Court the question was whether the order of refusal of local investigation by the trial Court was justified or not but the 1st Revisional Court without addressing the said issue passed the order of local inspection, so the order of the learned District Judge is suffering from gross illegality occasioning failure of justice to the plaintiff petitioner.

20. In my consideration since this revision under section 115(4) of the Code has been preferred by the plaintiff petitioner being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order passed by the learned District Judge as 1st Revisional Court directing for a local inspection of the suit land to ascertain two points mentioned in the application dated 15-11-2018. This Revisional Court should examine the legality and propriety of the said order. 

21. The 1st strong argument advanced by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner is that the 1st Revisional Court had no scope and jurisdiction for passing an order of local inspection as a Court of 1st instance as has been made in this particular case. In answering this proposition of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties referred the case of Md Shahjahan Khan vs Additional Deputy Commissioner, Munshiganj reported in 11 BLT (AD) at page 60 where in it has been said that there is no limit to area in which the revisional power is to be exercised by the High Court Division in the facts and circumstances of the each case. The observation of the Appellate Division made in the judgment is given hereunder: 
"It is well settled that once the conditions in section 115(1) of Code of Civil Procedure are satisfied and the High Court's jurisdiction to interfere is established, the proceedings as a whole from start to finish can be scrutinized and any order necessary for doing justice may be passed. There is no limit to the area in which the revisional power is to be exercised by the High Court Division in the facts and circumstances of the each case."(para 4 of the judgment) 

22. From the aforesaid observation of the Appellate Division it appears that the High Court Division can pass any order in exercising its revisional jurisdiction depending on the facts and circumstances of each case. In my consideration the same analogy is also applicable for the 1st Revisional Court also. 

23. However, in my consideration the District Judge in his revsional jurisdiction can pass any order to prevent the failure of justice. In this particular case there is a strong dispute between the parties regarding the nature and character of the suit land. The plaintiffs have been canvassing strongly that the suit land is the part and parcel of their homestead having some horticulture therein while the contesting defendants have also been asserting that the suit land is the part and parcel of a local school. So regarding the nature and character of the suit land there is a gulf of difference in the claim of the parties. 

24. It is fact that possession of a suit land should not be and cannot be ascertained by local investigation or local inspection but where there is a strong dispute between the parties regarding the nature and character of the suit land the same can and should be ascertained through local inspection and in that view of the matter the 1st Revisional Court in order to ensure the ends of justice passed the order of local inspection instead of local investigation. 

25. From the reported case of 45 DLR page 421 it appears that in a suit the plaintiff prayed for declaration that the Hiba-bil-ewaj deed 24-5-1986 was inoperative and is of no legal effect but there was also a prayer to the effect that the defendant opposite party No. 1 had not acquired any title over schedule 'ka' land which is purported to have been transferred by the said deed in favour of opposite party No. 1 by opposite party No. 2. 

26. In the plaint there was further allegation that the gift had not been acted upon. On the other hand in written statement defendant opposite party No. 1 made specific case to the effect that the deed in question had been acted upon and in consultation with opposite party No. 2 she had laid foundation of a school building and created four additional rooms on the existing building. 

27. In the above facts of the case, this division observed in the following manner in the reported case: 
"In view of the averments made by the contesting parties it appears that in order to ascertain whether the deed gift in question had been acted upon or not i.e. whether the possession had already been delivered to the donee is a material one as because if it is found that possession had been delivered and the done is in actual possession of the gifted land then a legal question as regards the form of the suit may be taken up by the contesting defendant. Under the circumstances I find that the local inspection of the gifted land as mentioned in the petition by the plaintiff-petitioner was neither irrelevant nor unnecessary. Rather it appears that it is necessary to avoid future complication". (Para 3). 

28. From the reported case it appears that to ascertain the nature and character of the suit land and also to avoid future complication an order for local inspection was passed by the Revisional Court. I find it difficult to take any different view from that of the reported case over and again where there is a sharp contradiction between the parties regarding the nature and character of the suit land it will be just and proper to ascertain the nature and character of the suit land through a local inspection and in that view of the matter the District Judge committed no error of fact and law in passing the impugned order for local inspection but in my consideration the terms and condition of the local inspection should be changed. 

29. The inspection should be only for the determination of the nature and character of the suit land. It can safely be said that whenever the conflicting parties have been asserting the different versions regarding the nature and character of the suit land, the local inspection may not be the last but the least resort to address the issue and having regards to the above discussion I find no merit in the Rule. 

30. In the result, the Rule is discharged with the modification of the impugned order. The local inspection will be held to determine the nature and character of the suit land only. The trial Court is directed to issue a commission for local inspection to ascertain the nature and character of the suit land only. 

Let a copy of this judgment and order to the Courts below for information and necessary action. 

End.

caseno: Value Added Tax Appeal No. 05 of 2020.
lawyer:
Fatema Anwar, Advocate—For the Appellant. 
Samarendra Nath Biswas, DAG with Md Abul Kalam Khan Daud, AAG with Rehana Sultana, AAG with Md Ali Akbar Khan, AAG with Nurunnahar, AAG—For the Respondent-government.
parties:
Robi Axiata Limited -------- Appellant
VS
Customs, Excise and j VAT Appellate Tribunal and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Farah Mahbub, J: Robi Axiata Limited as appellant has preferred the instant VAT appeal bearing VAT Appeal No.05 of 2020 under section 42(1) of the Value Added Tax Act, 1991(in short, the Act,1991) on 23-1-2020 against the judgment and order dated 14-11-2019 passed by the respondent No. 1, Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal under Nothi No. CEVT/Case(VAT)-42/2018 dismissing the appeal under section 42(1)(kha) of the said Act, 1991 and thereby affirming the order dated 20-11-2017 passed by the respondent No.2, Commissioner, Large Tax Unit-VAT under Nothi No. 4 /LTU-Mushak /BOA /36/Robi Axiata-SIM Replacement/17/1796 issued under section 55(3) of the Act, 1991 demanding Taka 28,52,090,535.07 as VAT and supplementary duty from the appellant. 

2. After the case has been registered as VAT Appeal No.05 of 2020 the matter duly appeared in the cause list of this Court on 23-11-2020 at the instance of the appellant with a prayer for submission of required number of paper books on being prepared since connected LCR has already been made available before this Court along with the said appeal. Allowing the said prayer this Court vide order dated 23-11-2020 directed the appellant to prepare and submit required number of paper books with the concerned section of this Court within 4(four) weeks from the said date. However, while finalizing the said order it came to the notice of this Court that the impugned judgment and order dated 14-11-2019 has been passed by the respondent No.1, Appellate Tribunal concerned after promulgation of the "মূল্য সংযোজন কর ও সম্পূরক শুল্ক আইন, ২০১২" (Act No. 47 of 2012) which came into operation on 1-6-2019.1n that view of the matter maintainability of the instant appeal has been cropped up, for, vide section 124 of the said Act of 2012 the Legislature has now created forum of revision for challenging the order passed by the Appellate Tribunal on and after 1-6-2019. Accordingly, today the matter has been posted in the cause list for hearing on the maintainability of the instant appeal. 

3. Ms. Fatema Anwar, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant in this regard submits that in the instant case the original proceedings under section 55(1) of the VAT Act, 1991 has been initiated long before promulgation of the Act, 2012 and that the final demand was also made by the respondent No. 2 on 20-11-2017 under section 55(3) of the Act, 1991. Challenging the said final demand the appellant preferred respective appeal before the Appellate Tribunal bearing No. CEVT/Case (VAT)-42/2018 in due compliance of law with deposit of 10% of the demanded amount to the government treasury. However, said appeal was ultimately dismissed by the respondent No.1 vide order dated 14-11-2019 .Hence, the instant appeal. 

4. In this connection referring to section 137 of the Act, 2012 she goes to argue that section 137(2)(ga) of the said Act clearly provides that any matter, if remains unresolved, shall be resolved under the VAT Act, 1991 as if VAT Act, 1991 has not been repealed. Accordingly, she submits that the impugned demand regarding SIM replacement having been emanated from the previous VAT Act, 1991 as such, pursuant to section 137(2)(ga) of the Act, 2012 this matter is to be resolved under the Act, 1991, not under the Act, 2012. Hence, she submits that instant appeal, filed under section 42(1)(ga) of the Act, 1991 is maintainable. 

5. She also goes to argue that in the present case appeal before the Appellate Tribunal concerned was filed on 18-2-2018 and that it was heard by the said appellate authority substantially on 19-3-2019, 28-4-2019 and 11-6-2019 respectively. While the appellant was awaiting final decision and order, the Tribunal was re-constituted; consequently, the appeal was heard afresh on 17-9-2019 and that the final hearing of the said appeal took place on 27-9-2019. Later, the impugned judgment and order was passed by the Tribunal concerned on 14-11-2019. 

6. As such, she submits that despite conclusion of hearing of the appeal on 11-6-2019 i.e. prior to promulgation of the Act, 2012 hearing of the matter was taken up afresh on 17-9-2019 and 27-9-2019 respectively by the re-constituted Bench of the Tribunal with the passing of the impugned judgment and order on 14-11-2019 i.e., after promulgation of the Act No. 47 of 2012. In the stated circumstances, the appellant cannot be prejudiced by application of section 124 of the Act, 2012 and thereby to deposit 10% of the demanded amount in order to challenge the said impugned order dated 14-11-2019 passed by the Appellate Tribunal. In this connection, she also submits that on similar issues another appeal of the appellant bearing No. CEVT/Case(VAT)-42/2018 was filed before the said Tribunal on the same date i.e. on 18-2-2018, which was duly disposed of by the Tribunal vide order dated 28-5-2018 i.e. before promulgation of the Act, 2012 whereas the appeal bearing No. (VAT)-42/2018 was held up, dragged on and delayed by the respondent No. 1 itself for no fault of the appellant. As such, she submits that on the said count as well the appellant cannot be put at a different stand. 

7. Ms. Fatema further goes to argue that right of appeal is a substantive right and it vests on the suitor at the time of initiation of the original proceedings. Accordingly, she submits that this right of appeal cannot affected by any change in the law after the institution of original proceedings, as the change of law is to operate prospectively in respect of the original proceedings which has been initiated before the change of law has come into effect. In support she has referred the decisions of the cases of Colonial Sugar and Refining Co. vs Irving reported in (1905) AC 363, Messers Hossein Kasam Dada vs The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 1953 AIR 221, the case of Barikapati Veerayn vs N. Subbiah Choudhury, reported in 1957 AIR 540, the case of State of Bombay vs Supreme General Films Exchange reported in 1960 AIR 980; also the case of Md Nazimuddin vs the State, reported in 30 DLR 49, the case of Parvin Akther vs Bangladesh and others, reported in 70 DLR 413 and the case of BRAC vs National Board of Revenue and others reported in 14 BLC 593. 

8. In view of the decisions, as referred to above she submits that section 124 of the Act, 2012 prescribing condition of deposit of an amount for maintaining the revisional application being prospective in effect since in express terms its retrospectively has not been given as such, it cannot affect an appeal from a proceeding initiated before enactment of this new law. 

9. Per contra, Mr Samarendra Nath Biswas, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the respondent government submits that vide section 42 of the VAT Act, 1991 the Legislature has created forum of appeal before the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh; however, vide section 137(1) of the Act No.47 of 2012 the VAT Act, 1991 has been repealed in its entirety with effect from 1-6-2019.

10. In this regard, he submits that on a plain reading of the preamble of the Act, 1991 as well as Act, 2012 it becomes evident that the Legislature with an intention to expand the periphery of imposition of tax and to make the process of realization of tax easier has enacted Act No. 47 of 2012 with effect from 1-6-2019 by repealing the earlier one and at the same time by incorporating section 124 they have created the forum of revision for challenging the order passed by the Tribunal/or Board, as the case may be. In this connection, he goes to argue that while incorporating sections 121 and 122 of the Act, 2012 in order to prefer appeal before the Commissioner (Appeal) and the Appellate Tribunal, as the case may be, the Legislature has used the words "এই আইন বা ততোধীন প্রণীত বিধিমালার অধীন", but with intention those words have not been incorporated in section 124 of the Act, 2012 only for the reason to extend the periphery of jurisdiction of revision over the disputes under the Act, 1991 as well as Act, 2012. Moreover, vide section 137(2)(ga) of the Act, 2012 if any proceeding is pending those will be regulated as per the provisions of the repealed Act i.e., Act, 1991. However, whenever the proceeding has been disposed of by the Appellate Tribunal the remedy lies only under revisional jurisdiction under section 124 of the Act, 2012, not under section 42(1)(ga) of the Act, 1991. 

11. He further submits that section 124(2) of the Act, 2012 provides applicability of the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure. Accordingly, this Hon'ble Court while exercising revisional jurisdiction has wide power in adjudicating the dispute by perusing the records, consider the evidence, even the respective contending parties can adduce additional evidence, if so requires, so that the litigant will not be prejudiced in any manner whatsoever. 

12 In this regard, referring to the observations so made by the Appellate Division in the case of BRAC vs National Board of Revenue and others reported in 14 BLC (AD) 113 he submits that the effect of repeal or amendment in the procedural law is that in the pending cases the new procedural law will apply as because as a general rule, alterations in the form of procedure are retrospective unless there is some contrary provision in the repealing or amending enactment. In that view of the matter he submits that since section 124 of the Act, 2012 is applicable in the case of the appellant for challenging the judgment and order dated 14-11-2019 passed by the Appellate Tribunal as such, preferring appeal before this Hon'ble Court under section 42(1)(ga) of the Act, 1991 for challenging the said order is not maintainable and hence, it is liable to be dismissed. 

13. Moot question which has cropped up for consideration is whether forum invoked by the appellant by preferring appeal under section 42(1)(ga) of the Act No. 22 of 1991 for challenging the impugned judgment and order dated 14-11-2019 passed by the Appellate Tribunal is maintainable in view of section 124 of the Act, 2012 which came into operation on 1-6-2019.
