18. In other words, appeal under sections 121 or 122 is maintainable when the same is preferred challenging the order passed under the Act, 2012 or the Rules so framed thereunder. 

19 Conversely, vide section 124 the Legislature has created a new forum i.e. revision in place of forum of appeal, to be invoked before the High Court Division for challenging the order passed by the Appellate Tribunal and at the same time made the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 applicable. Section 124 of the said Act is accordingly quoted as under— 
“[১২৪ । হাইকোর্ট বিভাগে রিভিশন —(১) বোর্ড বা আপীলাত ট্রাইব্যুনালের আদেশ দ্বারা সংক্ষুব্ধ ব্যক্তি বা কমিশনার বা মহাপরিচালক পদমর্যাদার নিচে নহেন, এমন কোন মৃসক কর্মকর্তা, উক্ত আদেশের আইনগত প্রশ্নে বাংলাদেশ সুগ্রীম কোর্টের হাইকোর্ট বিভাগে বিভিশনের আবেদন দাখিল করিতে পারিবেন
(২) আপাতত বলবৎ অন্য কোন আইনের যাহা কিছু থাকুক না কেন, উক্ত রিভিশনের বিষয়ে, যতদুর সম্ভব দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধির বিধানাবলী প্রযোজ্য হইবে ।
(৩) উপ-ধারা (১) এর অধীন হাইকোর্ট বিভাগে রিভিশনের আবেদন দাখিলের ক্ষেত্রে, তামাদি আইন, ১৯০৮ এর ধারা প্রযোজ্য হইবে ।
(৪) মুসক কর্মকর্তা ব্যতীত, অন্য কোন ব্যক্তি কর্তৃক উপ-ধারা (১) এর অধীন হাইকোর্ট বিভাগে রিভিশনের আবেদন দাখিলের ক্ষেত্রে, তাহাকে তর্কিত আদেশে উল্লিখিত প্রদেয় করের বা জরিমানার ১০(দশ) শতাংশ অর্থ পরিশোধ করিতে হইবে ।”

20. On careful examination of section 124 it appears that like sections 121 or 122 of the Act, 2012 the Legislature did not use the words " এই আইন বা ততোধীন প্রণীত বিধিমালার অধীন প্রদত্ত কোন আদেশ বা সিদ্ধান্ত”, rather has used the words "বোর্ড বা আপীলাত ট্রাইব্যুনাল এর আদেশ …. " However, while giving the definition of “আপীলাত ট্রাইব্যুনাল" in section 2(14) of the Act, 2012 the Legislature did not use the words “এই আইন এর অধীন গঠিত ট্রাইব্যুনাল”; rather, "আপীলাত ট্রাইব্যুনাল" has been defined as-

“২.। সংজ্ঞা ।___বিষয় বা প্রসঙ্গের পরিপন্থী কোন কিছু না থাকিলে, এই আইনে,

[(১8) আপীলাত ট্রাইব্যুনাল অর্থ Customs Act, 1969 এর section 196 এর অধীন গঠিত শুল্ক, আবগারি ও মূল্য সংযোজন কর আপীলাত ট্রাইবুন্যাল;]”

21. In view of the preamble of the Act, 2012 “……মুল্য সংযোজন কর, সম্পূরক শুল্ক এবং টার্ন ওভার কর আরোপের ক্ষেত্র বিস্তৃতকরণ এবং কর আদায় প্রক্রিয়া সহজীকরণ....”
 it is abundantly clear that the Leghislature has widen the scope of the application of section 124 of the Act, 2012. In other words, forum under section 124 has not been delimited within the order passed under section 122 of the Act, 2012, but it has also been made applicable for challenging the impugned order passed on and from 1-6-2019 (the date on which Act No. 47 of 2012 came into operation) despite the fact that proceeding has been initiated and disposed of under the Act of 1991. Said findings of ours are also fortified from section 137 of the Act, 2012, which provides as under:— 

“১৩৭ । রহিতকরণ ও হেফাজত।১) এই আইন প্রবর্তনের সঙ্গে সঙ্গে মূল্য সংযোজন কর আইন, ১৯৯১ (১৯৯১ সনের ২২ নং আইন) রহিত হইবে ।
(২) উক্ত আইন রহিত হওয়া সত্ত্বেও-
(ক) উক্ত আইনের অধীন কৃত ৰা গৃহীত ব্যবস্থা, সামঞ্জস্যপূর্ণ হওয়া সাপেক্ষে, এই আইনের অধীন কৃত বা গৃহীত হইয়াছে বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে;
(খ) উক্ত আইনের অধীন প্রণীত সকল বিধি, প্রদত্ত সকল আদেশ, জারিকৃত সকল প্রজ্ঞাপণ বা নোটিশ এই আইনের বিধানাবলীর সহিত সামঞ্জস্যপূর্ণ হওয়া সাপেক্ষে, রহিত বা সংশোধিত না হওয়া পর্যন্ত, বলবৎ থাকিবে এবং এই আইনের অধীন প্রণীত, প্রদত্ত বা জারিকৃত হইয়াছে বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে:
(গ) উক্ত আইন ছারা বা উহার অধীন আরোপিত কোন কর বা ফিস বা অন্য কোন পাওনা, এই আইন প্রবর্তনের অব্যবহিত পূর্বে অনাদায়ী থাকিলে, উহা উক্ত আইন অনুযায়ী আদায় করা হইবে, এবং কোন বিষয় অনিষ্পন্ন থাকিলে, তাহা উক্ত আইন অনুযায়ী নিষ্পন্ন হইবে যেন উক্ত আইন রহিত হয় নাই।”

22. Vide 137(1) of the Act, 2012, Act No. 22 of 1991 has been repealed in its entirety. But despite repeal of the said Act vide sub-section 2(ga) if any matter inclusive proceedings remains pending on the date of promulgation of the Act, 2012 said proceedings shall be disposed of under the repealed Act, 1991. Like, the appeal bearing No. CEVT/Case(VAT)- 42/2018 preferred by the appellant under section 42(1)(kha) of the Act,1991 has been disposed of by the Appellate Tribunal tinder the Act, 1991 vide order dated 14-11-2019. However, since meanwhile Act No. 47 of 2012 has come into operation with effect from 1-6-2019 as such, for challenging the order dated 14-11-2019 passed by the Appellate Tribunal the appellant is required to invoke the forum of revision created by the Legislature under section 124 of the Act, 2012, not under section 42 (1)(ga) of the Act, 1991 on the plea of initiation of the proceedings under the repealed Act.

23. In this regard, it is pertinent to observe that this right to revision under the Act, 2012 is a substantive right of the aggrieved person to place its respective grievances before the High Court Division against the order of the Appellate Tribunal passed on 1-6-2019 or subsequent thereafter under the Act, 1991 as well as the Act, 2012 respectively. In other words, with the creation of revisional forum by the Legislature the right of the aggrieved party to challenge the impugned order dated 14-11-2019 passed by the Appellate Tribunal has not been curtailed, rather with the application of the Code of Civil Procedure vide section 124(3) the periphery of section 124 has been widen coupled with the application of section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 and thereby has created scope for condonation of delay in preferring revision, which was absent in the repealed Act, 1991 while preferring appeal under section 42(1)(ga) of the Act, 1991. 

24. In view of our above observations and findings, the decisions so have been relied upon by the appellant have no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the present case and the position of law, as discussed above. 

25. However, the main concern of the appellant for opposing application of section 124 is the condition imposed by the Legislature under section 124(4) of the Act, 2012 as to payment of "এই তর্কিত আদেশে উল্লেখিত প্রদেয় করের বা জরিমানার ১০% (দশ) শতাংশ অর্থ…”for filing revision before the High Court Division. In this regard, relying upon the observations of the Appellate Division so made in the case of BRAC vs National Board of Revenue and others reported in 14 BLC (AD) 113 we have no manner of doubt to find that that the provision of sub-section(4) of section 124 of the Act, 2012 as to the requirement to pay 10% of the "প্রদেয় কর বা জরিমানা ", a condition precedent for filing revision, is merely a matter of procedural law and that procedural law has always have retrospective effect. 

26. Be that as it may, it can clearly be discerned that filing the instant appeal under section 42(1)(ga) of the Act,1991 for challenging the impugned judgment and order dated 14-11-2019 passed by the Appellate Tribunal is not maintainable. 

27. Accordingly, this appeal is dismissed as being not maintainable. 

28. The unsigned order dated 23-11-2020 is hereby re-called. 

29. There will be no order as to costs. 

Send down the LCR at once. 

End.

lawyer:
Shafique Ahmed, Senior Advocate with Mahbub Shafique and Md Azizul Bashar, Advocates—For the Petitioner. 

Nawroz Md Rasel Chowdhury, DAG with MMG Sarwar; AAG and Ashique Rubaiat, AAG—For the Respondent Nos. 2 and 3.

M Khaled Ahmed, Advocate—For the Respondent No. 6.
parties:
Nazrul and Brothers Limited ---- Petitioner
vs
Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Forest and Environment and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Mozibur Rahman Miah, J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to the Memo No. 22.02.0000.091. 001.4331.প্রশা:-797 dated 11-6-2018 issued under the signature of the respondent No. 4 as evidenced by Annexure-'K' to the writ petition should not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, this Court also stayed the operation of the above mentioned impugned Memo for a period of 6(six) months. The said order of stay was lastly extended on 2-12-2019 for another 6(six) months. 

3. The salient facts leading to issuance of the instant Rule are: The petitioner is a limited company registered with Joint Stock Company, Bangladesh which was setup with the objective of producing, manufacturing, purchasing and selling of tar (Alkatra) as well as Naphthalene be zone pitch, creosote oil, road tear and allied products and other chemicals for industrial and other purposes. He procured licence from the office of the Chief Inspector of Factories and also procured the trade licence from Dhaka City Corporation and renewed the same up-to-date. He has also registered its company in the office of the Board of Investment, Prime Minister's Office, Government of Bangladesh. The petitioner has been running the company very effectively by producing tar, pitch and Naphthalene as the bi-product of tar and marketing it in the local market as well as exporting it to abroad with very good reputation. The petitioner has procured Environment Clearance Certificate from the office of the respondent No. 2 containing Memo No. পরিবেশ/ঢা বি/ ৪৩৩১/৮৫৮ dated 5-4-2003 which was renewed on 1-11-2017 up to 5-4-2018. Thereafter, the petitioner on 29-3-2018 filed an application to the office of the respondent No. 2 for renewal of the environment clearance certificate by depositing requisite fees. While the petitioner was running his factory peacefully by producing the authorized goods and marketing the same in local and foreign market, all of a sudden, the respondent No. 3 on 1-11-2017 issued a letter asking him to control bad smell (odour) of the bi-product, naphthalene by applying proper technology within 6(six) months. The petitioner on 11-10-2017 then wrote a letter to the Director, BRTC, Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (shortly, BUET), Dhaka requesting them to introduce modern technique and system in the factory for controlling the smell of naphthalene. In reply to the said letter of the petitioner dated 11-10-2017, the Chemical Engineering Department of BRTC, BUET by its letter dated 15-10-2017 apprised him that, the solution of removal of odour of naphthalene can be mitigated and sent a quotation asking him to deposit an amount of Taka 4, 02,500 for accomplishing the job and the petitioner deposited the sum to Bangladesh Bank on 15-10-2017. In view of the said measure to be taken by BUET the petitioner then informed the development to the respondent No. 2 by a letter dated 16-10-2017 informing it that, BUET has agreed to take measures for removal of the odour (smell) of naphthalene. However, though the BUET agreed to install the odour removal system in the industry within 6(six) months, but it could not complete the installation within the specified period and the petitioner then on 5-4-2018 sent another letter requesting the respondent No. 2 to extend the time for installing odour removal system. In spite of the said request, respondent No. 2 on 20-5-2018 issued a letter asking the petitioner to show cause within 7(seven) days as to why legal action should not be taken against him as per the Bangladesh Environment Conservation Act, 1995 which the petitioner received on 24-6-2018. The petitioner then replied to that notice on 26-6-2018 requesting it to exonerate him from the said charge. It has further been stated that, though the show cause notice was issued on 20-5-2018 but it was posted on 12-6-2018 which the petitioner received on 24-6-2018 yet, the respondent No. 2 issued the impugned letter on 11-6-2018 directing the petitioner to stop production of naphthalene as a bi-product of tar until and unless the odour removal system is installed which has been impugned in the instant writ petition. 

4. Mr Shafique Ahmed, the learned senior counsel along with Mr Mahbub Shafique, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner upon taking us to the writ petition and all the annexure appended therewith, at the very outset submits that, the petitioner has been running the industry by registering the same with the Register of Joint Stock Company obtaining all necessary permission required for running the same specially on getting environment clearance certificate from respondent No. 2 and, as such, question of issuing the impugned letter dated 11-6-2018 directing the petitioner to stop production of naphthalene until the odour is removed and the system for containing it is installed is not lawful and liable to be declared illegal and without lawful authority. 

5. The learned counsel next contends that, the respondent No. 2 issued show cause notice on 20-5-2018 but the said letter was posted on 12-6-2018 and reached the petitioner on 24-6-2018 but before receiving the said show cause notice, the impugned letter dated 11-6-2018 was issued which is not lawful and beyond the principle of natural justice and, as such, it is liable to be declared illegal and without lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

6. The learned counsel further contends that, the impugned letter has been issued by the respondent No. 4, Director, Directorate of Environment directing the petitioner to stop production of naphthalene without making any investigation and finding report thereof as per section 4(5) of the Bangladesh Environment Conservation Act, 1995 (hereinafter referred to as "the Ain") which is totally illegal and cannot be sustained in law. 

7. The learned counsel goes on to submit that, naphthalene is a very useful product for its smell for using as insecticide and paste control and also for other purposes when no standard for the smell (odour) has yet been settled by law fixing up to what unit of the odour is tolerable and, as such, without ascertaining the tolerable standard of smell, the issuance of impugned letter is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

8. The learned counsel also contends that, in schedule 8 of পরিবেশ সংরক্ষন বিধিমালা, ১৯৯৭ (hereinafter referred to as the 'rule'), the standard of odour of certain items have been specified but in the said schedule of the rule, the name of naphthalene has not been mentioned and, as such, the production of the same goods cannot be stopped by any reason whatsoever and, as such, the impugned letter dated 11-6-2018 should be declared illegal and without lawful authority. 

9. The learned counsel further contends that, the petitioner has set up the industry in the declared industrial area on his own plot getting all sorts of licence and permission from the respective authority and renewed the licence up to 5-4-2018 and the petitioner has already applied for further renewal on depositing required fees which is under consideration and measures for the removal of odour has already been adopted by the BUET and in such a development, the issuance of the impugned letter for stopping the production is not lawful and beyond the principle of natural justice and, as such, the impugned letter should be declared illegal. 

10. The learned counsel lastly contends that, more than 1000 workers are working in the industry and if the production of the industry is stopped, then all of them will render jobless and the country will also face very dangerous consequence for want of naphthalene and, as such, the impugned letter dated 11-6-2018 is liable to be declared illegal. 

11. However, in support of his assertion, the learned counsel cited a plethora of decisions firstly, in the case of Assessing Officer, Narayanganj Ranges vs Burmah Eastern Limited reported in 1981 BLD (AD) 450 = 34 DLR (AD) 29, an unreported judgment passed in civil appeal No. 54 of 2001 that corresponds civil petition for leave to appeal No. 9 of 2001 dated 03-12-2003 both appeared in an online legal journal named, Manupatra; another unreported judgment passed in Writ Petition No. 50 of 1985 dated 09-6-1988 also appeared in Manupatra; decision in the case of Farid Uddin Mahmud vs Md Saidur Rahman, reported in 2011 BLD (AD) 79; judgment passed dated 9-4-1997 in Civil Appeal No. 5 of 1996 of the Appellate Division appeared in Manupatra; decision in the case of Abu Jafar Md Nurul Islam vs DG, Department of Environment, Government of Bangladesh reported in 56 DLR I and decision reported in 15 BLC 770. With above submissions and relying on those decisions, the learned counsel finally prays for making the Rule absolute. 

12. In contrast, the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 by filing an affidavit-in-opposition as well as supplementary affidavit-in-opposition opposes the contention taken in the writ petition asserting, inter alia, that, the petitioner got the environment clearance certificate from respondent No. 2 and it was renewed up to 5-4-2018 by letter dated 01-11-2017 and in condition (V) to the said clearance certificate it has clearly been outlined that " “আগামী ৬(ছয়) মাসের মধ্যে উপযুক্ত কার্যকরী প্রযুক্তি/সিস্টেম স্থাপন করে কারখানার বাইপ্রোডাক্ট হিসেবে উৎপন্ন ন্যাপথলিনের গন্ধ নিয়ন্ত্রণ/ অপসারণ নিশ্চিত করে অত্র দপ্তরকে লিখিতভাবে অবহিত করতে হবে”. In addition to that, in condition (a) it has been also mentioned, “উপর্যুক্ত শর্ত এবং পরিবেশগত ছাড়পত্রের প্রদত্ত অন্যান্য শর্তাবলী প্রতিপালনে ব্যর্থ হলে ছাড়পত্র বাতিল বলে গণ্য হবে এবং পরিবেশ সংরক্ষণ আইন, ১৯৯৫ (সংশোধিত-২০১০) এবং পরিবেশ সংরক্ষণ বিধিমালা, ১৯৯৭ অনুযায়ী আইনগত ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করা হবে” and therefore, the Department of Environment provided clear instruction earlier and even cautioned the petitioner when it issued renewal certificate.

13. The learned Deputy Attorney-General (shortly, DAG) by referring to the said affidavit-in-opposition also contends that, a complaint was filed against the petitioner in the Ministry of Environment and Forest as well as to the head office of the Department of Environment by the President of Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (shortly, BGMEA) and in response to that, those offices vide their letter dated 9-11-2016 and 22-11-2016 asked the concerned authority to take action on proper investigation of the allegations levelled by BGMEA. Accordingly, the Department of Environment conducted an investigation on the above mentioned complaint and issued a letter on 22-12-2016 to the petitioner asking it to take necessary measures to control bad odour and other inconvenience but no visible action has been taken by the petitioner in spite of giving that reminder having no illegality in the impugned letter. 

14. The learned DAG by referring to paragraph No. 17 of the writ petition also contends that, naphthalene is the bi-product of the factory run by the petitioner and it wafts bad smell which pollutes the environment in the industrial zone something to be controlled as per schedule 8 of the rule no matter there has been no specific standard for naphthalene therein. 

15. It has further been contended by the learned DAG with reference to the affidavit-in-opposition that, the Dhaka Metropolitan Office of the Department of Environment also conducted an inspection on the complaints made by the BGMEA and acting on that allegation, it issued a letter to the petitioner on 22-12-2016 asking him to take necessary measures to control the bad odour and other hazardous objects produced at the petitioner's factory and upon completion of inspection by the concerned official of the respondent No. 2, it found the complaint to be true. 

16. The learned DAG further contends that, as the petitioner's activities has been causing serious threats to the environment, the Department of Environment renewed the Environment Clearance Certificate (ECC) on condition that, the petitioner would install necessary equipments to control bad odour within 6(six) months and on failure, the ECC issued will be cancelled and in such a situation, no further notice would required to be issued, so mere absence of specific standard in the rules cannot be any ground for allowing the petitioner to continue damaging activities to the environment. 

17. It has lastly been averred by the learned Deputy Attorney-General that, the Department of Environment is legally bound to conserve environment according to the provision of Article 18(A) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh as well and considering the facts, circumstances and contention placed above, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 18. After filing of the affidavit-in-opposition, the learned DAG also filed a supplementary affidavit-in-opposition by inserting some new facts annexing a circular where it has been asserted that, under section 19(2) of পরিবেশ সংরক্ষন আইন, ১৯৯৫ a circular was issued by the Director General, Directorate of Environment bearing Memo No. পরিবেশ/আইন/বিধিমালা-১৫৯/২০১০/১৭ dated 31-1-2011 (Annexure-'9' to the said supplementary affidavit) delegating power to his subordinate officers on various issues and in serial No. 5 of the said circular, Director General of the said Directorate delegates power to Divisional/Metropolitan/ Laboratory/head of District Office (Director/ Deputy Director/any other officers in-charge of the directorate and by such delegation any Director/Deputy Director or any other officers reserves the authority to act on his behalf having no dispute about exerting authority of respondent No. 4 in issuing the impugned notice. 

19. The learned DAG by annexing another circular issued by respondent No. 1 dated 14-1-2018 (Annexure-'10' to the supplementary-affidavit) also submits that, the writ petition is not maintainable since there is an appellate authority for seeking redress against the impugned action. 

20. In the end, the learned DAG submits that, since there has been an alternative efficacious remedy open to the petitioner to get redress of his grievance by filing appeal as stated above, so the writ petition itself is not maintainable and liable to be discharged. 

21. Per contra, Mr M. Khaled Ahmed, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No. 6 at first filed an application for vacating the order of stay mainly basing on the provision of section 14 of the Ain asserting that, writ will only lie when there remains no efficacious remedy but in the present case, section 14 of the Ain clearly provides the provision of appeal against the grievance of the petitioner and it is clear that without exhausting the said provision of appeal the instant writ has been filed and even though the petitioner has not made any statement as to why he has not resorted to appeal, so the writ petition is not maintainable and the Rule liable to be discharged. 

22. It is worthwhile to mention here that, when we took up the said application, we found it expedient to hear the Rule instead of disposing of the said application and we then fixed the matter for hearing. After filing the said application for vacating the order of stay, the petitioner also filed a supplementary-affidavit where it has been stated that, the Directorate of Environment after investigation in regard to air pollution, issued a show cause notice upon the petitioner on finding some hazardous substance in the factory detrimental to the health of garments workers located adjacent to the petitioner's factory and in sub-clause (ka) and (uma) of clause-1 of the report submitted by the inspection team dated 8-12-2016, the directorate then vide Memo dated 22-12-2016 asked the petitioner to reply the show cause notice by 10-1-2017 as to why his environment clearance certificate would not be cancelled. 

23. However, it has further been submitted by the learned counsel for the respondent No. 6 that, the petitioner has not disclosed about the said Memo dated 22-12-2016 whereupon a show cause notice was issued earlier upon him and the way he has described the show cause notice dated 20-5-2018 has not been done in proper manner rather it invited some disputed question of facts and thereby the petitioner has clearly suppressed the fact. 

24. In this regard the learned counsel contends that, it is now well-settled that, if writ-petitioner suppressed any material facts and try to mislead the court, this Hon`ble court can discharge the Rule on the sole ground of providing some misleading facts before it. 

25. The learned counsel next contends that, the petitioner has not preferred appeal as provided in section 14 of the Ain and the impugned order dated 11-6-2018 has not yet been made final and therefore, the instant writ petition is a pre-mature one and without exhausting the forum of appeal it is hit by "doctrine of exhaustion" and, as such, it is not maintainable. 

26. By filing an affidavit-in-opposition this respondent has also denied the material statement so made in the writ petition contending that, the writ petition is not maintainable because the petitioner has not preferred appeal against the impugned letter dated 11-6-2018 passed by the respondent No. 2 and therefore, the writ petition is not maintainable. 

27. The learned counsel further contends that, the petitioner has brought some disputed questions of facts which cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction because disputed question of facts requires evidence to be adduced by the contending parties for resolving the issue. 

28. The learned counsel next contends that, in so far as regards to the show cause notice dated 20-5-2018 (Annexure-'J' to the writ petition) alleged to have received by the petitioner on 24-6-2018 and that of before replying the said notice dated 26-6-2018, the impugned order has been issued on 11-6-2018 asserted in paragraph Nos. 13 and 14 of the writ petition are all disputed question of facts and a writ court cannot decide any such disputed question of fact and therefore, the writ itself is not maintained. 

29. The learned counsel next submits that, it is the constitutional obligation of the government to ensure the right of people as regard to the protection and improvement of environment for the best welfare of its citizen and in case of breach thereof it should be enforced under Article 102 of the Constitution and this Hon'ble Court is the only instrumental for protecting such right to the affected people and for the welfare of the state as well as its citizen at large, but in the name of producing bi-product what the petitioner is doing totally goes against the express provision enumerated in Article 18A of our Constitution and therefore, the impugned letter has rightly been issued which is liable to be sustained. 

30. However, to buttress the above submissions, the learned counsel has placed his reliance to a slew of decisions, in the case of Controller of Examinations, University of Dhaka Mahinuddin reported in 44 DLR (AD) 305; in the case of Zahur Ahmed vs Commissioner of Customs reported in 51 DLR 206; in the case of Prof Nurul Amin Bepari vs Vice-Chancellor reported in 50 DLR 405; in the case of Gazi M Towfic vs Agrani Bank reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6; in the case of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) vs Artha Rin Adalat reported in 59 DLR (AD) 6; in the case of Moulana Md Abdul Kader Azadi vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 58 DLR 114; in the case of Dr. Moniuddin Farooque, Secretary General, Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers Association (BELA) being dead Ms Syeda Rizwana Hasan, Director (Programme) representing BELA vs Bangladesh and others reported in 55 DLR 69 and in the case of Bangladesh vs Anwar Ahmed reported in 18 BLD (AD) 281 = 51 DLR (AD) 42. The learned counsel finally prays for discharging the Rule. 

31. We have considered the submissions so placed by the learned counsels for the petitioner and those of the respondent Nos. 2-3 and 6. We have also gone through the writ petition, affidavit-in-oppositions and the supplementary-affidavits so filed by the respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 6 as well. Though in the affidavit-in-oppositions and those of the supplementary-affidavits, the respondents have deliberately assailed that, the instant writ petition is not maintainable for having alternative remedy that is to say, petitioner can resort to the appellate forum specified in the AM, yet the petitioner did not bother to advert to said legal assertion by filing any counter-affidavit other than making some verbal submission and by referring to several decisions.

32. However, since it is a legal point, it can be refuted in making verbal submission as well which the learned counsel for the petitioner has resorted to. However, in the four corner of the entire writ petition, there has been no explanation why the petitioner invoked the writ jurisdiction without resorting to the appellate forum—the point raised by respondents remained unanswered. 

33. In such a compelling proximate cause, we in the first place feel it expedient to figure out whether writ itself is maintainable and if on discussing legal aspect involved in this case we find the answer to the negative, we would then refrain from enter into the merit of the case. 

34. As discussed above, this Rule was fixed for hearing in the context of filing an application for vacating the order of stay by the respondent No. 6 where he took a sole ground that, the writ itself is not maintainable as there provides for appeal in section 14 of the Ain. 

35. Now let us reproduce section 14 of the Ain here: 
“১৪ । আপীল ।--(১) এই আইন বা বিধি অনুসারে প্রদত্ত কোন নোটিশ, আদেশ বা নির্দেশ দ্বারা কোন ব্যক্তি সংক্ষুব্ধ ��ইলে তিনি, উক্ত নোটিশ, আদেশ বা নির্দেশ প্রদানের ত্রিশ দিনের মধ্যে সরকার কর্তৃক গঠিত আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট উহার বিরুদ্ধে আপীল করিতে পারিবেন এবং আপীলের উপর উক্ত কর্তৃপক্ষের সিদ্ধান্ত চূড়ান্ত হইবে এবং এইরূপ সিদ্ধান্তের বিরুদ্ধে আদালতে কোল মামলা দায়ের করা যাইবে নাঃ
তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষ যদি এই মর্মে সন্তুষ্ট হয় যে, কোন অনিবার্য কারণে উক্ত সময়ের মধ্যে সংক্ষুব্ধ ব্যক্তি আপীল দায়ের করিতে পারেন নাই, তাহা
হইলে উক্ত কর্তৃপক্ষ আপীল দাখিলের জন্য অতিরিক্ত অনধিক ত্রিশ দিন সময় বৃদ্ধি করিতে পারিবে ।

(২) উপ-ধারা (১) এর অধীন গঠিত আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষ একাধিক সদস্য সমন্বয়ে গঠন করা যাইবেঃ

তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, যদি কোন আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষ একাধিক সদস্য সমন্বয়ে গঠন করা হয়, তাহা হইলে উহার একজন সদস্যকে সরকার উক্ত কর্তৃপক্ষেও চেয়ারম্যান নিযুক্ত করিবে।
(৩) এই ধারার অধীন দায়েরকৃত আপীল দায়েরের তারিখ হইতে তিন মাসের মধ্যে নিষ্পত্তি করা যাইবে ।”
36. Though the said provision provides for appellate authority (আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষ) but we find nothing therein about the composition of the said appellate authority. The learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently raised that shortcomings in the said provision. At this, the learned counsel for the respondents (respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 6), then referred to the provision of rules 9, 10 and 11 of পরিবেশ সংরক্ষন বিধিমালা, ১৯৯৭. 

37. Now let us examine what those provisions provide. They run as follows: 

“৯। আপীল ।-(১) ধারা ১৪ এর অধীন যে নোটিশ, আদেশ বা নির্দেশের বিরুদ্ধে আপীল দায়ের করা হইবে, তৎসম্পর্কে আপত্তির কারণসমূহ সংক্ষেপে ও স্পষ্টভাবে উল্লেখ করিতে হইবে।
(২) প্রত্যেকটি আপীলের সহিত নিন্নবর্ণিত কাগজপত্র থাকিতে হইবে, যথা:

(অ) যে নোটিশ, আদেশ বা নির্দেশের বিরদ্ধে আপীল করা হইতেছে উহার একটি করিয়া প্রমাণকৃত কপি;
(আ) পরিবেশগত ছাড়পত্রের কপি (যদি থাকে),
(ই) আপীল ফি বাবদ এক হাজার টাকা জমা প্রদানের প্রমাণস্বরূপ ট্রেজারী চালান;
এবং
(ঈ) আপীলের সহিত সম্পর্কযুক্ত অন্য কোন কাগজাদি।

১০। আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষ কর্তৃক অনুসরণীয় পদ্ধতি । (১) আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষ তাহাদের অফিসের কার্য ভার এবং প্রতিপক্ষের প্রতি নোটিশ জারীর জন্য প্রয়োজনীয় সময় বিবেচনা করিয়া আপীল শুনানীর জন্য একটি দিন ধার্য করিবে ।

(২) অধিদপ্তরের যে কার্যালয়ের নোটিশ, আদেশ বা নির্দেশের বিরুদ্ধে আপীল দায়ের করা হইয়াছে, সেই কার্যালয় বরাবরে আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষ আপীল শুনানীর তারিখ উল্লেখ করিয়া আপীলের কপিসহ নোটিশ প্রেরণ করিবে।

(৩) আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষ আপীল নিষ্পত্তির সুবিধার্থে প্রয়োজনীয় সকল কাগজ, তথ্যাদি যে কোন সময় আপীলকারী বা প্রতিপক্ষের নিকট হইতে তলব করিতে পারিবে।

১১। আপীল শুনানীকালীন পদ্ধতি ।-(১)শুনানীর জন্য নির্ধারিত তারিখে, অথবা শুনানী মুলতবী হইলে পরবর্তী তারিখে আপীলের সমর্থনে আপীলকারীর বক্তব্য শ্রবণ করা হইবে।

(২) শুনানীর জন্য ধার্য তারিখে অথবা শুনানী মুলতবী হইলে পরবর্তী তারিখে আপীল শুনানীর জন্য ডাক পড়িলে যদি আপীলকারী হাজির না হয়, তাহা হইলে আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষ আপীল খারিজের আদেশ দান করিতে
পারিবে।

(৩) যদি আপীলকারী হাজির হয়, কিন্তু প্রতিপক্ষ হাজির না হয় তবে একতরফভাবে আপীলের শুনানী হইবে।

(৪) যদি উপ-বিধি (২) অনুসারে আপীল খারিজ হয়, তবে আপীলকারী উক্ত খারিজের আদেশ প্রদানের তারিখ হইতে ত্রিশ কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে পুনরায় আপীল মঞ্জুরের জন্য আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট আবেদন করিতে পারিবে ।

(৫) আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষ পক্ষগণ বা কোন এক পক্ষের শুনানীর পর তর্কিত নোটিশ, আদেশ বা নির্দেশ অনুমোদন, রদবদল বা বাতিল করিতে পারিবে।

(৬) আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষ তাহার সিদ্ধান্তের অনুকূলে যুক্তিযুক্ত কারণ লিপিবদ্ধ করিবেন এবং আপীলকারী কি প্রতিকার প্রাপ্য হইবেন তাহা উল্লেখ করিবে।

(৭) আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষ প্রদত্ত আদেশের কপি যথাশীঘ্র সম্ভব আপীলকারী, অধিদপ্তরের সংশ্লিষ্ট কার্যালয় এবং মহাপরিচালক বরাবরে প্রেরণ করা হইবে।

38. However, ongoing through those different rules, we only find, the procedure to be followed by the aggrieved appellant and that of "appellate authority" in disposing of an appeal having no mention of composition of the appellate authority therein. 

39. In such a circumstances, the learned DAG for respondent Nos. 2-3 by annexing a circular dated 14-1-2018 as of Annexure-'10' to the supplementary-affidavit referred to the latest formation of "appellate authority" done as per section 14 of the Ain when the learned counsel for the respondent No. 6 has also referred chronological circulars in that respect ranging from 1997 till the year 2018 through supplying a book titled "পরিবেশ আইন সংকলন" published by respondent No. 2. 

40. So we find from the above circulars that, soon after rule of 1997 (promulgated on 27-8-1997) came into effect, the appellate authority started functioning vide memo No. পবম-৪/৩/২/৯৭/৬১২ তাং ৩-১১-১৯৯৭.

41. At this, the learned counsel for the petitioner raised a question that, the respondent No. 4 has no authority to issue impugned notice by closing the petitioner's factory which can only be done by the respondent No. 2 and in that case, the respondent No. 4 is a quoram non-judice in exercising such power. To refute such assertion, the respondent Nos. 2-3 by annexing a circular as of Annexure- '9' to the supplementary-affidavit asserts that, by virtue of delegation of power by the respondent No. 2 to the respondent No. 4, the impugned notice has been issued which has perfectly been done. 

42. Now, let us examine the legal provision surrounding the point. In that aspect, we feel it urge to reproduce the provision of section 19 of the Ain here, as the circular annexed as of Annexure- '9' to the supplementary-affidavit dated 31-1-2011 has been based on that very section: 
“১৯।ক্ষমতা অর্পণ।– (১) সরকার এই আইন বা বিধির অধীন উহার যে কোন ক্ষমতা মহা-পরিচালক বা অন্য যে কোন কর্মকর্তাকে অর্পণ করিতে পারে।
(২) মহা-পরিচালক এই আইন বা বিধির অধীন তাহার যে কোন ক্ষমতা অধিদপ্তরের ঘে কোন কর্মকর্তাকে অর্পণ করিতে পারিবেন ।”

43. So in view of the above provision, there is no shred of doubt that, the respondent No. 2 can delegate its power to any of its subordinate authority which has been manifested in the said circular and the respondent No. 4 has just issued the impugned notice in compliance with the said provision followed by circular issued thereunder. 

44. Pointing at the said circular dated 31-1-2011, particularly 2nd part of serial No. 5 thereof, Mr Mahbub Shafique, the learned counsel then contends that, since the production of the petitioner's factory has been declared closed vide impugned notice, it was supposed to be issued under section 4(4) of the Ain and should be made with the approval (অনুমোদনক্রমে) of respondent No. 2, but there has been nothing in the impugned letter whether respondent No. 4 has taken any approval from respondent No. 2 before issuing impugned notice and, as such, the same is totally without jurisdiction. 

45. To controvert the said assertion, the learned DAG and that of the learned counsel for the respondent No. 6 submits that, since the point has been raised by the petitioner so the onus lies upon him to prove that no approval was taken by respondent No. 4. In addition to that, the learned DAG contends that, taking approval is absolutely an internal official correspondence between respondent No. 2 and respondent No. 4 and obviously such approval was taken for which the petitioner has no occasion to be prejudiced when he repeatedly flouted the commitment made to those respondents to remediate the bad odour as deliberately found by the respondents. 

46. In this regard, we are of the view that, whether approval had been taken or not that can never be any point-in-issue to be agitated in writ jurisdiction as neither the law nor the rules provides anything contrary to that rather upon denying the alleged assertion raised by the petitioner by the respondent Nos. 2-3 it becomes a disputed question of facts which this court cannot looked into.

47. The petitioner has also raised a factual aspect to the effect that, he received the copy of the show cause notice issued on 20-5-2018 (Annexure-'J' to the writ petition) that posted on 12-6-2018 (paragraph Nos. 13 and 14 to the writ petition) on 24-6-2018 where seven days’ time was given to reply to that letter and replied to the said show cause notice on 26-6-2018 but before receiving so, impugned notice dated 11-6-2018 (Annexure-'K' to the writ petition) was issued which was posted on 14-6-2018. In order to prove those facts, the petitioner also annexed the postal envelope as of Annexure-'J-1' and 'K-1' to the writ petition. 

48. Those very factual aspects are found to have denied by respondent No. 6 in paragraph No. 13 of its affidavit-in-opposition and that of respondent Nos. 2-3 in paragraph No. 18 to the affidavit-in-opposition claiming it to be matter of record to be proved by the petitioner. 

49. Record further shows, in reply to the show cause notice issued on 20-5-2018 and that of the impugned notice dated 11-6-2018, the petitioner asserted to have received both the letters on 21-6-2018 (Anexure-'J-2' to the writ petition). But what we find from the assertion made in paragraph Nos. 13 and 14 of the writ petition as mentioned above, he claimed to have received the show cause notice on 24-6-2018. So, petitioner himself made contradictory statement about the fact of receiving letter having no reason to controvert the said fact by the respondents. Nonetheless, since the petitioner has replied the show cause notice on 26-6-2018 (by Annexure- 'J-2' to the writ petition) then why the petitioner did not take resort to the appellate authority invoking section 14 of the Ain is simply incomprehensible. However, whatever the fact might be with regard to the date of receiving the show cause notice and that of impugned notice could well be agitated before the appellate forum. 

50. Section 14(1) provide for 30(thirty) days’ time to prefer appeal and the very proviso provides another 30(thirty) days if the appellant can explain sufficient cause of not preferring appeal and from Annexure-'J-2' to the writ petition, we find that, the petitioner received the impugned letter on 21-6-2018 having ample time to prefer appeal. More so, that very assertion can in no way be agitated in writ jurisdiction as from the foregoing discussion we find it disputed question of fact that clearly negates invoking writ jurisdiction. 

51. Then again, both the respondent Nos. 2-3 and 6 in their respective affidavits and that of their submission also brought past conduct of the petitioner leveling similar allegations of polluting environment on the basis of the complaints made to the respondent No. 1 by the then President of BGMEA (the only organization representing the whole garments factory of this country fetching 85% of our total foreign exchange) by its letter dated 22-10-2016 (Annexure-'6' and Annexure-'X' to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 6). And on the basis of such allegation, respondent No. 4 was asked to take legal step following inspection by letters dated 22-11-2016 and 31-12-2016 (Annexure- '4' and Annexure- 'X-1' to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 6). 

52. Aside from that, from Annexure- 'E' to the writ petition, we also find that, when on 1-11-2017 the environment certificate of the petitioner was last renewed up to 5-4-2018, it was done giving condition of fulfilling certain requirement to be observed by the petitioner. As after expiry of the said period, the respondent No. 4 did not find any requirement supposed to be fulfilled by the petitioner and the respondent No. 2 then on 20-5-2018 has very logically issued the show cause notice (Annexure- 'J' to the writ petition). All the above facts lead us to legally assume that, the petitioner has willfully violated the provision laid down in the Ain else BGMEA or the present respondent Nos. 6 and 7 could not have raised the objection and respondent Nos. 2-3 deliberately cautioned him. Moreover, for one's hazardous wrongdoing, the surrounding industrial belt cannot suffer for years together. Keeping the importance of protecting environment from being impaired even our national Parliament has also felt it expedient to incorporate Article 18A in the Constitution. In line with the said beneficial provision set out in our Constitution meant for the welfare of the citizen and for the generation to come, the Hon'ble Appellate Division in the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Md Mustafijur Rahman set-out the following proposition which has been reported in 72 DLR (AD) 211: 
"Environmental justice”

In order to successfully confront the twenty-first century environmental challenges that include managing the current and mitigating the future impacts of climate change; conserving natural resources and bio-diversity and preventing pollution, and to ensure environmental justice, it is incumbent upon the state to develop, implement and enforce environmental laws and upon the Judiciary to see that all parties concerned follow the laws and no one transgresses the same." 

53. Ongoing through the said ratio, we also find that, the analogy set at rest is squarely applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case as well so far as regards to protect the environment at any place not to say in the industrial area. 

54. Now let us examine how far the decision cited by the learned counsel for the petitioner be applicable in filing and maintaining the instant writ petition. It is to be mention here that, insofar as regards to the decision reported in 58 DLR 405 (as cited by the learned counsel for the petitioner), the learned counsel for the respondent No. 6 submits that, in that decision, learned senior counsel for the petitioner had earlier canvassed for resorting alternative remedy that is to say, to file appeal while representing Dhaka University and he won the said writ petition on the point of maintainability, though in the instant writ petition, the learned senior counsel though took stand for the opposite. Controverting the said view of the learned counsel of the respondent No. 6, Mr Mahbub Shafique, the learned counsel for the petitioner then referred to a judgment dated 3-12-2003 passed in civil appeal No. 54 of 2001 corresponding to civil petition for leave to appeal No. 9 of 2001 appeared in the online legal journal named "Manupatra" where writ is found to be maintainable despite of having alternative remedy and his senior counsel had also represented Dhaka University and made similar assertion what he put forward in the case reported in 58 DLR 405. But the learned counsel has now been relying on subsequent decision as passed by the Appellate Division. 

55. We have also gone through the said judgment passed in civil appeal No. 54 of 2001 corresponding to civil petition for leave to appeal No. 9 of 2001 but what has been settled in that judgment is, if any action taken beyond the provision of law or derogation thereof, in that case, alternative remedy will not stand in the way of invoking writ jurisdiction. But the case in hand, we don't find that, the respondent No. 4 who passed the impugned notice lacks any jurisdiction or it caused any derogation to exert authority. So the decision upon which the learned counsel puts his emphasis has got no relevance with the facts and circumstances of the instant case.

56. Now let us take a glance to other decisions cited by the learned counsel for the petitioner. In the decision so have been reported in 1981 BLD (AD) 45 = 34 DLR (AD) 29, it has been held that, when the impugned action is without jurisdiction, the question of availing statutory alternative remedy does not arise. But this very finding is totally distinguishable with the facts and circumstances and point-in-issue involved in the instant writ petition because the learned counsel for the petitioner in the entire writ petition did not raise any objection with regard to the jurisdiction of the respondent No. 4 in issuing the impugned notice. 

57. The learned counsel for the petitioner then referred another judgment dated 9-6-1988 so appeared in the online legal journal 'Manupatra' in writ petition No. 50 of 1985, where it has been held that, "the provisions of Customs Act is a matter concerning the interpretation of an act of legislature- It was therefore fit and proper that the petitioner had agitated the matter in the original constitutional jurisdiction rather than leave it to be decided by the executive authority who is the appellate authority". This decision has also got no substantive implication in this case as well, as what has been held in the decision in particular, in paragraph No. 20 thereof, has subsequently been reversed by our Hon'ble Appellate Division in the judgment which has been reported in 20 BLC (AD) 64 as well as 52 DLR (AD) 149 and in those decisions, it has been settled once for all that, without resorting to the appellate authority, the aggrieved party cannot resort to writ jurisdiction challenging any action taken by the customs authority. So that very decision as relied by the petitioner as has been overruled by those two decisions by our Hon'ble Appellate Division and hence, it has no manner of application in the instant writ petition.

58. Then the learned counsel has also referred a decision reported in 2011 BLD (AD) 79 but on going through the entire judgment we find the same has nothing to do with the facts and circumstances and point-in-issue agitated in the instant writ petition. 

59. The learned counsel has next referred another judgment dated 9-4-1997 appeared in the online legal journal 'Manupatra' in civil appeal No. 5 of 1996 where we find that very appeal was preferred against the judgment passed by a Special Tribunal in an Arms Case but he could not prefer the same within the statutory period of time for which he at first resorted to the provision of section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and then invoked writ jurisdiction and both the miscellaneous case and the writ petition were dismissed in limini and challenging the judgment passed in writ petition, the convict-appellant then preferred civil appeal and in the appeal, the Hon'ble Appellate Division found that the learned Judge who passed the impugned conviction has got no jurisdiction that is, the learned Judge passed judgment without having any jurisdiction (Quoram non-judice) but in the instant case we overwhelmingly find that, the writ petitioner has ever raised any question as regards to the jurisdiction of the respondent No. 4 in issuing impugned letter and it has been found from the provision of the Ain of 1995 and that of Rule of 1997 that, there has been an appellate authority and respondent No. 4 has got the authority to issue the impugned notice. 

60. The learned counsel for the petitioner has also referred a decision reported in 56 DLR 1, where it has been held that, without giving any show cause notice no final order can be passed under the provision of sections 4(3), 8, 10 and 11 of the Ain and that of the Rule 5 but in the instant case, it has repeatedly been found that, before issuing the impugned notice the petitioner was served with several show cause notice and since the petitioner did not take any appropriate measure to correct the pollution caused by him as has been found by the respondent No. 2 and repeated allegations have been levelled against the petitioner and since show cause notice is found to have issued before passing the impugned notice, so that very decision has got no manner of application in this case. 

61. The last decision so have been cited by the learned counsel for the petitioner reported in 15 BLC 770 where it has been held that, if the impugned action is wholly without jurisdiction in the sense, of not being authorized by the statute or is in violation of a constitutional provision, a writ petition will be maintainable. But in the instant case, it has deliberately been found that, the petitioner did not raise any question as regards to the jurisdiction of the respondent No. 4 in issuing impugned notice, rather the alleged authority (whether delegation has been made or not) in issuing the same. But by filing different circulars both at the instance of respondent Nos. 2-3 by the DAG as well as the learned counsel for the respondent No. 6, it has palpably been found that, the power has been delegated by the respondent No. 2 upon the respondent No. 4 to do so, so under no circumstances, can it be said that, the respondent No. 4 has got no authority because those very circulars filed by the learned DAG as well as the learned counsel for the respondent No. 6 has not been controverted by the learned counsel for the petitioner by filing any affidavit-in-reply because it is found that there has been statutory provision providing appellate authority and the respondent No. 4 has been delegated power by respondent No. 2 to act on its behalf. So that very decision is totally inapplicable with the facts and circumstances of the instant case as well.

62. We have also perused the decisions cited by the learned counsel for respondent No. 6 and found that apart from decision reported in 55 DLR 69 all are related to the point of maintainability where it has been decided that under no circumstances, an aggrieved party can resort to writ jurisdiction if there has been an alternative remedy. However, the decision reported in 55 DLR 69 which is considered to be a pioneering judgment in the field of "public interest litigation" (in the case of Dr Mohiuddin Farooque vs Bangladesh and others) it has been held that: 
"Environment Protection Act, 1995 Section 4 Both the Constitution of Bangladesh and the environmental laws enjoined the government functionaries to take adequate measures to prevent environmental pollution. It is also the constitutional obligation of the Government to ensure that the rights of the people, so very glorified under Article 18 and Article 32 of the Constitution, are vindicated and defended and the provisions of the said Act is implemented in its real sprit to protect the interest of the people. In case of any breach or lathes in this respect, such constitutional obligations can be enforced against the Government under Article 102 of the Constitution. In such a process, the Supreme Court is only instrumental under the Constitution in achieving the constitutional objectives of a welfare state." 

63. Last but obviously not the least, from the terms of the Rule, we find that, the said Rule was issued in the form of "writ of certiorari" and definitely it is under Article 102(2)(a)(ii) of the Constitution—which provides "if the aggrieved party has no other equally efficacious remedy provided by law" but the case in hand, is totally otherwise where the petitioner has got alternative remedy. 

64. From the forgoing discussion and observation, it has unequivocally proved that, the petitioner has got equally efficacious remedy. But he did not resort to and why he did so nothing has been stated in the entire writ petition. But what has been cited by the learned counsel for the petitioner in support of his submission—those all are mere exception to evade alternative remedy—which are not at all applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case and those have elaborately been discussed in the penultimate paragraphs needs no repetition here. 

65. On top of that, if this court goes beyond the express provision set out in Article 102 and 18A of our Constitution and that of the statutory provision enumerated in relevant section of the Ain of 1995 in that case, there is every likelihood to jeopardize the spirit of those provision that will result in, this court will be flooded with writ petition bypassing the alternative forum which was not the intention of the legislators who framed our sacred Constitution. 

66. On the whole, we can conclude asserting once again that, by no stretch of imagination, the instant writ can be maintained as there has been clear alternative remedy in the Environment Conservation Act, 1995 and the rules framed thereunder. 

67. In that panorama, we can profitably rely in the case of Controller of Examinations, University of Dhaka vs Mohiuddin reported in 44 DLR (AD) 305 and in the case of Fariduddin Mahmud vs Md Saifur Rahman reported in 16 MLR (AD) 205 = 63 DLR (AD) 93. In the decisions of those cases, it has been settled that "where there is alternative remedy provided under the statute, the writ petition is not maintainable." 

68. At the very outset, we have stated that, if we find this writ is not maintainable, we will not touch upon the merit of the case and for that obvious reason we did so.

69. Regard being had to the above discussion and observation, we don't find any merit in the Rule. 

70. Resultantly, the Rule is discharged however without any order as to cost. 71. The impugned Memo No. 22.02.0000. 091.001.4331.প্রশা:-797 dated 11-6-2018 passed by the respondent No. 4 (Annexure 'K' to the writ petition) is thus found valid and thus sustained. 72. The order of stay granted stands recalled and vacated. 

Communicate a copy of this judgment and order to all the respondents forthwith. 

End.
